```tsx
<Carousel label="Product photos" style={{"--carousel-slide": "50%"}}>
  <Card>Front</Card>
  <Card>Back</Card>
  <Card>In use</Card>
  <Card>Packaging</Card>
</Carousel>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | One node per slide. Each child is wrapped in a group with aria-roledescription="slide" and the label "Slide 3 of 8", so the count is never the consumer's job to keep in sync. |
| `label` | `string` | Carousel | Accessible name of the region. Give it a real one — "Product photos" — because a page with two carousels announces two identical regions otherwise. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | true | Previous/next arrows. They disable themselves at each end, measured from the scroll position — not from the slide index, which would be wrong whenever more than one slide fits. |
| `indicators` | `boolean` | true | The row of dots. Each is a 24x24 target (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8) with an 8px mark drawn in ::before. |
| `--carousel-slide` | `CSS custom property` | 100% | How wide a slide is, and therefore how many are visible at once. It is CSS and not a prop because that is a layout decision of the page: set it to 50% for two at a time. Same escape valve as --qr-size and --media-h. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/chart.html">
# Chart

Sized, named surface that hosts a Recharts chart wearing Aurea tokens.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Chart} from "@aurea-uds/react/chart";
```

```tsx
<Chart label="Runs per month">
  <AreaChart data={data}>
    <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
    <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
    <Area dataKey="runs" name="Runs" stroke="var(--chart-2)" fill="var(--chart-2)" fillOpacity={0.15} />
  </AreaChart>
</Chart>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactElement` | none | REQUIRED. One Recharts chart element (AreaChart, BarChart, LineChart…). Aurea does not wrap the chart types: the engine draws, this component holds. |
| `label` | `string` | the provider's "Chart" | Accessible name of the whole drawing. Say what it plots, not that it is a chart. |
| `className` | `string` | none | Added to the box. The height is CSS, not a prop — a dimension comes from a class, so density still reaches it and nobody writes a raw pixel. To make the axis and legend text bigger — for low vision, for example — set `--chart-text` on the chart or any ancestor, such as `var(--text-sm)` or `var(--text-base)`; the default is `var(--text-xs)`. It is a CSS valve, like DataGrid's `--datagrid-max-h`: the rule is CSS and overrides the engine's own `tick` font size. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/chartlegend.html">
# ChartLegend

Which colour is which series, as a plain list under the chart.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Chart, ChartLegend} from "@aurea-uds/react/chart";
```

```tsx
<Chart label="Runs and errors">
  <BarChart data={data}>
    <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
    <Bar dataKey="runs" name="Runs" fill="var(--chart-2)" />
    <Bar dataKey="errors" name="Errors" fill="var(--chart-4)" />
    <ChartLegend />
  </BarChart>
</Chart>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payload` | `Array<{value, color}>` | the series, in the engine's order | The entries to list. Worth passing: as of recharts 3.10.1 the engine sorts its own payload alphabetically by dataKey, so the legend does not follow the order the series were declared in. This prop is the way to fix that from the outside. |
| `verticalAlign` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | "bottom" | Which side of the drawing the list sits on. |
| `…Legend` | `LegendProps` | none | Everything else goes to the engine's Legend. `content` is the exception: it is what this component IS. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/charttooltip.html">
# ChartTooltip

Values under the pointer, on the same tooltip surface as the rest of Aurea.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Chart, ChartTooltip} from "@aurea-uds/react/chart";
```

```tsx
<Chart label="Runs per month">
  <AreaChart data={data}>
    <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
    <Area dataKey="runs" name="Runs" stroke="var(--chart-2)" fill="var(--chart-2)" fillOpacity={0.15} />
    <ChartTooltip />
  </AreaChart>
</Chart>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | none | Pins the tooltip to one data point instead of following the pointer. Written for a page with no pointer — a static preview, a print, a screenshot. |
| `cursor` | `object \| false` | the Aurea cursor line | The mark the engine draws under the pointer. `false` removes it. |
| `…Tooltip` | `ComponentProps<typeof Tooltip>` | none | Everything else goes to the engine's Tooltip. `content` is the exception: it is what this component IS, so passing it would replace the Aurea surface. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/checkbox.html">
# Checkbox

Checkbox is a yes-or-no that waits: it changes a value the form will submit later. A Switch applies immediately — that is the whole difference, and it decides which one you want. The label is required and lives inside the <label>, so the entire row is the target, not a 16px box.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Checkbox} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Public workspace"
  description="Anyone with the link can read it." />
```

- The label is part of the target: clicking the words toggles it, which matters on a phone.

- description adds a second line for the consequence, without inflating the label.

- labelHidden keeps the name for the screen reader and takes it off screen — for a selection column.

- indeterminate is supported by the native input for a partially selected group.

- Checkbox waits for submit; Switch applies now. Pick by the moment of effect, not by the look.

## Examples

### A list of options

Many-of-many. Each one is independent — for one-of-many use Radio.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Email" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Push" />
<Checkbox label="Weekly digest" defaultChecked />
```

### Hidden label

A table selection column: the per-row name stays for the reader, off screen, so the column stays narrow.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Select Analyst" labelHidden />
```

### Disabled

Unavailable but still readable — the reason belongs somewhere on the screen.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Audit log" disabled />
<Checkbox label="SSO" defaultChecked disabled />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | REQUIRED, and inside the <label>: the whole row is the target, not just the 16px box. |
| `labelHidden` | `boolean` | false | Keeps the label in the DOM but out of sight — for a table selection column. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | Second line under the label, for the consequence of ticking it. |
| `checked / defaultChecked` | `boolean` | — | Controlled or uncontrolled. For a third state use indeterminate on the input. |
| `size` | `Responsive<FieldSize>` | md | The system's size step. It is not the HTML size attribute, which does not exist on a checkbox anyway. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/checkboxgroup.html">
# CheckboxGroup

CheckboxGroup is a set of checkboxes under one label, with a description and an error. It keeps the list of what is checked: each Checkbox inside says its own value, and the group hands it the checked state and the change.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CheckboxGroup, Checkbox} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup label="Your interests" description="Choose all that apply" name="interests">
  <Checkbox label="Coding" value="coding" description="Building software" />
  <Checkbox label="Design" value="design" description="Creating interfaces" />
  <Checkbox label="Writing" value="writing" description="Content creation" />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

- role="group" named by the label; the description and the error are read with it.

- value / defaultValue / onValueChange work on the list of checked values.

- name and disabled reach every checkbox; with an error, each one is marked invalid.

- Each checkbox keeps its own description, aligned with its text.

## Examples

### With an error

The error closes the group, and every checkbox is marked invalid.

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup label="Notifications" required error="Pick at least one channel">
  <Checkbox label="E-mail" value="email" />
  <Checkbox label="SMS" value="sms" />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | REQUIRED. The group's name. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | Help text under the label, read by screen readers with the group. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | — | The error at the end; each checkbox gets aria-invalid. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string[]` | — | The values of the checked boxes. Each Checkbox inside says its own value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | — | Called with the new list. |
| `name` | `string` | — | The name of every checkbox, for the form. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | Disables every checkbox inside. |
| `required` | `boolean` | false | The red asterisk after the label, like Field. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/chip.html">
# Chip

Another name for Badge, for those who know this piece as a chip. Identical in everything: the same props, the same look, the same behaviour.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Chip} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Chip tone="success">Paid</Chip>
  <Chip tone="primary" emphasis="solid">New</Chip>
  <Chip tone="blue">Design</Chip>
</Cluster>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `neutral \| primary \| info \| success \| warning \| danger \| running \| paused \| offline \| review \| red \| orange \| green \| teal \| cyan \| blue \| violet \| pink` | neutral | Tone of the label. The four operational ones exist because the state of a job is metadata as often as it is a condition; when it is a condition standing on its own, use Status. The eight colour names (red, orange, green, teal, cyan, blue, violet, pink) are CATEGORIES, not states — they mark a group (a section, a type of item) and say nothing about health. They skip yellow, which belongs to the brand, and pass AA in both themes in all three emphases. Pair the colour with a word or a leading icon: colour alone is never the label. |
| `tone` | `BadgeVariant` | — | The colour, with the native package's name — the same names on web and native. The same axis as variant; it wins when both are given. |
| `emphasis` | `soft \| outline \| solid \| flat` | soft | How loud the tone is. `soft` is the tinted pill you already know; `outline` is contour only; `solid` fills with the accent and is what a notification counter wants. All 36 combinations of variant × emphasis × theme were measured for contrast — the lowest is 5.6:1, and the skin spec keeps it that way. flat is the soft tone without the line around it, as the reference's chip. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg` | md | `md` is the historical size and did not move, so nothing that already uses Badge changed. `xs` (16px, borderless) is the counter that rides on an icon — it is what BottomNav asks for; `sm` sits between them; `lg` is for a standalone label. Every size is its OWN class, never a contextual override: `geometry.spec` holds `.badge` to one height per page, and a rule that shrank it by context reproved — correctly. |
| `dot` | `boolean` | false | A status dot before the text, inheriting the current colour. With `anchor` and nothing to show, the dot IS the badge — the plain 8px mark that means "something new". |
| `leading / trailing` | `ReactNode` | — | A glyph before or after the text. They take a NODE, not an icon name, and that is a boundary decision, not laziness: Icon reads the sprite through a hook, so importing it here would drag this module to the client and undo the 118.5 KB that ADR-0026 saved. |
| `image / imageAlt` | `string` | — | A round picture at the start — an avatar or a flag. Empty alt when it is decorative, which is the usual case beside a name. |
| `count / max / showZero` | `number / number / boolean` | — / 99 / false | Numeric content. Over `max` it reads `99+`. Zero hides itself unless `showZero`, because an empty inbox does not deserve a mark. `formatBadgeCount(count, max)` is exported so the accessible name can say the same string the eye sees. |
| `fit` | `"auto" \| "content"` | "auto" | `content` keeps the badge as wide as its text even inside a column. The default follows the container, and that was measured: `.stack` declares no `align-items`, so a badge inside it stretches (300 px in a 300 px column, 55 px loose in a block). Implemented as `inline-size: fit-content`, not `align-self`, so a badge in a row keeps its vertical centring. Ignored with `anchor`. The native Badge takes the same prop. |
| `anchor` | `top-end \| top-start \| bottom-end \| bottom-start` | — | Switches to the OVERLAY shape: `children` becomes the thing being decorated (a bell, an avatar, a menu row) and the badge hangs off that corner. Without it, `children` is the pill's content and nothing about the old usage changes. |
| `anchorShape` | `square \| circle` | square | `circle` pulls the badge 14% back into the corner — the `overlap` of one of the references, and the number is theirs, measured in their source. Without it a counter on a round avatar floats off the edge. |
| `invisible` | `boolean` | false | Hides the overlay without moving the child. Use it when the count is loading rather than absent. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The label — or, with `anchor`, the element being decorated. Short by construction: it is a pill, and a badge that wraps to a second line is a sentence in the wrong component. |
| `badgeContent` | `ReactNode` | — | What the overlay shows when it is not a number. Named after a reference library's prop and not `content`, which collides with the HTML attribute of that name. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/closebutton.html">
# CloseButton

CloseButton is the small round button that closes a notice, a panel or a dialog: a 24 circle on the neutral fill with a 16 X in the Bold stroke. It names itself — "Close", or "Fechar" with the Portuguese strings — so a bare `<CloseButton />` is never a mute control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CloseButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<CloseButton onClick={close} />
```

- The accessible name comes by itself; pass `label` to say what closes when a screen has more than one.

- A 24 circle with a 16 glyph, so it sits in a title row without making it taller.

- On touch the circle stays 24 and the target grows to 44 around it, invisibly.

- Darkens on hover and shrinks a little when pressed, like every Aurea button.

- `children` replaces the X when a closing action needs another glyph.

## Examples

### In a title row

At the end of a card's title row. The `label` says what closes.

```tsx
<Card>
  <div style={{display: "flex", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between"}}>
    <strong>Backup finished</strong>
    <CloseButton label="Close notice" onClick={close} />
  </div>
  <Text color="muted">Photos were saved at 22:40.</Text>
</Card>
```

### Disabled

When closing is not possible yet — while a save is still running, for example.

```tsx
<CloseButton disabled />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | strings.close | The accessible name. Defaults to "Close" ("Fechar" in ptBR); pass what closes when there is more than one on the screen, e.g. "Close notice". |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | the X (Bold) | Replaces the X, as in the reference. Keep it a 16 glyph. |
| `onClick` | `MouseEventHandler` | — | What closing does. On native, `onPress`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | Disables the button; it leaves the focus order. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/cluster.html">
# Cluster

Horizontal wrapping/layout primitive.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Cluster} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Badge>one</Badge>
  <Badge>two</Badge>
  <Badge>three</Badge>
</Cluster>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Horizontal flow that wraps: centred on the cross axis, --space-3 between items. It is the row of chips, buttons or tags — the one layout that must never cause sideways scrolling, which is why wrapping is not optional. |
| `gap` | `"tight" \| "normal" \| "loose"` | "normal" | Three steps and no others (ADR-0051): tight is --space-2, normal is --space-3, loose is --space-6. The old rule still holds against ANY spacing; these two extra steps exist for the two measured cases — a note under its value, and a grid of filters. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "baseline"` | "center" | The cross axis (vertical). Same names as the native Cluster. |
| `justify` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between"` | "start" | The main axis. `between` spreads the free space: a name on the left, a button on the right. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | true | The row wraps by default. `false` keeps everything on one line. |
| `className` | `string` | — | For justification or width. Every other div attribute passes through. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/code.html">
# Code

A short piece of code inside a sentence. For a block of code use CodeBlock.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Code} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Paragraph>Run <Code>pnpm build</Code> before you publish.</Paragraph>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | `"default" \| "muted"` | "default" | Two colours only, like the reference library: the text colour or the muted one. A closed list protects contrast — both pass AA on every Aurea surface. |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "muted" \| "subtle" \| "primary" \| "link" \| "danger" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "info"` | — | The text colour with the native package's name — the same names on web and native. link is the yellow made for text, readable on both themes; primary is the fill yellow and nearly disappears on the light theme. The state colours are the -400 pair. It wins over color when both are given. |
| `weight` | `"normal" \| "medium" \| "semibold" \| "bold" \| "extrabold"` | — (the role's own) | Overrides the weight of the role. Headings are semibold and body text is regular by default. "extrabold" (800, --weight-extrabold) is for a cover title; the default title weight is still semibold. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "justify"` | — (inherited) | Text alignment. start and end follow the writing direction, so the same value mirrors in RTL. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | false | One line, cut with an ellipsis. Turns the element into a block so the cut has a width to measure against. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The text. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | false | Tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) — for numbers that line up in a column (price, year, spec sheet) or change on screen. Off by default: in running text the narrow "1" is right. Native: the same prop sets fontVariant ["tabular-nums"]. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/codeblock.html">
# CodeBlock

Read-only syntax-highlighted code display.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CodeBlock} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<CodeBlock language="tsx" copyable>
  {'import {Button} from "@aurea-uds/react";'}
</CodeBlock>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `string` | — | The code, as a string and not as nodes: it goes verbatim inside <code>, so whitespace and line breaks are yours to control. |
| `language` | `string` | text | Written to data-language, which is what labels the block. It does not highlight — the component is a display, not a parser. |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | false | Draws the copy button. The copying itself lives in the core's aurea.js, so React and plain HTML share one implementation instead of two that drift. |
| `preview` | `ReactNode` | — | The live example of the code. With it, the block becomes the example box of Aurea's site: the Preview \| Code tabs (a segmented control across the width; arrows, Home and End move between them), the preview on the recessed surface and the code without a frame. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Lands on the outer element either way — on the <pre> when plain, on the wrapper when copyable. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/codeeditor.html">
# CodeEditor

Editable code surface.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CodeEditor} from "@aurea-uds/react/code-editor";
```

```tsx
import {javascript} from "@codemirror/lang-javascript";

<CodeEditor
  defaultValue={'const total = items.reduce((n, i) => n + i.price, 0);'}
  extensions={[javascript()]}
  onChange={setSource}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultValue` | `string` | "" | The starting document. Uncontrolled: it is read on mount and never again, so typing does not fight a re-render. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Fires on every document change. Held through a ref, which is why replacing the handler does not tear down the editor and lose the undo history. |
| `extensions` | `Extension[]` | — | Where your language goes. No language is bundled on purpose — pass @codemirror/lang-* and the weight, and the choice, stay yours. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | false | Reconfigured through a CodeMirror Compartment, so toggling it keeps the document, the selection and the history intact. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | "Code editor" | Accessible name of the editing area. It goes on the contenteditable itself, which is the element that takes focus. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the host element that CodeMirror mounts into. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/collapsible.html">
# Collapsible

One section that opens and closes, with the open state owned by the app.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Collapsible} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Collapsible trigger="Advanced options" defaultOpen>
  <p>Everything here is optional.</p>
</Collapsible>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `ReactNode` | — | What you click to open and close. It becomes the button, and the chevron is added in front of it. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The panel's content. It stays in the DOM when closed, so in-page search still finds it. |
| `open` | `boolean` | — | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | false | Starts open without controlling it. Do not switch this after mount on an uncontrolled Collapsible — the engine warns about it in as many words. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | Fires with the new state, from the trigger or from the keyboard. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | The trigger stays focusable and inert, so keyboard users still find out the section exists. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the outermost element, after the Aurea skin — your class wins on a tie. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/colorarea.html">
# ColorArea

ColorArea is the square where you pick two channels of a colour for the third one fixed — saturation (across) and brightness (up) by default, or any pair of HSB, HSL or RGB. It works by pointer, touch and keyboard, and the screen reader hears the channels and the colour's name.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ColorArea} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ColorArea defaultValue="#0485f7" aria-label="Fill" />
```

- The value is hex (#rrggbb), like the browser's colour input: value, defaultValue, onValueChange, onValueCommitted.

- Arrows move one step (Shift: ten); Page Up/Down change the brightness, Home/End the saturation.

- Two hidden range inputs, one per axis, announced as a 2D slider, with the colour's name in the app's language.

- colorSpace, xChannel and yChannel choose the pair: hue and saturation in HSL, red and blue in RGB…

- showDots draws a grid of dots over the area, to see the position.

- Dragging to grey keeps the hue: the area does not jump to red.

## Examples

### With dots

showDots: a grid of dots over the area.

```tsx
<ColorArea defaultValue="#7c3aed" showDots aria-label="Fill" />
```

### Colour spaces and channels

Any pair of channels, and the third one stays fixed: hue and saturation in HSL, red and blue in RGB, hue and brightness in HSB.

```tsx
<ColorArea colorSpace="hsl" xChannel="hue" yChannel="saturation" defaultValue="hsl(200, 80%, 50%)" aria-label="HSL" />
<ColorArea colorSpace="rgb" xChannel="red" yChannel="blue" defaultValue="rgb(120, 40, 220)" aria-label="RGB" />
<ColorArea xChannel="hue" yChannel="brightness" defaultValue="#16a34a" aria-label="HSB" />
```

### Disabled

The area does not move, and the keyboard skips it.

```tsx
<ColorArea defaultValue="#e11d48" disabled aria-label="Fill" />
```

### With the value

Controlled: the swatch and the code follow the area.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("#0485f7");

<ColorArea value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} aria-label="Accent" />
<ColorSwatch color={colour} label="Accent" />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | — | The colour, in hex or rgb()/hsl()/hsb(), controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | "#ffffff" | The starting colour when you do not control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called on every step with #rrggbb. |
| `onValueCommitted` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called when the pointer is released and on every key — the moment to save. |
| `colorSpace` | `"hsb" \| "hsl" \| "rgb"` | "hsb" | The colour space of the area. Without it, the one the channels ask for. |
| `xChannel` | `ColorChannel` | saturation (HSB, HSL) · red (RGB) | The channel across. |
| `yChannel` | `ColorChannel` | brightness (HSB) · lightness (HSL) · green (RGB) | The channel up. |
| `showDots` | `boolean` | false | A grid of dots over the area, as in the reference — it helps to see the position. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | The area does not move. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Sends the colour with a form, as #rrggbb. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the group. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | strings.colorPicker | What the colour is for ("Background"). The inputs are named "Background, Color picker"; without it, "Color picker". |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` | — | Names the group and the inputs by another element's id. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | Goes to the inputs. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the area, after the Aurea skin. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/colorfield.html">
# ColorField

ColorField is the field for a colour: the swatch in front and the code — hex, rgb(), hsl() or hsb(). The code applies on Enter or when the field loses focus; text that is not a colour goes back. With channel, it edits one channel as a number. It is the same Input, with the same sizes and variants, and Field gives it the label.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ColorField} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Field label="Colour">
  <ColorField defaultValue="#0485f7" />
</Field>
```

- The value is hex (#rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa with transparency): value, defaultValue, onValueChange, onValueCommitted — like ColorArea and ColorPicker.

- Without defaultValue the field starts empty; clearing it calls onValueChange with "".

- channel edits one channel — hue, saturation, brightness, lightness, red, green, blue or alpha — announced as a number with the colour's name.

- Inside a Field, the label, the description and the error are the Field's, as in every Aurea field.

- Inside a ColorPicker, without a value of its own, it edits the picker's colour.

- name sends the colour with a form, as hex.

## Examples

### Variants

Since 0.34.0 neither has a line: both are a translucent fill of the text colour — the same two as Input.

```tsx
<Field label="Primary"><ColorField defaultValue="#0485f7" /></Field>
<Field label="Secondary"><ColorField variant="secondary" defaultValue="#0485f7" /></Field>
```

### In a card

On a card the field background disappears; variant="secondary" keeps it visible.

```tsx
<Card>
  <Field label="Background"><ColorField variant="secondary" defaultValue="#7c3aed" /></Field>
</Card>
```

### Sizes

sm, md and lg — the same steps as Input and Button.

```tsx
<ColorField size="sm" defaultValue="#e11d48" aria-label="Small" />
<ColorField defaultValue="#e11d48" aria-label="Medium" />
<ColorField size="lg" defaultValue="#e11d48" aria-label="Large" />
```

### With a description

The Field's hint describes the field.

```tsx
<Field label="Link colour" hint="Hex, rgb() or hsl(). Enter applies it.">
  <ColorField defaultValue="#0485f7" />
</Field>
```

### Required

The Field's required marks the field.

```tsx
<Field label="Brand colour" required>
  <ColorField placeholder="#0485f7" />
</Field>
```

### Disabled and read-only

Disabled does not take input and is skipped by the keyboard; read-only is shown and focusable.

```tsx
<Field label="Theme colour"><ColorField defaultValue="#f0c200" disabled /></Field>
<Field label="Inherited colour"><ColorField defaultValue="#f0c200" readOnly /></Field>
```

### Width

The whole line, like the other fields. width sets another one.

```tsx
<Field label="Full line"><ColorField defaultValue="#16a34a" /></Field>
<Field label="Narrow"><ColorField defaultValue="#16a34a" width="12rem" /></Field>
```

### Validation

The Field's error marks the field invalid and is read with it. Here, while the field is empty.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("");

<Field label="Brand colour" required error={colour === "" ? "Pick a colour — hex, rgb() or hsl()." : undefined}>
  <ColorField value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} placeholder="#0485f7" />
</Field>
```

### One channel

channel edits one channel as a number: arrows, Page Up/Down, Home and End. Three fields share one colour.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("#0485f7");

<Field label="Hue"><ColorField channel="hue" value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} /></Field>
<Field label="Saturation"><ColorField channel="saturation" value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} /></Field>
<Field label="Brightness"><ColorField channel="brightness" value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} /></Field>
```

### With the value

Controlled: the code follows the field, and the button sets it from outside.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("#16a34a");

<Field label="Accent"><ColorField value={colour} onValueChange={setColour} /></Field>
<Button onClick={() => setColour("#0485f7")}>Reset</Button>
```

### In a form

name sends the colour as hex.

```tsx
<form onSubmit={save}>
  <Field label="Brand colour" required>
    <ColorField name="brand" defaultValue="#f0c200" />
  </Field>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | — | The colour, in hex or rgb()/hsl()/hsb(); "" is the empty field. Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | — | The starting colour when you do not control it. Without it, the field starts empty. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called when the code is applied (Enter or leaving the field) and on every key in a channel, with the hex — or "" when it is cleared. |
| `onValueCommitted` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called with onValueChange — the moment to save. |
| `channel` | `ColorChannel` | — | One channel, as a number, in place of the code: hue, saturation, brightness, lightness, red, green, blue or alpha. |
| `colorSpace` | `"hsb" \| "hsl" \| "rgb"` | "hsb" | With channel: the space of hue and saturation. |
| `swatch` | `boolean` | true for the code, false for a channel | The swatch in front. |
| `size` | `Responsive<sm \| md \| lg>` | md | The field height, the same scale as Input. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary"` | "primary" | secondary is the neutral background, for a field inside a card — the same as Input. |
| `width` | `string` | 100% | The field width — "20rem" or "auto". Without it, the whole line, like the other fields. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | The field does not take input. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | false | Shown and focusable, not editable. |
| `required` | `boolean` | false | Inside a Field, Field's required does it. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Sends the colour with a form, as hex. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Shown while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the input — what a label points at. Inside a Field, the Field gives it one. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Names the field when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` | — | Names the field by another element's id. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | Goes to the input. Inside a Field, the description and the error are added. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` | — | Marks the value as rejected. Inside a Field, the error does it. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the group, after the Aurea skin. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/colorpicker.html">
# ColorPicker

ColorPicker is a swatch with a name that opens a window to pick a colour: the area, the hue track and the hex field, which is always there. With swatches, ready colours too; as the swatches variation, a closed palette.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ColorPicker} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ColorPicker label="Brand colour" defaultValue="#0485f7" />
```

- The value is hex (#rrggbb): value, defaultValue, onValueChange, onValueCommitted — like ColorArea and Slider.

- The hex field applies on Enter or when it loses focus; text that is not a colour goes back.

- Swatches without a label are named by the colour's name, in the app's language.

- variant="swatches" is the closed palette: only the swatches and the hex field.

- Dragging to grey keeps the hue, and the hue track still moves the area.

- The window can be assembled: children replaces the default content, and the colour pieces inside — ColorArea, Slider with channel, ColorField — share the picker's colour.

## Examples

### With swatches

Ready colours under the hue track. Controlled: the code follows.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("#0485f7");

<ColorPicker label="Brand colour" value={colour} onValueChange={setColour}
  swatches={[{color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"}, {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"}, …]} />
```

### A closed palette

variant="swatches": only the swatches and the hex field.

```tsx
<ColorPicker label="Tag colour" variant="swatches" defaultValue="#16a34a"
  swatches={[{color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"}, {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"}, …]} />
```

### With fields

The window assembled with children: the area, the hue, and one field per channel — the colour space chosen in a Select.

```tsx
const [space, setSpace] = useState("hsl");
const channels = {hsb: ["hue", "saturation", "brightness"], hsl: ["hue", "saturation", "lightness"], rgb: ["red", "green", "blue"]};

<ColorPicker label="Pick a colour" defaultValue="hsla(220, 90%, 50%, 0.8)">
  <ColorArea />
  <Slider label="Hue" channel="hue" />
  <Select aria-label="Colour space" value={space} onValueChange={setSpace}
    items={[{value: "hsl", label: "HSL"}, {value: "hsb", label: "HSB"}, {value: "rgb", label: "RGB"}]} />
  <div style={{display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))", gap: "var(--space-2)"}}>
    {channels[space].map((channel) => (
      <ColorField key={channel} channel={channel} colorSpace={space} variant="secondary" aria-label={channel} />
    ))}
  </div>
</ColorPicker>
```

### With sliders

One track per channel, transparency included — the colour space chosen in a Select.

```tsx
const [space, setSpace] = useState("hsl");
const channels = {hsb: ["hue", "saturation", "brightness"], hsl: ["hue", "saturation", "lightness"], rgb: ["red", "green", "blue"]};

<ColorPicker label="Pick a colour" defaultValue="hsl(219, 58%, 93%)">
  <Select aria-label="Colour space" value={space} onValueChange={setSpace}
    items={[{value: "hsl", label: "HSL"}, {value: "hsb", label: "HSB"}, {value: "rgb", label: "RGB"}]} />
  {[...channels[space], "alpha"].map((channel) => (
    <Slider key={channel} label={channel} channel={channel} colorSpace={space} />
  ))}
</ColorPicker>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | REQUIRED. The name next to the swatch on the trigger ("Brand colour"). Names the trigger and the window. |
| `value` | `string` | — | The colour in hex (#rrggbb or #rgb), controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | "#ffffff" | The starting colour when you do not control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called on every step with #rrggbb. |
| `onValueCommitted` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called on release, on every key, when a swatch is chosen and when the hex is confirmed — the moment to save. |
| `swatches` | `(string \| {color, label?})[]` | — | Ready colours, under the hue track; with variant="swatches", in place of the area. Without a label, each is named by the colour's name in the app's language. |
| `variant` | `"full" \| "swatches"` | "full" | "swatches": the closed palette (ADR-0069, the "C") — only the swatches and the hex field. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | area, hue, swatches, hex field | The content of the window, built by you ("with fields", "with sliders"): the colour pieces without a value of their own — ColorArea, Slider with channel, ColorField — share the picker's colour. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | The trigger does not open. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Sends the colour with a form, as #rrggbb. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the trigger, after the Aurea skin. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/colorswatch.html">
# ColorSwatch

ColorSwatch shows a colour as a round sample. A thin ring inside keeps a colour that matches the background visible. It is an image for screen readers, named by label.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ColorSwatch} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ColorSwatch color="#f0c200" size="xs" label="Aurea yellow" />
<ColorSwatch color="#f0c200" size="sm" label="Aurea yellow" />
<ColorSwatch color="#f0c200" label="Aurea yellow" />
<ColorSwatch color="#f0c200" size="lg" label="Aurea yellow" />
<ColorSwatch color="#f0c200" size="xl" label="Aurea yellow" />
```

- Any CSS colour: hex, oklch(), or a token such as var(--primary).

- Five sizes from the reference library: 16, 24, 32, 36 and 40.

- Round only. A transparent colour shows a checkerboard underneath.

- role="img" named by label; without it, the colour value is read.

- With options, a group of swatches to pick one from: native radio buttons, so the choice and the arrows work without JavaScript.

## Examples

### A palette

Tokens work too; the ring keeps the background colour visible.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch color="var(--primary)" label="Primary" />
<ColorSwatch color="var(--success)" label="Success" />
<ColorSwatch color="var(--background)" label="Background" />
```

### Pick from a palette

options turns the swatch into a group to pick one colour. The chosen one gets the ring in its own colour and a check in the ink that contrasts most.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch
  name="accent"
  label="Accent colour"
  defaultValue="#0485f7"
  options={[
    {color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"},
    {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"},
    {color: "#f0c200", label: "Aurea yellow"},
    {color: "#e11d48", label: "Ruby"},
    {color: "#7c3aed", label: "Violet"},
  ]}
/>
```

### Transparency

A colour with alpha below 1 — hex of eight digits, rgba(), hsla() — shows the checkerboard underneath.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch color="#0485f7" label="Solid" />
<ColorSwatch color="#0485f7aa" label="Two thirds" />
<ColorSwatch color="rgba(4, 133, 247, 0.35)" label="A third" />
<ColorSwatch color="#0485f700" label="Transparent" />
```

### A name for the screen reader

The swatch is an image. label names it; without it, the screen reader reads the colour's code.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch color="#16a34a" label="Forest green" />
<ColorSwatch color="#16a34a" />
```

### Options in sizes

The group takes the same five sizes.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch size="sm" name="small" label="Small" defaultValue="#0485f7" options={…} />
<ColorSwatch name="medium" label="Medium" defaultValue="#0485f7" options={…} />
<ColorSwatch size="xl" name="large" label="Large" defaultValue="#0485f7" options={…} />
```

### A colour you cannot pick

disabled on one option: the others stay available. disabled on the group turns off all of them.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch name="plan" label="Plan colour" defaultValue="#0485f7" options={[
    {color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"},
    {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"},
    {color: "#f0c200", label: "Aurea yellow", disabled: true},
    {color: "#e11d48", label: "Ruby"},
  ]} />
```

### In a column

layout="stack": one under the other.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch layout="stack" name="stack" label="Status colour" defaultValue="#16a34a"
  options={[
    {color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"},
    {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"},
    {color: "#f0c200", label: "Aurea yellow"},
    {color: "#e11d48", label: "Ruby"},
    {color: "#7c3aed", label: "Violet"},
  ]} />
```

### Starting value

defaultValue picks one when the page opens; without it, none is picked.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch name="start" label="Theme colour" defaultValue="#7c3aed" options={…} />
<ColorSwatch name="none" label="No colour yet" options={…} />
```

### Options with the value

Controlled: onChange is the browser's event, as in Radio — event.target.value is the colour.

```tsx
const [colour, setColour] = useState("#e11d48");

<ColorSwatch name="label-colour" label="Label colour" value={colour}
  onChange={(e) => setColour(e.target.value)} options={[
    {color: "#0485f7", label: "Ocean"},
    {color: "#16a34a", label: "Forest"},
    {color: "#f0c200", label: "Aurea yellow"},
    {color: "#e11d48", label: "Ruby"},
    {color: "#7c3aed", label: "Violet"},
  ]} />
```

### Another mark

indicator replaces the check on the chosen colour; it gets the ink that contrasts most.

```tsx
<ColorSwatch name="favourite" label="Favourite colour" defaultValue="#e11d48"
  indicator={<Icon name="heart" />} options={…} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | `string` | — | REQUIRED without options. Any CSS colour: #f0c200, oklch(…), var(--primary). |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | "md" | 16, 24, 32, 36, 40 — the reference library's scale. Round only (Victor's decision); the checkerboard shows only under a transparent colour. |
| `label` | `string` | color | The name a screen reader announces ("Aurea yellow"); without it, the colour value. With options, the name of the group ("Accent colour"), and REQUIRED. |
| `options` | `(string \| {color, label?})[]` | — | The picker variation (ADR-0069): the colours to pick from, as a colour string or {color, label?, disabled?}. Turns the swatch into a radio group; a disabled option cannot be chosen. |
| `name` | `string` | — | With options, REQUIRED: the group's name in a form, and what makes the swatches one group (the arrows move between them). |
| `value` | `string` | — | With options: the chosen colour, controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | — | With options: the colour chosen at the start. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | — | With options: the browser's event, as in Radio — event.target.value is the chosen colour. |
| `layout` | `"grid" \| "stack"` | "grid" | With options: in a wrapping row (grid) or in a column (stack), as in the reference. |
| `indicator` | `ReactNode` | the check | With options: the mark of the chosen colour, in place of the check (an Icon, for example). It takes the ink that contrasts most. |
| `showLabels` | `boolean` | false | With options: each colour's name under it (its label, or the colour value), like the reference's theme picker. The whole item picks; the name is only for the eyes — the radio already has it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | With options: no colour can be chosen. |
| `id` | `string` | — | With options: the id of the group. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Added to the swatch. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/combobox.html">
# Combobox

Combobox is a Select you can type into: the list filters as you write, and the value is still one option out of the set. It runs on Base UI, so the keyboard contract — arrows, Enter, Escape, type-ahead — is the APG one and not our improvisation. If the user never needs to type, a Select is lighter and works everywhere.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Combobox} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Combobox size="sm" items={items} />
<Combobox items={items} />
<Combobox size="lg" items={items} />
```

- Base UI underneath: arrows move, Enter picks, Escape closes, and focus returns where it came from.

- Options are DATA ({value, label}) — no children to keep in sync with the filter.

- Typing filters the list; the value is still one option, never free text.

- An empty result says so in words, from the i18n dictionary.

- disabled goes on the whole control: field and both buttons, never one without the other.

- The previews show the CLOSED field; the popup lives in a portal and only exists in a real app.

## Examples

### Single choice

One option out of many, with the list filtering as you type.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(null);

<Combobox label="Component" placeholder="Search…" value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
  items={[{value: "button", label: "Button"}, {value: "badge", label: "Badge"}]} />
```

### Inside a Field

The Field names the question; the Combobox holds the answer.

```tsx
<Field label="Assignee" hint="Who picks this up">
  <Combobox items={people} value={who} onValueChange={setWho} />
</Field>
```

### Disabled

The field and both buttons go down together — a locked field that still opens is not locked.

```tsx
<Combobox label="Component" placeholder="Search…" items={items} disabled />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `ComboboxOption[] \| ComboboxOptGroup[]` | — | The options, as data: {value, label} — or groups of them, {label, items}. Grouping is the engine's own shape: the same `items` prop takes either, and the kind is read from the first element. Do not mix flat with grouped. |
| `value` | `ComboboxOption \| null` | — | The selected option, or null. |
| `onValueChange` | `(v) => void` | — | Fires with the chosen option. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Shown while nothing is selected. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Accessible name of the field. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | Turns off the field and both buttons at once. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | "No results" | What the list shows when nothing matches. A fixed string cannot say 'no fruit by that name', and the engine always allowed the content to be written. |
| `size` | `Responsive<'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'>` | md | The system's size step, not the HTML character count — it paints the inner input with the same .input-sm/.input-lg skin as the rest of the field family. Responsive: it resolves in the CSS layer, so it costs no observer. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the INPUT, not of the container — it is what a <label htmlFor> has to point at. Without it one is generated. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the field wrapper, not onto the input. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | Goes to the input, which is the focusable node. It is spelled out because this component unpacks a fixed list of props and silently drops anything else — that is what kept Field from reaching the input (AUD-0001). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | — | Same route and same reason as aria-describedby: the input carries it, the wrapper would not announce it. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible name when there is no visible label — a filter in a grid without labels. With `label`, prefer `label`. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/commandpalette.html">
# CommandPalette

The command palette with the engine wired up: type, filter, run.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CommandPalette} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Button leadingIcon="magnifying-glass" kbd="⌘K" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Search</Button>

<CommandPalette open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} items={[
  {id: "button", label: "Button", icon: "squares-four", group: "Components", run: () => go("/button")},
  {id: "close", label: "CloseButton", icon: "squares-four", group: "Components", run: () => go("/close-button")},
  {id: "theme", label: "Toggle theme", icon: "moon", kbd: "⌘T", group: "Actions", run: toggleTheme},
]} />
// Items with a group come together under its title; the line under the list teaches the keys.
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | REQUIRED. You own the state, as in Dialog and Drawer. Closed, it renders nothing at all. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | — | REQUIRED. Fires on Escape and after a command is chosen — in that order: closing happens BEFORE the command runs, so a command that navigates does not leave the palette floating over the new screen. |
| `items` | `CommandItem[]` | — | REQUIRED. Commands as DATA ({id, label, icon?, kbd?, run}), never children — a list kept as children drifts out of sync with the filter, which is the same decision Combobox took. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | "Type a command…" | Also the accessible name of the input. |
| `label` | `string` | "Command palette" | Accessible name of the dialog. |
| `shortcuts` | `boolean` | true | The line under the list that teaches the keys: ↑ ↓ move, Enter open, Esc close. Each item may also say its group (item.group): items of the same group come together under its title. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/commandpaletteshell.html">
# CommandPaletteShell

Overlay shell for a searchable command palette.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CommandPaletteShell} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<CommandPaletteShell open={open} query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery}>
  <div className="menu">
    <button className="menu-item" type="button">Go to Button</button>
    <button className="menu-item" type="button">Toggle theme</button>
  </div>
</CommandPaletteShell>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | Controlled. Closed it renders null, so nothing is left in the DOM to be tabbed into. |
| `query` | `string` | — | The value of the search field. Controlled, because the filtering is yours. |
| `onQueryChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Every keystroke. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | — | Called when the dialog asks to close — Escape, or a click outside. Without it the dialog stays open until `open` changes. |
| `label` | `string` | "Command palette" | The name of the dialog. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The results, rendered by you. The shell owns the surface and the field; matching is domain knowledge and does not belong to a design system. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/confirmdialog.html">
# ConfirmDialog

Alert dialog for a decision that cannot be taken back.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ConfirmDialog} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Delete article</Button>

<ConfirmDialog
  open={open}
  title="Delete this article?"
  description="It leaves the site immediately, and this cannot be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  destructive
  icon="trash"
  onConfirm={() => { remove(); setOpen(false); }}
  onCancel={() => setOpen(false)}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | REQUIRED. You own the state, as in Dialog and Drawer. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | REQUIRED. The question, in the words of the thing at stake — "Delete this article?", not "Are you sure?". |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | REQUIRED, and it is a prop rather than children because it is the node behind aria-describedby: only what goes through it gets announced. Say what is lost and whether it comes back. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | "Continue" | Name the action, not the agreement: "Delete" tells the reader what the button does; "OK" makes them remember the title. |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | "Cancel" | The way out. It is the focused control when the dialog opens. |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | false | Turns the confirm button danger. Use it when the action destroys data — not for merely important ones, or the colour stops meaning anything. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void` | — | REQUIRED. Fires only on the confirm button. Nothing else in this dialog can reach it. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | — | REQUIRED. Fires on the cancel button and on Escape. A click outside does NOT close this dialog — that is the difference from Dialog, and it is why an accidental click cannot answer for the user. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | — | An icon in a 40 circle above the title, as in the reference library's alert dialog. |
| `iconTone` | `"neutral" \| "brand" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | destructive ? "danger" : "neutral" | The circle's colour. Left out, it follows destructive. |
| `placement` | `"auto" \| "center" \| "top" \| "bottom"` | "auto" | Where it sits; auto is at the bottom on a phone and in the middle from 640 up. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/container.html">
# Container

The reading width of a website page: centred, capped, with side gutters that grow with the screen.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Container} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Container>
  <Heading level={2}>Fichas técnicas</Heading>
</Container>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl" \| "docs" \| "full"` | "xl" | How far the content grows, by the names of the breakpoint scale: sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280 (the default), 2xl 1536, docs 1400 (the documentation block, with 24 of padding from 768 up), or full with no cap. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The page content. The side gutter is --space-4 (16) on a narrow screen and --space-8 (32) from the md breakpoint up. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra classes on the <div>. |
</page>

# ContainerScope

Declares an Aurea container: the box that container-responsive values measure themselves against.

```tsx
import {ContainerScope} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ContainerScope>
  <Toolbar orientation={{base: "vertical", container: {sm: "horizontal"}}}>
    <Button>Salvar</Button>
    <Button>Descartar</Button>
  </Toolbar>
</ContainerScope>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | What is measured against this box. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the outermost element, after the Aurea skin — your class wins on a tie. |

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/contextmenu.html">
# ContextMenu

Actions menu opened by right-click or long-press.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ContextMenu} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ContextMenu label="Row actions" items={[
  {label: "Rename", leadingIcon: "pencil-simple"},
  "separator",
  {label: "Delete", leadingIcon: "trash"},
]}>
  <Card>Right-click me, or focus and press Shift+F10.</Card>
</ContextMenu>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The region that answers the right button. It is rendered focusable (tabIndex 0) on purpose: the keyboard route into a context menu is Shift+F10 or the Menu key, and the browser only fires those over a FOCUSED element. Without that, the menu is mouse-only. |
| `items` | `Array<MenuItemDef \| "separator">` | — | The menu, as data: {label, onClick?, disabled?, leadingIcon?}. The literal string "separator" draws a rule — a separator is not an item, so it never takes focus. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Names both the trigger region and the menu. A right-click target with no name is announced as nothing at all. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Goes on the trigger region, which is the element you can see. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/costmeter.html">
# CostMeter

Spend against a ceiling, with the soft and hard limits kept apart.

## Usage

```tsx
import {CostMeter} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<CostMeter spent={84.2} limit={100} softLimit={80} period="This month" />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spent` | `number` | — | Amount spent in the period. Costs below one cent are printed with up to six decimals: two fixed decimals, which is what the reference formatter uses, would print "$0.00" for a real spend of $0.004 and blank out the number in the very component built to watch it. |
| `limit` | `number` | — | The hard ceiling — the one that blocks. Without it there is no meter and no bar, only the amount. Measured from LiteLLM, the 2026 market standard for LLM cost control. |
| `softLimit` | `number` | — | The threshold that only warns. Absent, there is no warning state: deriving one at 80% of the limit would be an invented number, and an alert firing at a threshold nobody configured is noise wearing the clothes of a policy. Crossing it does NOT repaint the bar — measured: in the dark theme --warning-400 IS the brand yellow, the same value as --primary, so a warning bar would be indistinguishable from a normal one. The soft limit speaks in words, through the Alert; colour is kept for the hard limit, where red separates in both themes. |
| `segments` | `CostSegment[]` | — | Optional breakdown of the amount — input, output, cache — rendered as a DataList. |
| `period` | `ReactNode` | "Spent" | What the amount refers to, shown beside it: "This month", "Last 24h". |
| `currency` | `string` | "USD" | ISO currency code. |
| `locale` | `string` | "en-US" | Passed to Intl.NumberFormat. Fixed by default for the same reason as in ModelUsage: deterministic output across machines. |
| `label` | `string` | "Cost" | Accessible name of the region and of the meter. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the card. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/datagrid.html">
# DataGrid

Interactive grid with navigation, sort and selection.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DataGrid} from "@aurea-uds/react/data-grid";
```

```tsx
<DataGrid
  label="Members"
  filterable
  data={[{name: "Messenger", role: "Owner"}, {name: "Analyst", role: "Editor"}]}
  columns={[
    {accessorKey: "name", header: "Name"},
    {accessorKey: "role", header: "Role"},
  ]}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `T[]` | — | The rows. Sorted, filtered and paged in memory by default; pass the `manual*` flags when the server already did that work and `data` is a single page. |
| `columns` | `Array<ColumnDef<T, any>>` | — | TanStack Table column definitions, re-exported from this subpath so you do not add the dependency yourself. |
| `getRowId` | `(row: T, index: number) => string` | — | Pass it whenever `selectable` is on. Without a stable id TanStack keys selection by INDEX, so replacing or reordering `data` makes a checkbox follow the position and tick a different record. The grid covers the safe half on its own — it clears the selection when `data` changes — but only an id makes selection survive the change. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | false | Adds the checkbox column, header included. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(rows: T[]) => void` | — | Receives the ORIGINAL rows, taken before filtering and paging — so a selection does not vanish because you typed in the filter. Under `manualPagination` it can only hand you rows from the page in memory; use `onRowSelectionChange` there, which gives ids. |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | — | Controlled sort. Passing it hands the decision to you: the grid stops moving on its own and only reports through `onSortingChange`, so you can validate, confirm or wait for a request before letting it change. |
| `onSortingChange` | `(sorting: SortingState) => void` | — | Fires on every header click, controlled or not. Alone it does not make the grid controlled — `sorting` does. |
| `globalFilter` | `string` | — | Controlled value of the search field. Same rule as `sorting`: with it, typing reports and nothing narrows until you say so. |
| `onGlobalFilterChange` | `(filter: string) => void` | — | Fires on every keystroke in the search field. |
| `page` | `number` | — | Controlled page, 1-based — the same counting the visible Pagination uses, not the engine's 0-based index. A position in a list, not a dimension. |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` | — | Receives the 1-based page the reader asked for. |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | — | Controlled selection, keyed by row id — so it survives paging and reloading, which a list of rows cannot. Pair it with `getRowId`. |
| `onRowSelectionChange` | `(selection: RowSelectionState) => void` | — | The id map, every time it changes. This is the selection API for server-side data; `onSelectionChange` is the convenience one for a set held in memory. |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` | false | The server sorted. The grid stops sorting in memory but still marks the sorted column with `aria-sort`, so the reader is told what changed. |
| `manualFiltering` | `boolean` | false | The server filtered. Typing reports and nothing is hidden locally. |
| `manualPagination` | `boolean` | false | The server paged, and `data` is one page. Requires `rowCount`: without it there is no way to know how many pages exist and the pagination disappears from the screen. |
| `bulkActions` | `Array<{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; onAction: (rows: T[], clear: () => void) => void }>` | — | Turns a selection into something you can act on: a toolbar appears with the count, the actions, and a way to clear. `onAction` receives the ORIGINAL rows — taken before filtering, so acting on what the filter hid is still possible — and the `clear` function, so an action can drop the selection once it has run. No bar is drawn without a selection: it is the state, not decoration. |
| `filters` | `Array<{ column: string; label: string; facet?: boolean; options?: Array<{ value: string; label: string }> }>` | — | Adds a filter row inside the table header, one control per declared column, aligned with the column because the table is what aligns it. `facet: true` gives a multi-select built from the values present in the data, each option carrying its count. Declare `options` when a value must stay on the list even with no rows behind it — the difference between "no cancelled ones" and "cancelled does not exist". |
| `columnFilters` | `ColumnFiltersState` | — | Controlled per-column filters, same rule as `sorting`: with it, typing and picking report and nothing narrows until you say so. To put it in the address bar, `gridStateToParams` and `gridStateFromParams` are the format — imported from the package root, not from this subpath, because the code that reads a URL runs on the server and this subpath is client-only. The grid never writes the URL itself: only you know whether a change should push a history entry or replace one. |
| `onColumnFiltersChange` | `(filters: ColumnFiltersState) => void` | — | Fires whenever a column filter changes, controlled or not. |
| `rowCount` | `number` | — | Total rows on the server, used to compute the page count under `manualPagination`. A count, not a dimension. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | false | Pins the header — and the filter row with it — while the body scrolls. It also gives the scroll box a height, because it has to: the wrapper is the scroll container, and a box with no ceiling never scrolls inside itself, so the header would never have anything to detach from. The ceiling is `--datagrid-max-h` (60vh by default), set in CSS rather than as a prop — only the page knows how much screen it can spare, and a height is not a number this library accepts as an API. |
| `hideableColumns` | `boolean` | false | Adds a picker that turns columns on and off — the same multi-select the facet filter uses, because choosing several from a list is that component. When it is the only control, the search field keeps the full width it always had; the two only share a row when both are there. |
| `columnVisibility` | `VisibilityState` | — | Controlled map of column id to visible. It is a plain serialisable object, which is what makes the choice persistable — where it is persisted (local storage, user profile, the URL) is yours to decide, exactly as in F4. |
| `onColumnVisibilityChange` | `(visibility: VisibilityState) => void` | — | Fires whenever a column is shown or hidden. |
| `resizableColumns` | `boolean` | false | Adds a drag handle at the trailing edge of each header cell. The handle is a real button and answers the ARROW KEYS as well — 16px a press — because the engine only gives dragging, and a column you can only resize with a mouse is a feature that excludes people. |
| `columnSizing` | `ColumnSizingState` | — | Controlled map of column id to width in pixels. Serialisable, same rule as `columnVisibility`. |
| `onColumnSizingChange` | `(sizing: ColumnSizingState) => void` | — | Fires while dragging and on each arrow key. |
| `state` | `"loading" \| "error" \| "waiting_user" \| "waiting_approval" \| "waiting_dependency" \| "offline" \| "stale" \| "partial" \| "degraded"` | — | Says out loud what is going on with the data. `stale` and `partial` keep the rows on screen and label them, because a table showing old data without saying so is worse than an empty one. `error` uses `role="alert"` so it interrupts a screen reader; the other two use `role="status"` and wait for the next pause. `loading` never blanks rows that are already there — reloading is no reason to take away what someone was reading — and only draws skeleton rows when there is nothing to show. Since Part J the seven universal states are accepted here too, under the names the contract gives them — `stale` and `partial` already had them, which is why nothing was renamed. `loading` and `error` stay specific to this grid on purpose: in all seven universal states the screen still works, and with no rows at all it does not. The grid keeps its own three sentences because they talk about rows, and more specific wins over more general; the shared wording covers the four it did not have. |
| `stateMessage` | `string` | — | Replaces the built-in sentence. Only you know what actually failed: "the billing service is down" beats "the rows could not be loaded". |
| `renderDetail` | `(row: T) => ReactNode` | — | Adds a trailing column with a Details button per row, and opens what you return in a panel BESIDE the list — the list stays on screen, which is the point. The trigger is a button and not a clickable row: a row is not a focus target, and turning it into one means inventing a role, a tabindex and a key that a button already is. Closed, the markup is exactly what it was without this prop. |
| `detailRowId` | `string \| null` | — | Controlled id of the row whose panel is open. Same rule as every other axis here. |
| `onDetailRowIdChange` | `(id: string \| null) => void` | — | Fires when a panel opens or closes. |
| `onExport` | `(rows: T[], scope: { count: number; filtered: boolean; selected: boolean }) => void` | — | Draws a button whose LABEL states the scope — "Export 47 filtered rows", never a bare "Export", because the bare word hides the question that matters. Precedence follows what the person just did: a selection wins over a filter, a filter wins over everything. The grid produces no file: format, encoding and transport are yours, the same boundary the upload queue draws. |
| `filterable` | `boolean` | false | Draws the search field that filters across every column. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | — | Rows per page; passing it is what turns pagination on. A count of rows, not a dimension — there is nothing to measure here. |
| `label` | `string` | "Table" | Accessible name of the scrollable region around the table. That region is focusable on purpose, so a table wider than the screen can be scrolled with the arrow keys — the same wrapper the plain Table uses. Cell-by-cell arrow navigation is the APG grid pattern and this component does NOT implement it: it is a table with interactive controls in it, which is what the header buttons and the checkboxes are. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the grid wrapper. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/datalist.html">
# DataList

Key/value or item list for structured data.

```tsx
import {DataList} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<DataList items={[
  {term: "Plan", value: "Pro"},
  {term: "Seats", value: "12"},
]} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `Array<{term: ReactNode; value: ReactNode}>` | — | Term and value pairs, rendered as a real <dl>. The pairing is in the markup, so it survives with the stylesheet off and reads correctly to a screen reader. |
