<page url="https://aureauds.dev/datastate.html">
# DataState

One region, four faces: loading, failed, empty, or the content itself.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DataState} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<DataState state={query.state} message={query.error} skeleton={<InvoiceSkeleton />}
  emptyTitle="No invoices" action={<Button variant="primary">New invoice</Button>}>
  {() => <InvoiceTable rows={query.data} />}
</DataState>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `loading \| error \| empty \| UniversalState` | — | Leave it out and the children render, plain. THE RULE THAT MATTERS: the three terminal faces (loading, error, empty) replace the content, and every universal state (stale, partial, degraded, offline, waiting_*) does NOT — it keeps the content on screen and puts the notice above it. Showing old data without saying so is worse than showing none, and hiding what the reader already had because it went stale is losing information they were using. This is the same decision DataGrid took. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| (() => ReactNode)` | — | REQUIRED. Pass a function when building the content is expensive: in the loading face it is never called, so you do not pay to render what has not arrived. |
| `message` | `ReactNode` | — | Replaces the built-in sentence. Only you know what actually failed — "the billing service is down" beats "this could not be loaded". |
| `skeleton` | `ReactNode` | — | The shape of what is coming. The default is a single bar, which is honest but says nothing; a skeleton that mirrors the real layout is what stops the page from jumping when the data lands. |
| `emptyTitle` | `ReactNode` | "Nothing here yet" | Say what is missing in the words of the thing: "No invoices" beats "No results". |
| `emptyIcon` | `IconName` | "document--blank" | Passed through to EmptyState. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | — | The way out of the empty face — usually the button that creates the first one. |
| `catchErrors` | `boolean` | false | Catches a rendering error inside the region and shows the error face in its place, with a "Try again" button that renders the content again — the rest of the screen stays. Without it, the error goes up as before and can blank the whole page. The message prop also applies to this face. |
| `onCatch` | `(error: unknown, info: ErrorInfo) => void` | — | Called once for each error caught by catchErrors, with the error and React's component stack — the place to send it to your error log. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/datepicker.html">
# DatePicker

DatePicker is a field that opens the calendar. One date closes it on the pick; with range, the first pick is one end and the second the other, every time it opens.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DatePicker} from "@aurea-uds/react/calendar";
```

```tsx
<Field label="Check-in">
  <DatePicker defaultValue={new Date(2026, 7, 12)} minimumDate={new Date(2026, 7, 6)} name="checkin" />
</Field>
```

- The same name and props as the native DatePicker: value, onChange, minimumDate, maximumDate, disabled, size, format, placeholder, icon.

- range picks a range in the same component; every opening starts a new range.

- Inside a Field, the label names the trigger and the calendar window; the calendar opens with focus on the chosen day.

- locale sets the language of the trigger and the calendar together, with the same object Calendar takes. Without it, English.

- name sends the LOCAL date as yyyy-mm-dd; a range goes as yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd.

## Examples

### A range

The first pick is one end and the second the other, in any order.

```tsx
<Field label="Stay">
  <DatePicker range defaultValue={{from: new Date(2026, 7, 12), to: new Date(2026, 7, 18)}} name="stay" />
</Field>
```

### Another language

The trigger and the calendar change language together.

```tsx
import {ptBR} from "react-day-picker/locale";

<Field label="Check-in">
  <DatePicker locale={ptBR} defaultValue={new Date(2026, 7, 12)} />
</Field>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Date \| DateRange` | — | The chosen date (controlled). With range, {from, to}. |
| `defaultValue` | `Date \| DateRange` | — | The starting date when you do not control it. |
| `onChange` | `(value) => void` | — | Called on every pick. A single date closes the calendar; a range closes on the second pick. |
| `range` | `boolean` | false | Pick a range instead of one date. Every time the calendar opens, the first pick is one end and the second is the other, in any order — it does not stretch the range that was there. |
| `minimumDate` | `Date` | — | Days before it are disabled, and the calendar does not go back past its month. |
| `maximumDate` | `Date` | — | Days after it are disabled, and the calendar does not go past its month. |
| `format` | `(d: Date) => string` | the locale's language | How a date is written on the trigger. The default is day, short month and year in the language of locale — English without it, the same on the server and in the browser. |
| `locale` | `DayPickerLocale` | English | The language of the trigger AND the calendar, together: the object from react-day-picker/locale (import {ptBR} from "react-day-picker/locale"), the same one Calendar takes. It never comes from the environment, so the server and the browser write the same text. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | strings.datePlaceholder | The text of the empty trigger. With range, strings.dateRangePlaceholder. |
| `icon` | `IconName \| false` | "calendar" | The icon at the end of the trigger; false removes it. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Sends the value with a form: yyyy-mm-dd, from the LOCAL date; a range goes as yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd, the ISO 8601 interval. |
| `size` | `Responsive<sm \| md \| lg>` | md | The field height, the same scale as Select and Input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | The trigger does not open. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the TRIGGER, which is the focusable node — it is what a <label htmlFor> points at. Inside a Field, the Field gives it one. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Names the trigger when there is no visible label, and the calendar window too. With a Field, prefer the Field's label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` | — | Names the trigger and the calendar window by another element's id. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | Goes to the trigger. It is spelled out because this component unpacks a fixed list of props and drops anything else. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the trigger, after the Aurea skin. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/dependencygraph.html">
# DependencyGraph

Who depends on whom, on a canvas you can pan, zoom and build on.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DependencyGraph} from "@aurea-uds/react/graph";
import "@xyflow/react/dist/base.css";
```

```tsx
<DependencyGraph
  nodes={[
    {id: "ingest", label: "Ingest", kind: "source"},
    {id: "embed", label: "Embed", kind: "model"},
    {id: "index", label: "Index", kind: "store"},
    {id: "answer", label: "Answer", kind: "agent"},
  ]}
  edges={[
    {from: "ingest", to: "embed"},
    {from: "embed", to: "index"},
    {from: "index", to: "answer"},
  ]}
  onSelect={setSelected}
  selectedId={selected}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nodes` | `GraphNodeItem[]` | — | The vocabulary is ours, not the engine's. x and y are optional: without them a layered longest-path layout runs, because the engine positions nothing on its own and a graph with no coordinates piles every node at 0,0. A node can carry an `icon` (a sprite name or the app's own drawing) NEXT TO its kind, never instead of it; a `count` badge (with `countLabel` for the screen reader); a `status` badge (a word, with a tone that only reinforces it); `ports` (named handles on a chosen side); and a `layer`, the band the node sits in on the `layered` layout. `layer` is an ORDER, not an index: 0, 5 and 10 become the 1st, 2nd and 3rd band, and nodes with the same `layer` sit at the same height. It applies only when EVERY node outside a container has one (a container takes its own `layer`, or the smallest one inside it); with `layer` on only some nodes the map comes out as if there were none, and says so once in the console. INSIDE a container the engine arranges on its own: there `layer` does not apply (sending it there breaks the whole map, measured). Round 2: `parentId` puts the node inside a CONTAINER (site, floor, rack — one parent each; a VLAN is a filter, not a container, because one device sits in several); `collapsed` starts a container or a subtree closed; `pinned` keeps the node where it is; `shape: "cloud"` draws it as a cloud (Internet, public cloud, remote site). |
| `edges` | `GraphEdgeItem[]` | — | {from, to} — not {source, target}. Keeping our own words is what lets the engine be replaced without breaking anyone, the same reason Chart does not expose Recharts types. An edge can attach to ports (`fromPort`, `toPort`), write port names at its ends (`sourceLabel`, `targetLabel`), and say what it is without relying on colour: `pattern` (solid, dashed, dotted, double), `weight` (regular, thick, heavy), `mark` in the middle (cross, dot, lock), a `count` (for example the members of a link aggregation) and a `legend` name — the KIND of link (copper, fibre). Its STATE is separate: `status` (`label`, `tone`, and an optional `mark` such as the cross of a down link), the same shape as a node's status badge. The tone colours the line and doubles its thickness (all three weights double together, so speed still reads between coloured lines) — a hairline loses its colour when the map is zoomed out. The word goes into the legend, so colour is never the only signal. Round 2: `priority` decides which label stays when two labels touch (higher wins; on a tie, the earlier edge). |
| `selectedId` | `string \| null` | — | Controlled selection. |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | — | Without it nodes are plain text instead of buttons — a control that does nothing does not get drawn. |
| `connectable` | `boolean` | false | Shows the connection handles. Off by default: a handle hanging off a read-only graph is an affordance lying — it promises a drag that goes nowhere. |
| `onConnect` | `(edge: {from: string; to: string; fromPort?: string; toPort?: string}) => void` | — | Fires when someone draws a new edge. |
| `onNodeMove` | `(id: string, pos: {x: number; y: number}) => void` | — | Enables dragging and reports where the node landed. Whoever passes x and y back keeps the position; that is what lets a builder store what the person arranged without fighting the automatic layout. |
| `height` | `string` | "28rem" | A canvas needs a definite height or it collapses. A CSS length, not a number — check 23. |
| `label` | `string` | "Dependency graph" | Accessible name of the group. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the canvas wrapper. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | "horizontal" | `vertical` draws top to bottom: edges enter a node from the top and leave from the bottom, and each layer is centred on the widest one, so the root sits in the middle. |
| `layout` | `"simple" \| "layered" \| "tree" \| "radial"` | "simple" | `layered` arranges the graph with elkjs (an optional peer): fewer crossings, balanced children, ports where the node draws them, children INSIDE their container, and right-angle routes with parallel lines kept apart. `tree` is a compact tree and `radial` puts the root in the centre with straight lines. They arrive after the first paint; the simple layout stands until then. |
| `rootId` | `string` | — | The node pinned to the first layer in the `layered` layout. |
| `edgeShape` | `"curve" \| "step"` | "curve" | `step` draws edges at right angles, with the small radius at each bend. In the `layered` layout the route comes from elkjs and keeps parallel lines apart; after a manual arrangement, a line that would cross a node is routed around it by @tisoap/react-flow-smart-edge (an optional peer). Where a line crosses another, the one drawn later jumps over it. |
| `groupParallel` | `boolean` | false | Edges between the same two nodes (in either direction) collapse into one line with their count. The count is a button that expands them into separate lines and joins them again; its name says what it does and how many. |
| `minimap` | `boolean` | false | An overview in the corner, with the visible area marked. It can be dragged and zoomed. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | false | Zoom in, zoom out and fit-to-screen buttons in the corner. |
| `legend` | `boolean` | false | A legend built from what is on the canvas, in two parts: the KIND of link (one row per distinct `legend` name, drawn without colour) and its STATE (one row per distinct `status.label`, drawn in its tone). Each sample shows what all the lines in its row share — a fibre row stays double even when only some fibre lines are thick. With only one part, it is a single list without titles. |
| `focusId` | `string \| null` | — | Centres the canvas on this node and marks it — the 'go to' of a search. The mark is the brand border, not the keyboard focus ring. |
| `highlight` | `{nodes?: string[]; edges?: string[]} \| null` | — | Lights a path and dims everything else. Edges are matched by their `id`; without edge ids, an edge stays lit when both its ends are lit. |
| `highlightNeighbors` | `boolean` | false | With a selected node, lights it, its neighbours and the edges between them, and dims the rest. |
| `hiddenIds` | `string[]` | — | Hides these nodes and their edges WITHOUT re-running the layout: everything else stays exactly where it was. Filtering a map should not reshuffle it. |
| `onNodeHover` | `(id: string \| null) => void` | — | The pointer entered a node (its id) or left it (null) — for a summary card. |
| `onNodeContextMenu` | `(id: string, point: {x: number; y: number}) => void` | — | Right click on a node, with the point on the screen — for a ContextMenu. The browser's own menu does not open. |
| `onEdgeSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | — | A click on an edge, or Enter on a focused edge. With it, edges show the pointer and take the Tab; without it they do neither, because nothing would answer. |
| `textSize` | `"md" \| "lg"` | "md" | The text of the nodes and edge labels, independent of zoom. `lg` grows the node box in the same proportion, so names do not cut sooner. |
| `highContrast` | `boolean` | false | Edges, labels and node borders in the text colour, and the base line thickness doubles. Every weight and pattern is a multiple of the base, so they all follow. |
| `apiRef` | `Ref<DependencyGraphApi>` | — | Commands for the app: fitView(), zoomIn(), zoomOut(), focus(id), toDrawio() (a draw.io file with the current positions), toPng() and toSvg() (a data: URL; they need modern-screenshot). Round 2: undo(), redo(), align(edge), distribute(axis), relayout() and getLayout(). |
| `editable` | `boolean` | false | The ARRANGE mode: dragging on empty canvas draws a lasso; Shift, Ctrl or Cmd add to the selection; dragging moves every selected node; a toolbar aligns, distributes, pins, rearranges, undoes and redoes; arrow keys move the selection (with Shift, four steps); Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y, and Ctrl+A. The canvas pans with the middle or right button, or Space + drag. Off, it is the read-only map. |
| `grid` | `boolean` | true | The snapping grid of the arrange mode (16 px, `--space-4`), drawn as the background dots. |
| `onLayoutChange` | `(layout: GraphLayoutChange) => void` | — | The arrangement changed — a drag, align, distribute, pin, rearrange, undo or redo. It carries every node's position and the pinned ids; storing it is the app's job. Whoever passes the positions back as x/y keeps them. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(ids: string[]) => void` | — | The selection of the arrange mode. With exactly one node selected, `onSelect` is called too. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | false | Nodes with a subtree get the button to close and open it. A node's subtree is what can only be reached THROUGH it — with a redundant cable, an access switch does not vanish with one of its two cores. Containers always have the button. |
| `onCollapseChange` | `(id: string, collapsed: boolean) => void` | — | A container or a subtree opened or closed. |
| `visibleOnly` | `boolean` | false | Renders only what is on screen — for a very large map. |
| `layoutWorker` | `() => Worker` | — | A worker that runs elkjs off the main thread. The app provides it because each bundler creates workers its own way, and copying elkjs's worker into this package would redistribute it; the README has the recipe. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/dialog.html">
# Dialog

Modal surface that interrupts for a focused task.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Dialog} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Delete project</Button>

<Dialog
  open={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Delete project"
  icon="trash"
  iconTone="danger"
  footer={<><Button variant="tertiary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete</Button></>}
>
  This removes every component and token in it. It cannot be undone.
</Dialog>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | Controlled, always. The dialog never closes itself; it asks, through onClose, and you decide. Two sources for one piece of state is how a dialog gets stuck open. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | Rendered as the <h2> in the header and used as the accessible name. Required: a modal with no name announces only "dialog". |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The body. It is the part that scrolls; the header and footer stay put. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | — | The actions row. Leave it out and the footer is not rendered at all, rather than rendered empty. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | — | Called by Escape, by the backdrop, and by the close button — one exit for the three, so a dialog cannot be dismissable one way and not another. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "full"` | "md" | The width: the reference library's four — xs 320, sm 384, md 448 (the default) and lg 512 —, xl (1024, the --breakpoint-lg token) for a wide detail view, and full: the screen minus the usual margin, keeping the 22 radius. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | true | false keeps the dialog open during an operation: no Escape, no click outside, and the close button is DISABLED rather than hidden, so the header does not move mid-operation. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | — | An icon in a 40 circle above the title, as in the reference library. Decorative: the title says what the dialog is. |
| `iconTone` | `"neutral" \| "brand" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | "neutral" | The circle's colour: the state colours (the *-bg fill and the -400 glyph, ADR-0061), or brand — the light yellow wash with the yellow-as-text glyph. |
| `placement` | `"auto" \| "center" \| "top" \| "bottom"` | "auto" | Where the dialog sits. auto, the reference library's default: at the BOTTOM on a phone (below 640, where the thumb reaches) and in the middle from 640 up. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/drawer.html">
# Drawer

Panel that slides in from a screen edge.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Drawer} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit member</Button>

<Drawer open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Edit member" side="right"
  footer={<Button variant="primary">Save</Button>}>
  <Field label="Name"><Input defaultValue="Analyst" /></Field>
</Drawer>

// On a phone, the panel that rises from the bottom (swipe down to close):
<Drawer open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Filters" side="bottom">…</Drawer>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | Controlled, same contract as Dialog. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | The <h2> in the header, and the accessible name. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The panel body. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | — | The actions row, at the end, with 8 between the buttons. Left out, there is no footer. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | — | Escape, backdrop and close button all route here. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "top" \| "bottom"` | right | The edge it slides from — all four, as in the reference library; bottom is the panel that rises on a phone. left/right are PHYSICAL sides. The side ones are 320 wide on a phone and 384 from 640 up (never more than 85% of the screen), with the 22 corner on the inner side; top and bottom take the full width and up to 85% of the height, with the 32 sheet corner and the 36 × 4 handle. A swipe toward its edge closes it. The default is right (the reference library's is bottom). |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/dropdownmenu.html">
# DropdownMenu

Menu of actions triggered by a control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DropdownMenu} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<DropdownMenu
  label="Record actions"
  trigger={<Button variant="outline" trailingIcon="caret-down">Actions</Button>}
  items={[
    {label: "Duplicate", leadingIcon: "copy"},
    {label: "Rename", leadingIcon: "pencil-simple"},
    "separator",
    {label: "Delete", leadingIcon: "trash"},
  ]}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `ReactElement` | — | The element that opens the menu. Usually a Button or an IconButton. |
| `items` | `Array<MenuItemDef \| "separator">` | — | The menu, as data: {label, onClick?, disabled?, leadingIcon?}. The literal string "separator" draws a rule — a separator is not an item, so it never takes focus. |
| `side` | `top \| right \| bottom \| left` | bottom | Preferred side; it flips when there is no room. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Accessible name of the menu itself. Worth setting when a page has more than one — otherwise a screen reader lists several menus with nothing to tell them apart. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/emptystate.html">
# EmptyState

Placeholder for an empty or zero-result view.

## Usage

```tsx
import {EmptyState} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<EmptyState
  titleAs="h2"
  title="No results"
  description="Try a different filter."
  action={<Button variant="primary" leadingIcon="plus">New project</Button>}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | What is not here. Required: an empty state without a sentence is a blank area. |
| `titleAs` | `h2 \| h3 \| h4 \| p` | h3 | The heading level belongs to the DOCUMENT, not to the component. Frozen at h3, an empty state at the top of a page jumps h1 → h3 and axe fails heading-order. Pass `p` when it is not a heading at all. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | One line on why it is empty, or on what fills it. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | — | The way out — usually a Button. An empty state with nothing to do next is a dead end. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | — | Glyph above the title, rendered at size xl. Defaults to `document--blank`. |
| `state` | `waiting_user \| waiting_approval \| waiting_dependency \| offline \| stale \| partial \| degraded` | — | Universal state (Part J). It derives no colour on purpose — an empty view is already neutral, and colouring it would be an alarm where there is only absence. What it does is set `data-state` and supply the default description, so “no connection” is not seven different sentences on seven screens. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/eventstream.html">
# EventStream

What happened, in order, live.

## Usage

```tsx
import {EventStream} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<EventStream events={[
  {id: "1", title: "Run started", time: "10:02", group: "Today"},
  {id: "2", title: "Tool denied", time: "10:04", severity: "danger"},
]} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `events` | `StreamEvent[]` | — | Consecutive events sharing a `group` are rendered under one heading. This is NOT LogStream, and the difference is the ROLE, not the look: `role="log"` is for text output that piles up; an event has structure — title, time, severity — so it is `role="feed"`. |
| `follow` | `boolean` | false | Scrolls to the newest event. Opt-in, and deliberately so: without it whoever is reading the top misses what arrives, but WITH it and no control, whoever is reading the middle gets dragged down. |
| `label` | `string` | "Events" | Accessible name of the feed. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the feed. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/field.html">
# Field

Field is the label, the help text and the error of a control, bound together. It gives one unnamed control a real <label for> and a matching id, so clicking the label focuses it and the screen reader gets a precise name. Field organises; Input is the control. That distinction is why they are two components.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Field, Input} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Field label="E-mail" required><Input type="email" /></Field>
```

- One unnamed native control or documented Aurea control gets a real <label for> and a matching id; arbitrary wrappers become groups.

- hint and error are descriptions via aria-describedby; they never become the accessible name.

- error also marks the focal control invalid — a red field alone tells a colour-blind user nothing.

- A child with its own accessible name (label or ARIA), or several children, makes Field a named group instead of adding a second label.

- The label is required by the type. A field with no label is not a field, it is a box.

## Examples

### With hint

Label, control and help in one block. The hint explains, it does not repeat the label.

```tsx
<Field label="Email" hint="We never share it.">
  <Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
</Field>
```

### With error

The error joins the hint in the accessible description and marks the control invalid. Never colour alone.

```tsx
<Field label="Workspace slug" error="Already taken.">
  <Input defaultValue="aurea" />
</Field>
```

### Any control

A single unnamed control gets a real label; a control with its own accessible name stays named by itself inside the Field group.

```tsx
<Field label="Region"><Select>…</Select></Field>
<Field label="Notes"><Textarea rows={3} /></Field>
<Field label="Volume"><Range defaultValue={60} /></Field>
```

### Required and disabled

State belongs to the control, not to the wrapper: Field only shows what the control already is.

```tsx
<Field label="Name" hint="Required"><Input required /></Field>
<Field label="Plan"><Input defaultValue="Pro" disabled /></Field>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | REQUIRED. This is the accessible NAME of the control, and nothing else is. Clicking it focuses the control — Field wires htmlFor to the id it gives the child, so there is no id to keep in sync. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | — | Help text beside the label. Announced as DESCRIPTION via aria-describedby — it is deliberately outside the name, so a screen reader says "E-mail" and not "E-mail we use it to sign you in". |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | — | Shown below the control when the value is rejected, and joined to hint in the description. Also sets aria-invalid on the control: a red border alone says nothing to a colour-blind or blind user. |
| `id` | `string` | auto | The id of the CONTROL, not of the wrapper — it is what htmlFor points at. Omit it and Field generates one. An id already declared on the child wins over this. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The control. Field owns the name for a single child that does not name itself: Input, Select, Textarea, Range, Combobox, MultiCombobox. Pass a control that carries its own label, aria-label or aria-labelledby (including Switch, Checkbox and Radio), or several children, and Field becomes a named group instead — see a11y.apg. Controls with a label of their own and their own layout (NumberField, OTPField, SegmentedControl, Toggle) are not Field children. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Ties this field to a key in the Form's errors. With it, the child becomes the form's control and receives aria-invalid plus the message id; without it, Field behaves exactly as it did before — the addition is deliberately additive, because this component's semantics were paid for with an audit (AUD-0001) and are not touched to add a feature. |
| `orientation` | `Responsive<FieldOrientation>` | vertical | Label to the left of the control instead of above it — the settings-form row. It is a GRID and not a flex row on purpose: in a row the error message would become a third column beside the control, and it talks about the VALUE, so it has to fall under the control. |
| `labelWidth` | `"auto" \| string` | — | Width of the label column when orientation is horizontal. "auto" sizes it to the label; any CSS length fixes it. Without it the column is the --field-label-width token (12rem), which on a 375px phone leaves a Combobox no room for its value. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | Help text that needs a sentence: it sits under the control and does not share the label's line. `hint` stays a short note beside the label. It is the reference library's Description and the `description` Checkbox already has. Joins aria-describedby in screen order: hint, description, error. |
| `required` | `boolean` | false | The red asterisk after the label (hidden from screen readers) and required on the control — which is what announces it. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/fileinput.html">
# FileInput

FileInput collects files by click or by drop, refuses what does not fit before anything is sent, and — when you give it an upload function — runs the real transfer with progress, cancel and retry. The type and size checks run on the DROP too, not only in the picker dialog, which is where most implementations let the wrong file through.

## Usage

```tsx
import {FileInput} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<FileInput label="Attachments" hint="PDF or PNG, up to 5 MB"
  accept=".pdf,.png" maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024} multiple
  onFilesChange={setFiles} />
```

- accept and maxSize are enforced on drop as well as on pick — the dialog filter is not a guarantee.

- A refused file says why, in words: wrong type or over the limit, from the i18n dictionary.

- upload() drives real progress per file, with cancel and retry, and announces the outcome.

- Added and removed files are announced through a live region, so the list is never silent.

- A restored item shows its receipt and offers removal, never a retry button that would fail.

- The previews show the RESTING states; progress, pause and retry only move in a real app.

## Examples

### Real upload

With upload() it owns progress, cancel and retry for each file.

```tsx
<FileInput label="Import" accept=".csv" maxSize={2000000}
  upload={async ({file, onProgress, signal}) => {
    await put(file, {onProgress, signal});
  }} />
```

### A queue that survived the page

initialQueue restores the receipt of what failed — and offers no retry, because a file that came back from storage has no bytes to send.

```tsx
<FileInput
  label="Attachments"
  initialQueue={[
    {id: "f0", name: "contacts.csv", bytes: 84210, status: "error", progress: 0.42},
  ]}
  onQueueChange={save} />
```

### One file only

Without multiple, a new pick replaces the previous file instead of stacking.

```tsx
<FileInput label="Avatar" accept="image/png,image/jpeg" maxSize={512000} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accept` | `string` | — | MIME types or extensions, checked on drop too — not only in the picker dialog. |
| `maxSize` | `number` | — | Limit in bytes. Over it the file is refused with a readable message, not silently. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | false | More than one file per pick. |
| `onFilesChange` | `(files: File[]) => void` | — | Fires with the accepted list, after filtering by type and size. |
| `upload` | `(ctx: UploadContext) => Promise<void>` | — | Real upload with progress, cancel and retry. Without it the component only collects files. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Names the drop zone. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | — | What is accepted, in words, beside the zone. |
| `initialQueue` | `FileQueueItem[]` | — | Restores a queue you persisted earlier — id, name, bytes, status and progress, all plain data. It is INITIAL and not controlled, and the word is literal: a `File` does not come back from storage, so a restored item has the record and not the bytes. It can be shown and removed, never re-sent, and the Retry button is hidden on it rather than offered and broken. An item restored with an ACTIVE status (pending, uploading, paused) is normalised to `canceled`, because without the bytes it is neither uploading nor able to: before 2026-08-12 it showed inert Pause/Resume/Cancel buttons and counted as in-flight, which held the receipt back forever (AUD-0006). Ids you pass are respected and new ids skip them, so `f0` from a restored queue no longer collides with the first file added (AUD-0002). |
| `onQueueChange` | `(queue: FileQueueItem[]) => void` | — | Fires on every change to the queue, in serialisable form. Where you persist it — local storage, a server, nowhere — is yours, the same boundary the grid draws for its URL state. |
| `preview` | `boolean` | false | Shows a thumbnail for image files, in the same slot the document icon occupies — the row does not change height because of it. Only images: generating an object URL for a 40 MB PDF shows nothing. The URL is revoked whenever the item LEAVES the queue — removed, replaced in single mode, or replaced by a name conflict — and any survivor is revoked on unmount. The browser holds the bytes until someone says otherwise, and until 2026-08-12 only the remove path revoked (AUD-0009). |
| `checksum` | `boolean` | false | Computes SHA-256 of each file with the Web Crypto API — no dependency — shows the first eight digits and puts the whole value in the queue. Opt-in and not the default for two measured reasons: `crypto.subtle` only exists in a secure context (https or localhost), and the digest needs the WHOLE file in memory, because Web Crypto has no streaming hash. If your `upload` resolves with `{checksum}`, the two are compared and a mismatch fails the item: bytes that differ are not a detail. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Merged onto the outermost element, after the Aurea skin — your class wins on a tie. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Id of the focusable control, which is what a <label htmlFor> has to point at. Generated when you do not pass one. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/form.html">
# Form

Shows the error and collects the values. It does not decide what an error is.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Form, Field, Input, Button} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Form errors={errors} onSubmit={values => save(values)}>
  <Field label="E-mail" name="email"><Input name="email" type="email" /></Field>
  <Field label="Display name" name="nickname"><Input name="nickname" /></Field>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` | — | Errors you already decided, keyed by the Field's name. AUREA VALIDATES NOTHING: no schema, no rules, no resolver, no field state. Validate wherever it suits you — a schema on the client, a server action, the API's answer — and hand the result over. That is why no form library is a dependency here: marrying one would force every project using Aurea to adopt it, including those that already validate another way. |
| `onSubmit` | `(values) => void` | — | Fires with the collected values, already gathered from the named controls. The native submit is prevented for you. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Fields and the submit button. The form only stacks them with breathing room — arranging beyond that is Stack and Grid's job, not a third way of doing layout. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Added to the <form>. Every other form attribute passes through. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/gallery.html">
# Gallery

A grid of pictures you can pick from, and enlarge in the dialog that already exists.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Gallery} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Gallery
  label="Product photos"
  items={photos}
  selected={chosen}
  onSelect={setChosen}
  zoom
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `Array<{id, src, alt, caption?, kind?, duration?}>` | — | The pictures, as data — the same idiom as Timeline, DataList and Stepper. Each tile renders an <Image>, so the reserved box and the broken-source fallback come with it. `kind: "video"` puts the house Badge on the photo, with `duration` (seconds) as m:ss — the media player's format — and "Video" for screen readers. Without `kind`, it is a photo, as before. |
| `selected` | `string` | — | The id of the chosen item. The gallery keeps no selection of its own: in the MediaLibrary archetype the library, the detail panel and the player share ONE constant, and three parallel strings that happen to agree today is the I1 finding waiting for the first rename. |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | — | Called on click. Without it and without zoom the tiles are not buttons at all — a button that does nothing is a focus stop that lies to anyone on a keyboard. |
| `selectionMode` | `"single" \| "multiple"` | "single" | The reference library's name for it. With "multiple", every tile is a toggle button (aria-pressed) with the same .is-selected mark as everywhere else, clicking marks instead of zooming, and the chosen ids come from selectedIds. |
| `selectedIds` | `string[]` | — | The chosen tiles when selectionMode is "multiple". The gallery keeps no choice of its own, as with `selected`. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(ids: string[]) => void` | — | The new list after a tile is toggled, in the order they were chosen. The same name as DataGrid. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` | false | There is more after the last tile. A row after the grid (the measure of the reference library's load-more table row) is watched, and calls onReachEnd when it enters the screen. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | false | A part is on its way: the row shows the Spinner, the list is aria-busy, and onReachEnd is not called again until it ends. |
| `onReachEnd` | `() => void` | — | Called when the end row is on screen and nothing is loading. If the new part does not fill the screen, it is called again. |
| `zoom` | `boolean` | false | Clicking also enlarges the picture in the Dialog this library already has — focus trap, Escape and backdrop included. No second floating surface is born for this. |
| `ratio` | `string` | 1/1 | Aspect ratio of every tile, passed straight to Image. Square by default because a grid of mixed ratios is a ragged grid. |
| `label` | `string` | Gallery | Accessible name of the list. Name it for what it holds — two unnamed galleries on a page announce the same thing twice. |
| `--gallery-min` | `CSS custom property` | 8rem | Minimum tile width. The grid fills with as many columns as fit, so the container decides the count, not a prop. Same escape valve as --carousel-slide. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/grid.html">
# Grid

Two-dimensional layout primitive.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Grid} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Card>Two</Card>
  <Card>Three</Card>
</Grid>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Responsive columns with no breakpoints: each one is at least --grid-min wide (15rem by default) and they fill the row, with --space-4 between them. |
| `gap` | `"tight" \| "normal" \| "loose"` | "normal" | Three steps and no others (ADR-0051): tight is --space-2, normal is --space-4, loose is --space-6. The old rule still holds against ANY spacing; these two extra steps exist for the two measured cases — a note under its value, and a grid of filters. |
| `min` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| string` | "md" | The minimum column width. By name: xs 8rem, sm 12rem, md 15rem (the default) or lg 20rem — each a number the system already uses (the Gallery tile, the health matrix cell, the Grid default, the xs dialog). Or as a CSS length ("10rem", "155px"), the --grid-min the CSS reads. |
| `columns` | `number` | — | A fixed number of equal columns. With it, `min` stops applying. With 12, Grid.Item's `span` gives the 7-of-12 layout of a website page. |
| `Grid.Item span` | `Responsive<"1" \| … \| "12">` | — | Grid.Item is a grid child that knows how many columns it takes. Responsive and mobile-first: span={{base: "12", viewport: {md: "7"}}} takes the whole row on a narrow screen and 7 of 12 from md up. By container too ({base, container: {sm: …}}). Without span, one column, like any grid child. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Where you set --grid-min for a denser or a wider grid. That variable is the adjustment knob, the same idea as --qr-size on QRCode: a column count as a prop would freeze a number that the container is the one who knows. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/header.html">
# Header

The top bar of an app or a website — also called header, navbar or top bar. Brand, the site's links with the current page marked, actions, and on a phone a menu button that drops the links below the bar.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Header} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Header
  variant="flush"
  divider
  maxWidth="xl"
  brand={<strong>Acme</strong>}
  items={[
    {id: "home", label: "Home", href: "/"},
    {id: "pricing", label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing"},
    {id: "docs", label: "Docs", href: "/docs"},
  ]}
  current="pricing"
  actions={<Button variant="primary" size="sm">Sign up</Button>}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `floating \| flush \| pill` | floating | The skin. floating is a detached card; flush merges into the background so the bar frames the window; pill is a centred capsule for a site header — not for a shell, because search plus density plus theme plus command do not fit in a capsule. |
| `brand` | `ReactNode` | — | The lockup. It lives here and not in the sidebar: the top crosses the full width and the side panel starts below it. Inside a shell this is also where the drawer toggle sits, injected before what you pass. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Everything beside the brand: sections, search, actions, account. Presentational — the bar never decides what collapses. It wraps by content, so text at 200% breaks it to a second line instead of overflowing; hide what is secondary with hide-below-md/lg. |
| `divider` | `boolean` | false | Only on `flush`: a hairline under the bar. flush has the page's background and sticks to the top, so without a line the content scrolls under it with nothing saying where the bar ends. |
| `items` | `SidebarItem[]` | — | The website's links — the same list the Sidebar and the BottomNav take, so the app keeps one menu. Uses id, label, href and render (the router link); sub-items, icon and onClick are ignored: the bar is flat. Below 768px they leave the bar and drop into the menu panel. |
| `current` | `string` | — | The id of the current page's item: it gets aria-current="page", the highlight colour and the medium weight, in the bar and in the menu panel. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | — | What sits on the right: search, a call to action, the account. It stays in the bar on a phone too. |
| `maxWidth` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "2xl" \| "docs" \| "full"` | — | How far the bar's content grows, on the Container's scale, so the bar lines up with the page below it. Without it, the bar keeps its own padding. docs is the documentation block, 1400 (--docs-width), with 24 of padding from 768 up. |
| `itemsJustify` | `"start" \| "end"` | "end" | Where the links sit: end (just before the actions, at the other end from the brand) or start (right after the brand, with the actions at the other end — the reference's home page). |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` | "md" | The bar's height: md is 64 (the reference's bar guide), sm is 56 (the reference's home page), with 6 between the actions instead of 8. |
| `blurred` | `boolean` | false | Only on flush: a transparent background that blurs what scrolls under it, as the reference's home page. With reduced transparency asked by the system, or a browser without backdrop blur, the background is solid. |
| `menuActions` | `ReactNode` | — | What only the phone menu carries, under the links (the GitHub link, the account). Not shown in the wide bar. |
| `navLabel` | `string` | "Main" | The navigation's name for screen readers. Pass it in the page's language. |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | "Menu" | The phone menu button's name for screen readers. Pass it in the page's language. In an app with client-side routing the panel does not close by itself on a page change: give the Header a key that changes with the route. |
| `menuId` | `string` | "aurea-header-menu" | The id of the phone menu panel, which the button points at with popovertarget. Change it only when a page has two website headers: each one needs its own. |
| `tabs` | `HeaderTab[]` | — | A second row: the site's areas, each with an optional icon, like the area row of the reference documentation. The row is 40 tall, the areas sit at its bottom, 12 apart (4 on a phone), and it scrolls sideways when they do not fit. The current one gets aria-current="page" and a 2px bar in the accent color. It comes last in the Tab order, after the actions. With tabs the bar is exactly its height and the divider line hangs just below it. |
| `currentTab` | `string` | — | The id of the current area in the second row. |
| `tabsLabel` | `string` | "Sections" | The accessible name of the second row. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/heading.html">
# Heading

A heading, h1 to h6. The level picks both the element and the size, as in the reference library.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Heading} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Heading level={2}>This month</Heading>
<Heading level={3}>By team</Heading>
<Heading level={4}>Analyst</Heading>
<Heading level={5}>Notes</Heading>
<Heading level={6}>Footnote</Heading>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | 1 | The heading level: it renders h1…h6 and takes that role's size (4xl down to base, semibold, tight leading). There is no separate size prop, as in the reference library — the level is the design. |
| `color` | `"default" \| "muted"` | "default" | Two colours only, like the reference library: the text colour or the muted one. A closed list protects contrast — both pass AA on every Aurea surface. |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "muted" \| "subtle" \| "primary" \| "link" \| "danger" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "info"` | — | The text colour with the native package's name — the same names on web and native. link is the yellow made for text, readable on both themes; primary is the fill yellow and nearly disappears on the light theme. The state colours are the -400 pair. It wins over color when both are given. |
| `weight` | `"normal" \| "medium" \| "semibold" \| "bold" \| "extrabold"` | — (the role's own) | Overrides the weight of the role. Headings are semibold and body text is regular by default. "extrabold" (800, --weight-extrabold) is for a cover title; the default title weight is still semibold. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "justify"` | — (inherited) | Text alignment. start and end follow the writing direction, so the same value mirrors in RTL. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | false | One line, cut with an ellipsis. Turns the element into a block so the cut has a width to measure against. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The text. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | false | Tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) — for numbers that line up in a column (price, year, spec sheet) or change on screen. Off by default: in running text the narrow "1" is right. Native: the same prop sets fontVariant ["tabular-nums"]. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/healthmatrix.html">
# HealthMatrix

What is up, in a grid.

## Usage

```tsx
import {HealthMatrix} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<HealthMatrix entries={[
  {id: "1", name: "API", state: "operational"},
  {id: "2", name: "Workers", state: "degraded"},
]} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entries` | `HealthEntry[]` | — | Five states, the standard status-page vocabulary measured from the reference: operational, degraded, down, maintenance, unknown. Each cell carries a Status, so the state is a word and not only a colour. |
| `label` | `string` | "Health" | Accessible name of the grid. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the grid. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/hovercard.html">
# HoverCard

Rich preview that opens when the pointer rests on a link, and whose content can be reached.

## Usage

```tsx
import {HoverCard} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<HoverCard trigger={<Button variant="link" href="#curator">Curator</Button>}>
  <strong>Curator</strong>
  <p className="muted">Reviews and files what comes in.</p>
</HoverCard>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `ReactElement` | none | REQUIRED. The element the pointer rests on, usually a link or a name. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | The preview. Never put anything essential here: pointer rest is not available to keyboard-only or touch users. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | "bottom" | Preferred side. The engine flips it when there is no room. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/humanapproval.html">
# HumanApproval

The gate: what is about to happen, and a person's decision.

## Usage

```tsx
import {HumanApproval} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<HumanApproval
  title="Delete 12 archived records"
  risk="high"
  details={[{term: "Table", value: "invoices"}, {term: "Rows", value: "12"}]}
  onApprove={() => {}}
  onDeny={() => {}}
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | What is being asked for. Names the region for a screen reader when it is a string. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | — | What will happen if this is approved, in plain words. |
| `details` | `Array<{ term: string; value: ReactNode }>` | — | The exact parameters, as a DataList and not as prose: whoever approves needs to read what will actually run, and a paragraph hides a file path in the middle of a sentence. |
| `risk` | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high"` | — | Three steps, measured from the reference. |
| `reasoning` | `ReactNode` | — | Why the agent wants this. |
| `deadline` | `ReactNode` | — | When the decision is due. Shown as text — expiry is yours to enforce, because only you know what happens when it lapses. |
| `decision` | `"approved" \| "denied"` | — | Once decided, the pair of buttons becomes the RESULT instead of disappearing. Disappearing erases the trace of what the person chose, and that is the difference between a record and a tidy screen. |
| `onApprove` | `() => void` | — | Fires on approve. |
| `onDeny` | `() => void` | — | Fires on deny. Deny comes FIRST in reading and tab order: the destructive action should not be the first to take focus nor the easiest to hit without reading. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the region. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/icon.html">
# Icon

Icon primitive rendered from a sprite.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Icon} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Icon name="magnifying-glass" />
<Icon name="plus" size="lg" />
<Icon name="check" size="xl" />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `IconName \| AureaIconComponent` | — | The glyph id, resolved against the sprite as #i-<name>. A name with no glyph renders nothing visible and throws nothing — check it against the catalogue. It also takes the app's OWN drawing — a component that returns its <svg> and receives the Aurea class and size, inheriting the colour (currentColor) — for a glyph the set does not have, or the app's logo, with no sprite of its own. A drawing has no fill weight. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg \| xl` | md | Token scale. It follows the text it sits next to. |
| `spriteUrl` | `string` | — | LOCAL override of where the glyphs come from. The normal way is to set it once on AureaProvider; this is for the rare page carrying two sprites. |
| `weight` | `"regular" \| "fill" \| "bold"` | "regular" | fill draws the filled shape of the glyph — the one the selected item uses (ADR-0053). bold draws the thick stroke, only for the glyphs drawn in it (today, x — the CloseButton's); the others stay regular. An app's own glyph stays regular. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/iconbutton.html">
# IconButton

IconButton is a Button whose whole label is a glyph. The `label` prop is required and becomes the accessible name — an icon carries no text, so without it the control is mute to a screen reader. That requirement is the reason this component exists instead of a Button you happen to fill with an Icon.

## Usage

```tsx
import {IconButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<IconButton icon="pencil-simple" label="Edit" />
<IconButton icon="copy" label="Duplicate" variant="outline" />
<IconButton icon="gear" label="Settings" variant="secondary" />
<IconButton icon="trash" label="Delete" variant="danger-ghost" />
```

- label is required, not optional: the API refuses to let you ship a nameless control.

- Square target — the width follows the same density token as the height, at every size.

- Softly squared, not pill: a round-ended square would read as a dot next to a text button.

- Every Button variant and state applies, including loading, href and pressed.

- Pair it with Tooltip when the glyph alone is not obvious; the tooltip repeats the label.

## Examples

### Sizes

Five square targets. The glyph keeps its own scale; the box grows with the density token.

```tsx
<IconButton icon="plus" label="Add" size="xs" />
<IconButton icon="plus" label="Add" size="sm" />
<IconButton icon="plus" label="Add" />
<IconButton icon="plus" label="Add" size="lg" />
<IconButton icon="plus" label="Add" size="xl" />
```

### With tooltip

When the glyph is not self-evident, the tooltip says the same words as the label — never different ones. The preview shows the trigger: the balloon lives in a portal and only appears on hover, in a real app.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Duplicate">
  <IconButton icon="copy" label="Duplicate" />
</Tooltip>
```

### Toggle

aria-pressed works here too: a pinned view, a muted channel, a starred row.

```tsx
<IconButton icon="star" label="Star" pressed />
<IconButton icon="push-pin" label="Pin" pressed={false} />
```

### Loading and disabled

Busy replaces the glyph with the spinner and sets aria-busy; disabled keeps the target in place.

```tsx
<IconButton icon="floppy-disk" label="Save" loading />
<IconButton icon="floppy-disk" label="Save" disabled />
```

### Row of actions

Grouped, they get one accessible name for the set — the classic end of a table row.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup label="Row actions">
  <IconButton icon="eye" label="Open" />
  <IconButton icon="pencil-simple" label="Edit" />
  <IconButton icon="trash" label="Delete" variant="danger-ghost" />
</ButtonGroup>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | REQUIRED. Becomes aria-label: an icon with no text has no accessible name without it. |
| `icon` | `AureaIcon` | — | Glyph, from the contract's allowlist — or the app's own drawing (a component that returns its <svg>), as Icon and the native IconButton take. |
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant \| danger-soft` | ghost | Same variants as Button. Ghost by default, so a row of them stays quiet. `secondary` is the neutral fill with the brand-coloured label; `tertiary` the neutral fill with the plain label (the default). |
| `appearance` | `solid \| outline \| ghost \| link \| nav \| soft` | ghost | Inherited from Button. How much weight the box carries; the default here is ghost. |
| `tone` | `neutral \| brand \| danger \| success \| warning \| info` | neutral | Inherited from Button. What the colour means; every combination exists. |
| `size` | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg \| xl` | md | Square target: the width follows the same density token as the height. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | false | Spinner in place of the glyph, aria-busy set, interaction blocked. |
| `href` | `string` | — | Renders an anchor with the same skin, like Button. |
| `leadingIcon` | `AureaIcon` | — | A second glyph before the main one. Rare on an icon button, and it is here because the type is shared with Button. |
| `trailingIcon` | `AureaIcon` | — | A glyph after the main one — a chevron on a button that opens a menu, for instance. |
| `kbd` | `string \| string[]` | — | Shows the shortcut inside the button AND announces it with aria-keyshortcuts. Showing it without announcing would be decoration. A list (["Ctrl", "K"]) shows one key cap per key and announces the combination (Control+K). |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | false | Fills the width of the container instead of hugging the glyph. |
| `grow` | `boolean` | false | In a row (Cluster), takes an equal share with the other buttons that also grow. `fullWidth` asks for the whole line instead. |
| `target` | `HTMLAttributeAnchorTarget` | — | Link attribute, only with `href`. |
| `rel` | `string` | — | Link attribute, only with `href`. |
| `download` | `boolean \| string` | — | Link attribute, only with `href`. |
| `render` | `ReactElement` | — | The element drawn instead of the <button>/<a> — your router's link, e.g. render={<Link href="/reports" />}. It receives the button's skin, content (icons, label, shortcut) and attributes; the destination is its own. Disabled or loading, its click is blocked too, like the disabled link. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | — | Deprecated, removed in 1.0: paints and announces aria-pressed while YOU keep the state. Use Toggle, which keeps the state and demands an accessible name when it is icon-only. |
| `share` | `{ url?: string; title?: string; text?: string }` | — | The button shares. It asks the browser whether it can share this link (navigator.canShare) — detecting the capability, not guessing the device. If it can (phones; Chrome, Edge and Safari on desktop), the device's share sheet opens, and cancelling is not an error. If it cannot, it copies the link and shows "Link copied" anchored to the button, at the button's size. If the copy fails, it says so and shows the link selected. The notice speaks to the screen reader. Without url, it is the page's address. Needs the AureaProvider (or aurea.js on the page) to give the notice; it emits [data-aurea-share], which aurea.js also reads. Only on a <button> (ignored with href or render). On native, the same name opens the system share sheet. |
| `quiet` | `boolean` | false | Less weight: muted text one step smaller — the Button's quiet. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/image.html">
# Image

An image that reserves its box before the bytes arrive, and falls back when they never do.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Image} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Image src="/photo.jpg" alt="The product, from the front" ratio="16/9" />
<Image src="/photo.jpg" alt="The same photo, uncropped" ratio="1/1" fit="contain" />
<Image src="/home.png" srcDark="/home-dark.png" alt="The app's home screen" frame="phone" />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string` | — | The image. Every <img> attribute is forwarded, srcset and sizes included — the point of this component is not to wrap them, it is to reserve the box around them. |
| `alt` | `string` | — | Accessible name. It survives the broken state: the fallback box keeps role="img" with this text, which is what the browser's broken-image glyph throws away. |
| `ratio` | `string` | auto | CSS aspect-ratio, as text: "16/9", "1/1", "4/5". This is the layout-shift fix — without a reserved box the image measures zero until it loads and the page jumps. Leave it off when you pass width and height, because then the browser already knows the intrinsic ratio. |
| `fit` | `cover \| contain` | cover | cover fills the reserved box and crops; contain shows the whole picture inside it and drops the background, which is what an enlarged photo wants. |
| `render` | `ReactElement` | — | Swap the <img> for someone else's — typically the framework's own optimised Image. Ours keeps the skin and the reserved box; theirs keeps the CDN, the srcset generation and the loader. Same render prop the engine uses elsewhere in this library. |
| `loading` | `lazy \| eager` | lazy | Defaulted, not forced. An image above the fold should be eager — a lazy hero delays the largest paint. |
| `frame` | `"phone"` | — | The capture inside a phone frame — GENERIC on purpose, with no island, notch or buttons: a manufacturer's marketing rules forbid simulating its device, and the Aurea carries no third-party marks. The frame follows the theme (card surface, border, medium shadow) and has the sheet's corner (--radius-sheet); the inner corner follows it. With a frame, className and style go to the FRAME (size and placement); ratio (default 9/19.5) goes to the capture. |
| `srcDark` | `string` | — | The capture for the dark theme. A page under data-theme="dark" shows this one; otherwise, src. The hidden one is display:none, out of the accessibility tree, and lazy, so the browser does not fetch it. On native the same prop is sourceDark (the native Image takes source). |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/input.html">
# Input

Input is the control and nothing else: one line of value, in a pill. It adds no state, and every native attribute passes through — type, required, pattern, autoComplete and inputMode behave exactly as the platform behaves. One exception, and it is deliberate: `size` is the system step (sm/md/lg), not the HTML character count. Width is CSS. The label, the hint and the error belong to Field.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Input} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<Card>
  <Field label="Project name"><Input variant="secondary" placeholder="Aurea" /></Field>
</Card>
```

- Native attributes pass through: type, required, pattern, min, max, step, autoComplete, inputMode.

- `size` is ours, not the HTML attribute: sm, md, lg — the same steps as Button.

- type="date", "time", "color" and "file" use the browser's own widget — themed by tokens, not rebuilt.

- No internal state: controlled or uncontrolled is your call, as in plain React.

- The focus ring is the system's, and it never relies on colour alone.

- Pair with Field for the label; alone it is a control with no name, which is a bug.

## Examples

### Sizes

Three steps, and they are the SAME steps as the button: a sm field and a sm button on one row measure the same, in all three densities. md is the default and needs no prop.

```tsx
<Input size="sm" placeholder="Small" />
<Input placeholder="Medium (default)" />
<Input size="lg" placeholder="Large" />
```

### Text

The plain case. The placeholder is an example of the value, never a stand-in for the label.

```tsx
<Field label="Full name"><Input placeholder="Ada Lovelace" /></Field>
```

### Types

Email, password and number, all native — the keyboard on a phone changes with the type.

```tsx
<Input type="email" autoComplete="email" />
<Input type="password" autoComplete="current-password" />
<Input type="number" min={1} max={99} />
```

### Date and time

The browser's own picker, wearing our tokens. Rebuilding a calendar would mean rebuilding every locale with it.

```tsx
<Field label="Starts"><Input type="date" /></Field>
<Field label="At"><Input type="time" /></Field>
```

### Formatting a plate or a document

formatOnBlur normalises the value after focus leaves — it never masks while you type. A live mask makes the screen reader announce what was typed while the field shows something else; the US federal design system ships its input mask with a recorded WCAG 2.1 AA failure, and one of the references dropped masked date fields for the same reason. Type and paste freely; the formatted text becomes the field's own value, so there is nothing painted over it and nothing hidden from a form.

```tsx
const plate = v => {
  const raw = v.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, "");
  return raw.length > 3 ? `${raw.slice(0, 3)}-${raw.slice(3, 7)}` : raw;
};

<Field label="Plate" hint="Type it however you like — it tidies up when you leave">
  <Input formatOnBlur={plate} defaultValue="ABC-1D23" />
</Field>
```

### Disabled and read-only

Disabled is not submitted and is skipped by the keyboard; read-only is submitted and still reachable.

```tsx
<Input defaultValue="Pro" disabled />
<Input defaultValue="acme-42" readOnly />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | text | Native type. date, time, color and file use the browser's own widget, themed by tokens. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string \| number` | — | Controlled or uncontrolled, as in plain React. The component adds no state of its own. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | An example of the value, never a substitute for the label. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | Native disabled: skipped by the keyboard and not submitted. |
| `formatOnBlur` | `(value: string) => string` | — | Normalises the value AFTER focus leaves the field — a licence plate, a document number, a phone. It deliberately does not mask while you type: another design system ships its input mask with a recorded WCAG 2.1 AA failure, one of the references dropped masked date fields because the text leaks between sections, and a live mask makes the screen reader announce what was typed while the field shows something else. Aurea supplies the moment; the format stays yours, because plates and documents are country rules. The formatted text becomes the element's own value — nothing is painted over it — and your onChange is called with it, so controlled fields work. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra classes on the field. Every native attribute of the element passes through: name, required, autoComplete, pattern, min/max, and the rest. |
| `size` | `Responsive<FieldSize>` | md | The system's size step (sm/md/lg), NOT the HTML size attribute — that one is a width in characters and it is deliberately shadowed here, because two meanings for one prop name is worse than losing the native one. |
| `variant` | `primary \| secondary` | primary | secondary is the neutral fill with no visible border, for a field inside a card. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/inputgroup.html">
# InputGroup

The box that looks like a field and holds the control plus whatever is glued to it.

## Usage

```tsx
import {InputGroup} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon>
  <Input placeholder="acme.dev" />
</InputGroup>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | `string` | — | Takes the group out of 100%: "20rem" for a measure, "auto" for the content size. With it the group also stops growing in a row. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/inputgroupaddon.html">
# InputGroupAddon

What sits glued to the control inside an InputGroup: a glyph, a prefix, a button.

## Usage

```tsx
import {InputGroupAddon} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<InputGroupAddon side="start" layout="inline"><Icon name="magnifying-glass" /></InputGroupAddon>
<InputGroupAddon side="end" layout="inline">.00</InputGroupAddon>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | `AddonSide` | start | Which end of the group the addon is glued to. It is LOGICAL, not physical: in RTL "start" is the right-hand side. |
| `layout` | `Responsive<AddonLayout>` | inline | "block" puts the addon on its own line above or below the control instead of beside it — the shape a filter bar takes when it runs out of width. Responsive, so it can be inline on a wide screen and block on a narrow one. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/interagentmessage.html">
# InterAgentMessage

A message from one agent to another, where the direction is the data.

## Usage

```tsx
import {InterAgentMessage} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<InterAgentMessage messages={[
  {id: "1", from: "Curator", to: "Writer", kind: "handoff",
   body: "Draft ready for review.", time: "10:02"},
  {id: "2", from: "Orchestrator", kind: "broadcast",
   body: "Rate limit reached, pausing.", time: "10:04"},
]} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `AgentMessage[]` | — | Each entry carries from, to, body and an optional kind. Not MessageList: that one is a conversation with a person; here the handoff between two agents is what you are reading, and a list with two authors cannot say who delivered what to whom. |
| `label` | `string` | "Agent messages" | Accessible name of the list. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the list. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/invocationpanel.html">
# InvocationPanel

One execution: what was asked, the steps, what came out.

## Usage

```tsx
import {InvocationPanel} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<InvocationPanel
  title="Summarise the changelog"
  input="Summarise the last 20 entries."
  steps={[{id: "1", label: "read", detail: "20 entries", state: "done"}]}
  output="Three themes: performance, a11y, packaging."
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | Names the panel, and names the region for a screen reader when it is a string. |
| `input` | `ReactNode` | — | What was asked. Yours to format — a prompt, a form, a payload. |
| `steps` | `InvocationStep[]` | — | What happened in between. A step with `content` becomes a native <details>: folding is platform behaviour, with keyboard and ARIA already in it, where the reference spends a library Collapsible to arrive at the same place. |
| `output` | `ReactNode` | — | What came out. |
| `running` | `boolean` | false | Marks `aria-busy` on the whole region. The reference animates the label with a shimmer instead — decoration a screen reader cannot reach and that reduced-motion would have to undo. |
| `className` | `string` | — | On the panel. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/kbd.html">
# Kbd

A keyboard key or shortcut, shown as the user would press it. Renders the <kbd> element.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Kbd} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
Press <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> <Kbd>K</Kbd> to search.
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The key or combination, written the way the platform writes it (⌘K, Ctrl+K). |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra classes. Inside a Button it inherits the button's colour automatically. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/kpi.html">
# KPI

Single headline metric with optional delta.

## Usage

```tsx
import {KPI} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<KPI label="Revenue" value="$48.2k" trend="+12% vs last month" />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | What is being measured. Sits above the number, in muted text. |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | — | The number itself, already formatted — the component does not format. |
| `trend` | `ReactNode` | — | The change, as a node and not a number: the sign, the unit and the wording belong to the domain, not to a card. |
| `direction` | `up \| down \| flat` | — | Where the number went. Draws the arrow (trend-up, trend-down, minus), colours the trend and puts a word in front of it for screen readers — so the direction never depends on colour alone. |
| `tone` | `success \| danger \| neutral` | from direction | The colour of the trend. By default up is success, down is danger and flat is neutral; set it when going up is bad (cost, errors). Without direction it paints nothing: colour never travels alone. |
| `directionLabel` | `string` | Up / Down / No change | The word a screen reader hears before the trend. English by default, like every built-in label of the web package; pass it in the language of the page. |
| `variant` | `card \| plain` | card | `plain` drops the card: the number sits inside a card that already exists, instead of a box inside a box. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/label.html">
# Label

The field label on its own, for when you are not using Field.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="workspace">Workspace</Label>

```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `htmlFor` | `string` | — | The id of the control this labels. Without it the label names nothing — use Field when you want that wiring done for you. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/link.html">
# Link

Link is a text link: medium weight in the link colour, with no underline until the pointer rests on it. external opens in a new tab and shows the arrow; disabled does not navigate.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Link} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<p>Read the <Link href="/terms">terms of use</Link> before you sign.</p>
<Link href="/pricing">See the plans</Link>
```

- A real <a href> — the browser opens it in a new tab, copies it, and a search engine follows it.

- The underline appears on hover and while pressed, 4 below the text.

- external sets target="_blank" with rel="noopener noreferrer" and draws the arrow.

- disabled renders without href and with aria-disabled.

- It wraps inside a paragraph, which a page zoomed to 200% needs.

## Examples

### External and disabled

The arrow says it leaves the site; the disabled one does not go anywhere.

```tsx
<Link href="https://example.com" external>Documentation</Link>
<Link href="/export" disabled>Export (no permission)</Link>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | — | Where it goes. |
| `external` | `boolean` | false | Opens in a new tab (target="_blank", rel="noopener noreferrer") and shows the reference library's arrow, drawn by CSS mask. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | false | Does not navigate: rendered without href and with aria-disabled. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The link text. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Added to the <a>. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/listbox.html">
# ListBox

ListBox is a standalone list of options: icons, descriptions and sections, with none, one or many chosen. With no selection it is a list of actions. It is the list a Select opens, without the trigger around it.

## Usage

```tsx
import {ListBox} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<ListBox label="Plan" defaultValue={["pro"]} items={[
  {id: "free", label: "Free", description: "For trying it out", icon: "leaf"},
  {id: "pro", label: "Pro", description: "For a small team", icon: "rocket-launch"},
  {id: "team", label: "Team", description: "For the whole company", icon: "buildings"},
]} />
```

- One tab stop. Arrows, Home and End move; Space and Enter choose; a letter jumps to the next option starting with it.

- selectionMode: single (the default), multiple (Space toggles) or none (onAction).

- Sections are groups named by their title. Disabled options are skipped by the arrows.

- The chosen option shows a check at the end; a danger option is written in the danger colour.

## Examples

### Sections, many chosen

Space toggles each option. A disabled one keeps its place.

```tsx
<ListBox label="Columns" selectionMode="multiple" defaultValue={["name", "status"]} items={[
  {title: "Basic", items: [{id: "name", label: "Name"}, {id: "status", label: "Status"}]},
  {title: "Dates", items: [{id: "created", label: "Created"}, {id: "due", label: "Due", disabled: true}]},
]} />
```

### Actions

With no selection, an option is an action. The dangerous one says so in colour and in words.

```tsx
<ListBox label="File" selectionMode="none" onAction={run} items={[
  {id: "rename", label: "Rename", icon: "pencil-simple"},
  {id: "share", label: "Share", icon: "share-network"},
  {id: "delete", label: "Delete file", icon: "trash", danger: true},
]} />
```

### Sections, descriptions and shortcuts

Each item with a line under its name and the key that fires it at the end, and a line between the sections, as in every sectioned list of the reference.

```tsx
<ListBox label="File actions" selectionMode="none" items={[
  {title: "Actions", items: [
    {id: "new", label: "New file", description: "Create a new file", icon: "plus-square", kbd: "⌘N"},
    {id: "edit", label: "Edit file", description: "Make changes", icon: "pencil-simple", kbd: "⌘E"}]},
  {title: "Danger zone", items: [
    {id: "delete", label: "Delete file", description: "Move to trash", icon: "trash", kbd: "⌘⇧D", danger: true}]},
]} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | REQUIRED. The list's name for screen readers. |
| `items` | `(ListBoxItem \| ListBoxSection)[]` | — | Options ({id, label, description?, icon?, disabled?, danger?, textValue?, kbd?}) and sections ({title, items}). kbd shows the item's shortcut at the end of the row, as the reference — display only; the app binds the key. |
| `selectionMode` | `none \| single \| multiple` | single | none turns it into a list of actions (onAction). |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string[]` | — | The ids of the chosen options. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` | — | Called with the new list of ids. |
| `onAction` | `(id: string) => void` | — | Called when an option is activated (Enter, Space or click). |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/logstream.html">
# LogStream

Live-appending stream of log lines.

## Usage

```tsx
import {LogStream} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<LogStream lines={[
  {time: "09:14:02", text: "build started"},
  {time: "09:14:07", level: "warn", text: "2 baselines missing for linux"},
  {time: "09:14:09", level: "error", text: "exit 1"},
]} />
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lines` | `Array<{time?: string; level?: string; text: string}>` | — | The lines. The container is role="log" with aria-live="polite", so lines added after mount are announced as they arrive and the ones already there are not re-read. `level` becomes the .log-<level> class. |
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/mediaembed.html">
# MediaEmbed

A third-party video page (YouTube, Vimeo) inside the Aurea frame, loaded only when asked for.

## Usage

```tsx
import {MediaEmbed} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
<MediaEmbed
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
  title="Official trailer"
  poster="/trailers/cover.jpg"
  href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID"
/>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string` | — | The provider's EMBED address, e.g. https://www.youtube.com/embed/<id>. Any other <iframe> attribute is accepted and forwarded, and wins over the defaults. |
| `title` | `string` | — | Required. The accessible name of the frame — an unnamed iframe fails axe, so the type refuses to compile without it. |
