<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-run-session-panel.html">
# Run session panel

One run, end to end: what state it is in, the turns, the tool it is calling, where it resumes from, the receipt it already owns, and only the actions the run can take right now. The approval gate takes the place of the actions while a person has to decide.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Status, MessageList, InvocationPanel, HumanApproval, DataList, Toolbar, ToolbarButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the RUN, so it comes from the run's own state
// machine — never from a list written next to the buttons, where it drifts unseen.
const actions = allowedFrom(run.state);   // e.g. running -> ["interrupt", "cancel"]

<div className="stack">
  <div role="group" aria-label="Run" className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
    <strong>{run.id}</strong>
    {/* the three "waiting" states are universal (ADR-0018): pass the state and the
        sentence comes from the vocabulary. The other six carry their own label. */}
    {run.state.startsWith("waiting_")
      ? <Status state={run.state} />
      : <Status variant={tone[run.state]}>{label[run.state]}</Status>}
  </div>

  <MessageList label="Turns" messages={run.turns} />
  <InvocationPanel title="write_file" running={run.state === "running"}
    input={run.tool.input} steps={run.tool.steps} output={run.output} />

  {run.state === "waiting_approval" &&
    <HumanApproval title="Write to the repository" risk="medium"
      details={run.approval.details} onApprove={approve} onDeny={reject} />}

  {/* the receipt exists from the moment the run is accepted, and is never erased */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Checkpoint"><DataList items={run.checkpoint} /></div>
  <div role="group" aria-label="Receipt"><DataList items={run.receipt} /></div>

  {actions.length > 0 &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Actions">
      <Toolbar label="Run actions">
        {actions.map(a => <ToolbarButton key={a} onClick={() => send(a)}>{label[a]}</ToolbarButton>)}
      </Toolbar>
    </div>}
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-review-compare.html">
# Review compare

Nothing changes until someone sees what would change: the difference, the checks that ran on it, the one decision the change can take right now, and the receipt that apply writes and rollback points back to. Additions and deletions are text, so the diff reads the same without colour.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Status, CodeBlock, Alert, Toolbar, ToolbarButton, DataList} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the CHANGE, so it comes from its own state
// machine. ReviewCompare has no separate "actions" region — `decision` is where every
// human action lives — so nothing is filtered out of the derivation.
const actions = allowedFrom(change.state);   // applied -> ["rollback"]

<div className="stack">
  <div role="group" aria-label="Change" className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
    <div><strong>{change.file}</strong><div className="hint">{change.range}</div></div>
    <Status variant={tone[change.state]}>{label[change.state]}</Status>
  </div>

  {/* additions and deletions are TEXT — the +/- of a unified diff — never colour alone */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Comparison">
    <CodeBlock language="diff">{change.diff}</CodeBlock>
    <div className="hint">{added} added, {removed} removed</div>
  </div>

  {/* announced: Alert is role="status", and role="alert" on its own when it is a failure */}
  {change.test &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Test result">
      <Alert variant={change.test.variant}>{change.test.text}</Alert>
    </div>}

  {actions.length > 0 &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Decision">
      <Toolbar label="Review decision">
        {actions.map(a => <ToolbarButton key={a} onClick={() => send(a)}>{label[a]}</ToolbarButton>)}
      </Toolbar>
    </div>}

  {/* apply writes the receipt; rollback points back at it and never erases it */}
  {change.receipt &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Receipt"><DataList items={change.receipt} /></div>}
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-resource-workbench.html">
# Resource workbench

Where resources come from, what is in there, what the selected one is, what is in flight right now, where it all came from, and only the actions this phase allows. The transfer says its phase and its percent in words, so the bar is never the only thing carrying the news.

## Usage

```tsx
import {TreeView, Table, Status, Progress, Alert, DataList, Toolbar, ToolbarButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the TRANSFER, so it comes from its own state
// machine — never from a list written next to the buttons, where it drifts unseen.
const actions = allowedFrom(job.state);   // transferring -> ["pause", "verify"]

<div className="stack">
  {/* tree and list side by side: that is what a workbench IS, and stacking them
      costs the height the other four regions need */}
  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"minmax(140px,1fr) 2fr"}}>
    <TreeView label="Workspace" items={job.tree} defaultExpandedIds={["brand"]} />
    <Table caption="Resources">{...}</Table>
  </div>

  {/* "conflict requires preview": the conflict is explained HERE, next to what arrived,
      because whoever chooses has to see what is about to be overwritten */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Preview">
    <strong>{job.selected.name}</strong>
    <div className="hint">{job.selected.summary}</div>
    {job.state === "conflict" &&
      <Alert variant="warning" title="Name already taken">{job.conflict.existing}</Alert>}
  </div>

  {/* one number feeds BOTH the bar and the sentence — "progress announces percent
      and phase", and a bar on its own is drawing, not announcing */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Transfer queue">
    <div className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
      <span>{job.file.name}</span>
      <span className="hint">{job.phase} · {job.percent}%</span>
    </div>
    <Progress value={job.percent} label={job.phase + " " + job.file.name} />
  </div>

  {/* "restore keeps provenance": it exists from discovery and survives everything,
      so it is not conditional on any state */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Provenance"><DataList items={job.provenance} /></div>

  {actions.length > 0 &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Actions">
      <Toolbar label="Workbench actions">
        {actions.map(a => <ToolbarButton key={a} onClick={() => send(a)}>{label[a]}</ToolbarButton>)}
      </Toolbar>
    </div>}
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-analytics-workbench.html">
# Analytics workbench

The period, the filters, the segments and the export scope on one line; the number, the curve and the same curve as a table below it. The table is not a fallback and not a tab: a chart without its numbers excludes whoever cannot read the chart.

## Usage

```tsx
import {SegmentedControl, Status, Select, Button, KPI, Chart, Table, Alert} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the DATA, so it comes from its own state machine.
// This contract has no "actions" region: seven of its eight actions have no transition,
// because changing the range does not change the STATE — it refetches. The regions ARE
// the controls, and `refresh` lives with the range, which is what owns freshness.
const actions = allowedFrom(view.state);   // ready -> ["refresh"]

<div className="stack" style={{"--chart-h":"8rem"}}>
  <div className="cluster">
    <div role="group" aria-label="Time range">
      <SegmentedControl label="Time range" items={RANGES} value={view.range} onChange={setRange} />
      {/* two of the seven states are UNIVERSAL (ADR-0018): pass the state and the
          sentence comes from the vocabulary, so the tela never invents a second wording */}
      {isUniversal(view.state)
        ? <Status state={view.state} />
        : <Status variant={tone[view.state]}>{label[view.state]}</Status>}
      {actions.map(a => <Button key={a} size="sm" onClick={() => send(a)}>{label[a]}</Button>)}
    </div>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Filters"><Select value={view.filter} …/></div>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Segments"><Select value={view.segment} …/></div>
    {/* "export records scope and freshness": both in the LABEL, because whoever clicks
        needs to know what comes out before it comes out. Keep it SHORT — this row holds four
        control groups on one line, and a label that wraps costs the box 43px of height */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Export">
      <Button>Export {view.rangeLabel} · {view.asOf}</Button>
    </div>
  </div>

  {/* announced by ROLE, never by moving focus — Alert is role="status" on its own */}
  {view.notice && <Alert variant={view.notice.variant}>{view.notice.text}</Alert>}

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"minmax(9rem,1fr) 3fr"}}>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Indicators"><KPI label="Runs" value={view.total} trend={view.trend} /></div>
    {/* the Chart names itself with `label`, so it IS the visualization region */}
    <Chart label="Runs per day">
      <AreaChart data={view.series}>…</AreaChart>
    </Chart>
  </div>

  {/* "visualization always has a tabular alternative" — a sibling region, not a tab.
      A tab panel that is not rendered is an alternative that does not exist. */}
  <Table caption="Runs per day, as numbers">…</Table>

  <div role="group" aria-label="Annotations"><div className="hint">{view.annotations}</div></div>
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-transaction-flow.html">
# Transaction flow

What is being bought, what it adds up to, which saved method pays for it, and — before anything is charged — the consequence in one sentence. Every terminal result leaves an immutable receipt with the idempotency key, so a double click has an answer. A refund points back at that receipt instead of erasing it.

## Usage

```tsx
import {Status, Alert, DataList, Toolbar, ToolbarButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the TRANSACTION, so it comes from its own state
// machine. This contract has no "actions" region, so each action lives in the region it
// affects: refund in `reversal`, cancel and authorize in `review`, next to the sentence
// that says what they will do. Three of the six actions have no transition at all, and
// settle/fail/dispute are transitions without an action — the acquirer settles, the
// network declines, and the cardholder disputes through the issuer. Never this screen.
const actions = allowedFrom(tx.state);   // settled -> ["refund"]

// Money is an INTEGER in minor units: there is still no decimal type in JavaScript
// (TC39 Decimal is stage 1). Sum in integers, divide by 100 only to format.
const total = subtotal + fees.reduce((t, f) => t + f.cents, 0);
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style: "currency", currency, currencyDisplay: "code"});
const show = cents => money.format(cents / 100);

<div className="stack">
  {/* Status says what state it is IN; the Alert announces what just happened —
      Alert is role="status" on its own, and role="alert" when it is a failure */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Status">
    <div className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
      <strong>{tx.id} · {tx.reference}</strong>
      {/* requires_action IS the universal waiting_user (ADR-0018): pass the state and
          the sentence comes from the vocabulary, so there is no second wording */}
      {tx.state === "requires_action"
        ? <Status state="waiting_user" />
        : <Status variant={tone[tx.state]}>{label[tx.state]}</Status>}
    </div>
    {notice && <Alert variant={notice.variant}>{notice.text}</Alert>}
  </div>

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    <div>
      <div role="group" aria-label="Items">
        <DataList items={tx.items.map(i => ({term: i.label, value: show(i.cents)}))} />
      </div>
      {/* the total is SUMMED, never written beside the numbers it sums */}
      <div role="group" aria-label="Amounts">
        <DataList items={[{term:"Subtotal", value: show(subtotal)},
                          ...fees.map(f => ({term: f.label, value: show(f.cents)})),
                          {term:"Total", value: <strong>{show(total)}</strong>}]} />
      </div>
    </div>
    <div>
      {/* the method is a REFERENCE to something the provider holds. No card number, no
          CVV, no expiry: under PCI DSS 4.0.1 those fields belong to the provider's
          iframe or redirect, never to this page */}
      <div role="group" aria-label="Payment"><DataList items={tx.method} /></div>
      {/* immutable receipt on every terminal result, and it carries the idempotency key —
          the only thing that answers "did the double click charge me twice?" */}
      {tx.receipt &&
        <div role="group" aria-label="Receipt"><DataList items={tx.receipt} /></div>}
    </div>
  </div>

  {/* amount, currency, fees and CONSEQUENCE before the commit — the number inside the
      sentence is the same show(total), so the two can never disagree */}
  {!tx.receipt &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Review">
      <div className="hint">{card} will be charged {show(total)} once. Retrying with the
        same Idempotency-Key does not charge twice.</div>
      {review.length > 0 && <Toolbar label="Review decision">…</Toolbar>}
    </div>}

  {/* a reversal never erases: it points back at the original receipt */}
  {(tx.reversal || refund.length > 0) &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Reversal">
      {tx.reversal && <div className="hint">{tx.reversal}</div>}
      {refund.length > 0 && <Toolbar label="Reversal">…</Toolbar>}
    </div>}
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-device-control.html">
# Device control

One device inside its fleet: what it is, what it is reading right now — with the time and the quality of each reading — what a command would reach and what it would do, the calibration with its default and a way back, and who touched it last. Live readings can be paused, and a firmware update asks before it drops the equipment.

## Usage

```tsx
import {HealthMatrix, Status, DataList, Alert, Toolbar, ToolbarButton, Button, Field, Range, HumanApproval} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the DEVICE, so it comes from its own state machine.
// Four of the seven actions have no transition — select, command, confirm, pause_live —
// and that is not a hole in the contract: they change the SCREEN, not the equipment.
// Each one lives in the region it affects.
const actions = allowedFrom(device.state);   // online -> ["update", "calibrate"]

<div className="stack">
  <div className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
    <strong>{device.name}</strong>
    <Status variant={tone[device.state]}>{label[device.state]}</Status>
  </div>

  {/* the fleet is a HealthMatrix: it names itself, so it IS the region */}
  <HealthMatrix label="Fleet" entries={fleet} />

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Device"><DataList items={device.facts} /></div>

    {/* "telemetry timestamp and confidence are visible" — the quality vocabulary is the
        domain's own (OPC UA: Good · Uncertain · Bad), not one we invented. Paused or
        offline, the value is the LAST USABLE one and the clock stops: that is what the
        timestamp is for. */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Telemetry">
      <DataList items={readings.map(r => ({
        term: r.name, value: `${r.value} · ${r.at} · ${r.quality}`}))} />
      {/* "live telemetry can be paused" — and the control says which way it is */}
      <Button onClick={toggleLive}>{paused ? "Resume live" : "Pause live"}</Button>
    </div>
  </div>

  {/* "critical alerts do not rely on sound": Alert danger IS role="alert", and the text
      carries the threshold and the reading. Acknowledge lives here — you acknowledge the
      alarm, not the device. */}
  {device.alert &&
    <div role="group" aria-label="Alerts">
      <Alert variant="danger" title={device.alert.title}>{device.alert.detail}</Alert>
      {actions.includes("acknowledge") && <Toolbar label="Alert actions">…</Toolbar>}
    </div>}

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    {/* "commands show target scope and expected effect" — both as TEXT, before any button */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Commands">
      <div className="hint">Scope: {command.scope}</div>
      <div className="hint">Effect: {command.effect}</div>
      {actions.includes("update") && <Toolbar label="Device commands">…</Toolbar>}
    </div>

    {/* "calibration retains defaults and rollback": the default is written next to the
        current value, and the way back is a button that exists even when the device does not
        answer — whoever mis-calibrated should not have to wait for the equipment */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Calibration">
      <Field label="Head temperature offset (°C)"
        hint={`Now ${cal.current} · default ${cal.default}`}>
        <Range min={-2} max={2} step={0.1} value={cal.value} onChange={setOffset}
          aria-label="Head temperature offset in degrees Celsius" />
      </Field>
      <Button variant="ghost">Revert to default</Button>
    </div>
  </div>

  {/* "unsafe actions require gated confirmation" — the gate takes the place of the action,
      and it carries the scope and the rollback, not just a yes/no */}
  {actions.includes("update") &&
    <HumanApproval title="Update firmware" risk="high" description={command.effect}
      details={[{term:"Scope",value:command.scope},{term:"Rollback",value:"2.4.1 stays on the device"}]} />}

  <div role="group" aria-label="Audit"><div className="hint">{device.audit}</div></div>
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-media-library.html">
# Media library

One selection shared by the gallery, the detail and the player — never three strings that happen to match. The resume position is a number, the optional capabilities say which ones exist, and the queue can be reordered without touching what is playing. The transport lives in the player and nowhere else.

## Usage

```tsx
import {MediaPlayer, Status, DataList, Toolbar, ToolbarButton, EmptyState} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about PLAYBACK, so it comes from its own state machine.
// Six of the nine actions have no transition — seek, queue, playlist, chapter, track,
// favorite — and that is not a hole: choosing a chapter does not change the library's state.
const actions = allowedFrom(view.state);   // ready -> ["play"]

<div className="stack" style={{"--media-h":"6rem", "--media-ar":"auto"}}>
  <div className="cluster" style={{justifyContent:"space-between"}}>
    <strong>{item.title} · {item.meta}</strong>
    {/* offline here IS the universal state (ADR-0018): it is OUR connection that dropped,
        which is the opposite of what the same word means in DeviceControl */}
    {isUniversal(view.state)
      ? <Status state={view.state} />
      : <Status variant={tone[view.state]}>{label[view.state]}</Status>}
  </div>

  {/* "gallery selection works by keyboard": the tiles are BUTTONS. Measured — the core's
      .card-interactive has cursor:pointer and :hover and no focus at all, because a div
      never takes Tab. The skin is the one that exists; the element is what the keyboard
      reaches. aria-current marks the selected one, and the word is in the text too. */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Library" className="cluster">
    {library.map(i =>
      <button key={i.id} type="button" className="card card-interactive"
        aria-current={i.id === selection ? "true" : undefined}
        onClick={() => select(i.id)}>
        <strong>{i.title}</strong>
        <div className="hint">{i.id === selection ? i.meta + " · selected" : i.meta}</div>
      </button>)}
  </div>

  {/* ONE selection feeds the gallery, the detail and the player. Three hand-written strings
      that agree today are one rename away from disagreeing. */}
  <MediaPlayer kind="audio" title={item.title} subtitle={item.subtitle} />

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Item detail">
      <DataList items={[{term:"Duration",value:item.meta},{term:"Resume at",value:item.resumeAt}]} />
    </div>
    {/* optional capabilities: what exists is declared, so nobody goes looking for it */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Chapters"><DataList items={item.chapters} /></div>
  </div>

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    {/* "bulk organize never interrupts playback": none of these is a transport control */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Queue">
      <DataList items={[{term:"Next",value:queue[0].label}]} />
      <Toolbar label="Queue actions">…</Toolbar>
    </div>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Tracks"><DataList items={item.tracks} /></div>
  </div>

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr auto"}}>
    {/* "autoplay never surprises" — said in TEXT, where whoever arrives goes looking */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="History">
      <div className="hint">Last played {h.when}, stopped at {h.at} · autoplay is off</div>
    </div>
    {/* library actions, never transport: the transport is the player's, and two buttons for
        the same thing are two truths about who controls it */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Actions"><Toolbar label="Library actions">…</Toolbar></div>
  </div>
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/block-visual-builder.html">
# Visual builder

A canvas with an ordered outline that says the same thing, so building never requires a mouse: add from the palette, move in the outline, connect in the inspector. Credentials appear as references and never as values. Undo and redo sit beside whatever the state machine actually allows right now.

## Usage

```tsx
import {DependencyGraph, Status, Alert, Button, DataList, Field, Select, Toolbar, ToolbarButton} from "@aurea-uds/react";
```

```tsx
// Which actions exist is a fact about the FLOW, so it comes from its own state machine.
// Seven of the ten actions have no transition — add, connect, configure, move, delete,
// undo, redo — because editing the canvas changes the drawing, not the machine. And the
// reverse happens too: edit and resume are transitions that are NOT in actions, so no
// button offers them.
const actions = allowedFrom(flow.state);   // idle -> ["run"]

<div className="stack">
  {/* the palette adds by BUTTON: in a drag-only palette, whoever cannot drag builds nothing */}
  <div role="group" aria-label="Palette" className="cluster">
    {kinds.map(k => <Button key={k} leadingIcon="plus" onClick={() => add(k)}>{k}</Button>)}
    <Status variant={tone[flow.state]}>{label[flow.state]}</Status>
  </div>

  {/* "validation errors link to nodes": the message names the node, and the node exists */}
  {flow.state === "invalid" && <Alert variant="danger" title="1 problem">{error.text}</Alert>}

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 15rem"}}>
    {/* height is a PROP of the graph (Part H), so no core change was needed here */}
    <DependencyGraph label="Canvas" height="9rem" nodes={nodes} edges={edges}
      selectedId={selected} onSelect={setSelected} />

    {/* "canvas has an equivalent ordered outline" — ONE source feeds both, and the outline is
        where moving happens without dragging: every row has up and down */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Outline">
      <ol>{nodes.map((n, i) =>
        <li key={n.id}>
          <span>{n.label}</span>
          {i > 0 && <Button variant="ghost" aria-label={"Move " + n.label + " up"}>↑</Button>}
          {i < nodes.length - 1 && <Button variant="ghost" aria-label={"Move " + n.label + " down"}>↓</Button>}
        </li>)}</ol>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr"}}>
    {/* the inspector is where CONNECTING happens without dragging: a select of valid targets
        does by keyboard what a dragged edge does by mouse */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Inspector">
      <DataList items={[{term:"Node",value:node.label},{term:"Detail",value:node.detail}]} />
      <Field label="Connect to">
        <Select value={target} onChange={connect} aria-label={"Connect " + node.label + " to"}>…</Select>
      </Field>
    </div>

    {/* "credentials are referenced never exposed" — the value is not here, not even masked:
        a mask is a value with tape on it, and it is still in the DOM */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Variables"><DataList items={variables} /></div>
  </div>

  <div className="grid" style={{gridTemplateColumns:"1fr auto"}}>
    <div role="group" aria-label="Run history"><DataList items={history} /></div>
    {/* "undo redo and versioning cover structural edits" — they exist always, beside whatever
        the transition table permits right now */}
    <div role="group" aria-label="Actions">
      <Toolbar label="Builder actions">
        <ToolbarButton>Undo</ToolbarButton><ToolbarButton>Redo</ToolbarButton>
        {actions.map(a => <ToolbarButton key={a} onClick={() => send(a)}>{label[a]}</ToolbarButton>)}
      </Toolbar>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-35-0.html">
# v0.35.0

A documentation layout for the AppShell, a second row of area tabs in the Header, five docs width tokens, and snapping in the editable DependencyGraph.

This release adds a documentation layout built from existing components: [AppShell](./appshell.html) gets `layout="docs"`, the [Header](./header.html) gets a second row of area tabs, and [Container](./container.html) gets a docs width. In the editable [DependencyGraph](./dependencygraph.html), moved nodes now snap to the grid, to their neighbors and to straight edges. No new components.

## New

- **`AppShell layout="docs"`**: a documentation layout. A 1400px block centered on the screen holds the sidebar (220px), the text column (912px, each block up to 900px) and, from 1280px up, the table of contents (240px at the start of a 268px column, aligned with the right edge of the bar).
- **`AppShell layout="docs"` spacing**: the columns start 16px below the bar and stop 32px above the bottom edge. In the sidebar, items have 16px on both sides and 8px inside each item. The table of contents does not show a scrollbar.
- **`AppShell layout="docs"` on small screens**: below 1024px the sidebar becomes the drawer, and the text sits 24px from the edge.
- **`AppShell` `topbarTabs`, `topbarCurrentTab` and `topbarTabsLabel`**: pass the second row of tabs to the `Header`.
- **`Header` `tabs`, `currentTab` and `tabsLabel`**: a second row in the bar for the areas of a site. Each area has its icon and is 40px tall. The current one gets `aria-current="page"` and a 2px underline in the accent color.
- **`Header` tabs and the keyboard**: the tab row comes last in the Tab order. On phones it scrolls sideways (the page does not), and the focus ring stays inside each area.
- **`Header` tabs and `divider`**: with `tabs`, the bar has an exact height, and the `divider` line sits right below it.
- **`Container size="docs"`**, and `maxWidth="docs"` on `Header` and `Section`: the 1400px block, with 24px of padding from 768px up.
- **Five width tokens**: `--docs-width` (1400), `--docs-sidebar-width` (220), `--docs-aside-width` (268), `--docs-toc-width` (240) and `--docs-text-width` (900).

## Changed

- **The full-width line under the `Header` area tabs** is the second line Aurea draws under its no-lines rule, alongside `Card variant="outline"`.
- **`DependencyGraph`, editable mode: moved nodes stay aligned.** With the grid on, the automatic layout now lands on the 16px grid, and the edges follow the node.
- **`DependencyGraph`, dragging a node**: the node snaps to the edge or center of a neighbor within 8px, and to the position where its connected edge becomes straight. A guide appears in the focus color and thickness (`.graph-guide`).
- **`DependencyGraph`, before this release**: nodes started off the grid and only snapped later, leaving a step in the edge. An edge leaving a port that is not centered never became straight.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.35.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.35.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.35.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.35.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.35.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-34-0.html">
# v0.34.0

No lines. Components no longer draw borders on web or React Native; what needed a border to stand out now gets a translucent fill.

Aurea no longer draws borders. Every border color is now transparent, but the border width stays, so no size changes. Parts that used to rely on a line to stand out get a translucent fill in the text color instead. Focus rings stay. No new components.

## Changed

### No lines

- **No component draws a border**, on the web, in the CSS and in React Native. Every border color is transparent; the width stays, so no measurement changes. Thin `box-shadow` rings are gone too.
- **Focus stays visible**: the focus ring on the web, and a border in the focus color in React Native.
- **The only remaining line**: `Card variant="outline"`, in a light line (the text color at 10%).

### Fills that replace the line

- **Parts that disappeared into the background now get a fill**: translucent fills of the text color that stand out on any background behind them.
- **`--fill-1`** (6%).
- **`--fill-2`** (10%): `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `SearchField`, `NumberField`, `OTPField`, `InputGroup`, `MultiCombobox`, the outline `Button`, `Toolbar`, `CodeBlock`, `LogStream` and `FileInput`.
- **`--fill-3`** (20%): the box of `Checkbox` and `Radio`, and the track of `Switch`.
- **Opaque fills** (`--fill-2-solid`, `--fill-3-solid`): the dot of `Stepper`, the `Avatar`, and the `DependencyGraph` node.
- **Outline `Button` with a tone, and outline `Badge`**: the tone at 16% as background (22% on hover for the button).
- **React Native**: fields inside `Card variant="brand"` use the card's ink at 14%, and so do the outline `Button` and `IconButton` there.

### Contrast

- **Light theme, outline `Button` and `IconButton` with a status tone** (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`): the text moves 20% toward the text color. On the new 16% background, blue had dropped to 4.02:1. The worst case is now blue on hover, at 4.64:1 (web and React Native).
- **Outline `Badge`, both themes**: the text moves 20% toward the text color. The worst case is now 4.79:1. The soft and flat badges keep their own background and do not change.
- **`LogStream`**: the `info` level text also moves toward the text color (it was 4.08:1 in the light theme on the new background).

### States that used to be a line

- **Signals that were a line are now a fill**: the invalid field (`--danger-bg`), the selected `Card` (brand color at 12%), the `Stepper` step with an error, a running or failed run, the error message, the active media item, and the selected node and container in the `DependencyGraph`.
- **Drawings that were strokes are now solid shapes**: the `Checkbox` check, the `Spinner` (same arc), the thumbs of the color `Slider` and the `ColorArea` (white underneath, a dot in the color on top), the `ColorSwatch` swatch (with a shadow), the offline mark of `Status`, the `Card accent` stroke, and the `CodeEditor` cursor.
- **Windows high contrast**: the `Spinner` and the `Checkbox` check opt out of the color override and paint in the text color, so they no longer vanish.
- **`TableOfContents`**: the marker of the current item was a one-sided border. It is now a solid shape, in the same place and at the same size.

## Fixed

- **`Stepper` on the web**: a completed step never turned yellow. The component wrote `step-done` and `step-active`, while the CSS only read `.step.done` and `.step.active`. Both forms now work.

## Breaking changes

- **Appearance, across all components.** If you identified a state by its line (the red invalid field, the selected item), you now see a fill instead.
- **Variants that were only a line now look closer to others**: outline `Badge` and `Button` get a background, `Card variant="contrast"` in the dark theme loses its yellow outline, `Tabs` `secondary` loses the bottom line, `Table` loses the lines between rows, and the pressable `Card` in React Native looks the same as the regular one.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.34.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.34.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.34.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.34.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.34.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-33-0.html">
# v0.33.0

RadioGroup on the web, a three-position ThemeToggle with a system preference, Card parts, soft buttons, a blurred Header, and popups that stay above fixed headers.

The new component is [RadioGroup](./radiogroup.html) on the web, with the same API as React Native. [ThemeToggle](./themetoggle.html) gets a three-position mode, and `AureaProvider` can follow the system color scheme. [Card](./card.html) gets composable parts, `Button` gets a soft appearance, and the [Header](./header.html) can blur its background. Popups no longer slide under a fixed header, and [CommandPalette](./commandpalette.html) now closes on Esc and outside click.

## New

### Components and props

- **`RadioGroup` on the web**: uses the React Native names (`value`, `onValueChange`, `orientation`, `disabled`, `invalid`) and `RadioGroup.Item` (the `Radio`). Options are native radio buttons with a shared name: Tab enters the selected one, and the arrow keys move and select.
- **`Radio` and `Switch` `description`**: a muted line under the label, like `Checkbox`.
- **`labelHidden` on `Switch`, `Radio` and `RadioGroup`**, as on `Checkbox`: the label leaves the screen and stays for screen readers.
- **`Switch` `indicatorPlacement="end"`**: the switch after the label, the same name as on the React Native `RadioGroup`. The default stays `"start"`.
- **`OTPField` `groupSize`** (a dash every N boxes, for example 3 + 3) and **`variant="secondary"`**.
- **`Button` `appearance="soft"`**: a light background in the tone and text in the tone, in every tone. Also the **`variant="danger-soft"`** shortcut and **`quiet`** (muted text, one step smaller).
- **`Button` `kbd` accepts a list** (`["Ctrl", "K"]`): one key cap per key, and screen readers get the combination (`Control+K`). A string still renders one key cap.
- **`Button` `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon`, and `IconButton` `icon`**, accept your own icon component (`AureaIcon`), as `Icon` already did. Icon names work as before.
- **`Card` parts**: `Card.Header`, `Card.Title` (an `h3`), `Card.Description`, `Card.Content` and `Card.Footer`, with 12px between them.
- **`Alert` `action`**: a button before the close X. On phones it moves below the text.
- **`ListBox` item `kbd`**: a shortcut at the end of the row.
- **`Avatar` `tone` and `emphasis="soft"`**: the color of the fallback letters or icon, and a light background in the tone.
- **`Badge` `emphasis="flat"`**: the usual tone without the surrounding line.
- **`ColorSwatch` with options, `showLabels`**: the name of each color under it. The whole label selects.
- **Section dividers** in `ListBox`, in `Select` with groups and in the comboboxes.
- **`CommandPaletteShell` `onClose` and `label`**: the shell is now the same dialog as `CommandPalette`. Esc and outside click call `onClose`, Tab stays inside, and focus returns to the trigger. Without `onClose`, it stays open until `open` changes.

### Header and layout

- **`Header` `size="sm"`**: 56px tall, 6px between actions.
- **`Header` `blurred`**: a background that blurs what scrolls behind it. It stays solid for users who ask the system for reduced transparency.
- **`Header` `menuActions`**: actions that only the mobile menu shows.
- **`Header` `itemsJustify`** (`"end"`, the default, or `"start"`): with `"start"`, the links sit next to the brand and the actions at the other end.
- **`Section variant="footer" layout="inline"`**: a one-line footer.

### Theme

- **`ThemeToggle mode="light-dark-system"`**: a three-position theme switch.
- **`AureaProvider` preference `"system"`**: follows `prefers-color-scheme` and changes with it. Also `onThemePreferenceChange` and the `AureaThemePreference` type.
- **New base tokens**, the same in both themes: `--white` and `--black`.

## Fixed

- **`CommandPalette` closes on outside click, and on Esc wherever focus is.** It now lives in a dialog: it traps Tab, locks background scrolling and returns focus to the trigger. Class names stay the same (`.command-overlay`, `.command-palette`).
- **Fields with a leading icon**: the text sat 24px from the icon (28px at `lg`), with 13px on the other side. Now it is 12px, the icon, 12px; in search fields, 12px, the magnifier, 8px. This applies to every `InputGroup` with an inline leading addon (`SearchField`, `CommandPaletteShell`, the `DataGrid` search), including responsive values.
- **`Card.Header`**: the title and description were 16px apart because of an old `.card-header` rule.
- **Popups slid under a fixed header**: their stacking layer was on a static inner box, where it has no effect. The 13 popups (popover, menus, `Select` and `Combobox` lists, tooltip, hover card, calendar) now carry the `positioner` class with the layer on it.
- **The three-position `ThemeToggle`**: the selected option is white in both themes, the moon and monitor are pure black (21:1), and the selected sun is the brand yellow.
- **Soft buttons**: danger, success, warning and info now use the alert backgrounds (`--danger-bg`, `--success-bg`, `--warning-bg`, `--info-bg`) and 8% of the tone on hover. The `info` label had dropped to 4.10:1 in the light theme; the worst case is now 5.08:1 at rest and 4.61:1 on hover. The general tone hover rules no longer paint over the soft button.
- **`AureaProvider`** only queries the system color scheme when the preference is `"system"`.
- **`Button` docs**: they said the default variant was `secondary` and did not list `tertiary`. The default is `tertiary`.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` (web) has four new keys**: `themeChoice`, `themeLight`, `themeDark` and `themeSystem`. If you build the whole object yourself (your own translation), add them.
- **Component `category` groups changed** in the registry: 15 groups in alphabetical order, then AI & Agents, Code and Communication. If you filter components by the old group names, use the new ones.
- **`CommandPalette` and `CommandPaletteShell` render in a portal**, like `Dialog`. Tests that looked for the box inside the component's container need to look in the document.
- **`Button` types**: `kbd` is now `string | readonly string[]`, and `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` are `AureaIcon`. Code that reads these props expecting `string` or `IconName` needs to accept the rest.
- **The `.card-header` CSS class** is no longer an inline row header (with a 16px gap and 16px below). It is now the column of `Card.Header`. For a row with an action on the right, use `Cluster`.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.33.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.33.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.33.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.33.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.33.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-32-0.html">
# v0.32.0

Twelve new components, including Slider, ListBox, DatePicker on the web and a full color family; redesigned controls and dialogs; and a 48px touch scale for React Native.

The largest release so far. Twelve new components: `CloseButton`, `Slider`, `CheckboxGroup`, `ListBox`, `Link`, `ColorSwatch`, `ProgressCircle`, `TagGroup`, `DatePicker` on the web, `ColorArea`, `ColorField` and `ColorPicker`. Most existing components get new anatomy, sizes and states, and React Native moves to a touch scale with 48px as the medium size. Read the Changed and Breaking changes sections before upgrading: several defaults changed.

## New

### New components

- **[CloseButton](./closebutton.html)**, web and React Native: a neutral gray circle with a dimmed X, labeled "Close" by default ("Fechar" in `ptBR`). `label` says what it closes; `children` replaces the X. Web: 24px, with a 44px touch area around it. React Native: 40px, with a 12px extended touch area.
- **[Slider](./slider.html)**: label and value on top, a 20px track with a fill and a capsule thumb. One value or two (`defaultValue={[20, 80]}`, `thumbLabels`), vertical, values formatted with `Intl` (`format`, `locale`), and `onValueChange` and `onValueCommitted` with the number. `Range` (the browser input) stays as it was.
- **[CheckboxGroup](./checkboxgroup.html)**: label, description, the boxes and the error. It holds the list of checked values (`value`, `onValueChange`); each `Checkbox` inside sets its own `value`.
- **[ListBox](./listbox.html)**: a standalone list of options with icons, descriptions and sections. Selection of none (an action list, `onAction`), one or many. Keyboard per the ARIA Authoring Practices: arrows, Home, End, Space, Enter and type-ahead.
- **[Link](./link.html)**: a text link in medium weight and the link color, underlined on hover. `external` opens a new tab with an arrow; `disabled` does not navigate.
- **[ColorSwatch](./colorswatch.html)**: a round color sample with `color`, `size` (xs 16 to xl 40) and `label` for screen readers. Transparent colors (4- or 8-digit hex, `rgba()`, `hsla()`) show a checkerboard.
- **[ProgressCircle](./progresscircle.html)**: circular progress at 20, 28 or 36px, with the `Progress` colors. Without `value`, it spins.
- **[TagGroup](./taggroup.html)**: tags with selection of none, one or many, a remove X (`onRemove`), description and error. One Tab stop, arrows between tags, Delete removes.
- **[DatePicker](./datepicker.html) on the web**, in `@aurea-uds/react/calendar`: the same name and props as React Native (`value`, `onChange`, `minimumDate`, `maximumDate`, `disabled`, `size`, `format`, `placeholder`, `icon`), plus `defaultValue`, `name`, `range` and `locale`. The trigger is the `Select` field with a calendar icon; the popup is the `Calendar` in a popover. Forms receive the local date (`yyyy-mm-dd`, or `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd` for a range).
- **`DatePicker` language**: `locale` takes the same object as `Calendar` (`import {ptBR} from "react-day-picker/locale"`), and the field and calendar change together. Without it, English. It never uses the environment language, so server and browser render the same text.
- **[ColorArea](./colorarea.html)**: a square to pick saturation and brightness of a hue, by pointer, touch or keyboard. Or any pair of HSB, HSL or RGB channels (`colorSpace`, `xChannel`, `yChannel`), with an optional dot grid (`showDots`). The value is hex, with `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` and `onValueCommitted`. Screen readers hear a 2D control and the color name ("vivid blue"). No new dependency.
- **[ColorField](./colorfield.html)**: a color swatch and the code (hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` or `hsb()`), applied on Enter or blur. Invalid text reverts; empty clears (reports `""`). With `channel`, one channel as a number with arrows, Page Up/Down and Home/End. Same skins as `Input` (`size`, `variant`); inside a `Field`, it uses its label, description and error; `name` submits the hex.
- **[ColorPicker](./colorpicker.html)**: the trigger is the swatch with its name; the popup has the area, the hue track and the code field, always. `swatches` adds preset colors, named in the app's language; `variant="swatches"` is a closed palette (swatches and code only). You can also compose it with `children`: the `ColorArea`, `Slider` with `channel` and `ColorField` inside share the picker's color.

### New props on the web

- **`Slider` `channel`**, color tracks: `hue`, `saturation`, `brightness`, `lightness`, `red`, `green`, `blue` or `alpha` (`colorSpace` sets the space). The value is the color, and `onValueChange` returns the hex, so several tracks share one color. Screen readers hear the channel, its value and the color name.
- **`ColorSwatch` `options`**: with `options` (hex or `{color, label}`), `name` and `label`, swatches become a choice group built on native radio buttons, with no JavaScript, rendered on the server. Five sizes, a `disabled` option, `layout="stack"` and a custom `indicator`. The check uses whichever ink contrasts more with the color (WCAG).
- **`Icon` `bold` weight**, only for the names drawn in it (today, `x`). Sprite id `i-x-bold`; React Native `@aurea-uds/native/icons/x-bold` (register it as `"x-bold"`).
- **`Button variant="tertiary"`**: the neutral background with regular text, which is what `secondary` looked like up to 0.31.0.
- **`ButtonGroup`**: `variant`, `size` and `disabled` apply to every button inside (each can override), plus `fullWidth` and `detached`. **`ToggleGroup`**: `size`, `fullWidth` and `detached`.
- **`Toggle` `variant`**: `default` (neutral background, the default) or `ghost` (no background, the previous look).
- **`Field` `required`**: a red asterisk after the label (hidden from screen readers) and `required` on the control.
- **`Input` and `Textarea` `variant="secondary"`**: a neutral background with no visible border, for use inside cards.
- **`Tabs` `variant="secondary"`**: no rail, a line under the list, and the selected tab underlined.
- **`Pagination`**: `variant` (`numbers`, the new default; `simple`, previous and next only; `compact`, the previous look), `summary`, `href` (each page becomes a real link), `siblings` and `label`.
- **`Accordion`**: `variant="surface"` (in a card), `multiple`, `defaultValue` and `disabled` items.
- **`Sidebar` `placement="right"`**, and the `AppShell` right column (`aside`, `asideLabel`) for an "On this page" column from 1280px up; below that, it goes after the content.
- **`Sidebar` `variant="plain"`**: a sidebar with no box. **`AppShell` `asideVariant`** sets the variant of the right column.
- **`Sidebar` `scrollbar`** (`hover`, the new default, or `visible`), passed through by **`AppShell` `sidebarScrollbar`**.
- **`Card variant="outline"`**, web and React Native: a card in the color of what is behind it, with only a line around it.
- **`CommandPalette`**: titled groups (`group` on each item) and a row of keyboard hints at the bottom (`shortcuts`, on by default).
- **`Dialog` and `ConfirmDialog`**: `icon` (in a 40px circle above the title), `iconTone` (`neutral`, `brand`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`; in `ConfirmDialog` it follows `destructive`) and `placement` (`auto`, `center`, `top`, `bottom`).
- **`Drawer`**: all four sides (`side="top"` and `side="bottom"`, the bottom sheet on phones), `footer`, and drag to close. Top and bottom drawers have a handle.
- **`Tooltip`**: `arrow`, `delay` and `closeDelay`. **`Popover`**: `arrow`.
- **`Badge` `tone`**: the React Native name for the color.
- **`Alert variant="accent"`**, in the Aurea link color.
- **`Text`, `Heading`, `Paragraph` and `Code` `tone`**: `default`, `muted`, `subtle`, `primary`, `link`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`. It wins over `color`.
- **`CodeBlock` `preview`**: a Preview | Code example box, with the preview on a sunken background.
- **`Spinner` `size="xl"`** (40). **`Progress`**: `showLabel`, `showValue` and `size` (a 4, 8 or 12px track). **`Skeleton` `animation`**: `pulse` (default) or `none`.
- **`AureaProvider` `toastPlacement`**: `bottom` (default), `bottom-start`, `bottom-end`, `top`, `top-start`, `top-end`. Toasts accept `actionProps`, and a `promise()` toast shows a spinner while loading.
- **`DataState` `catchErrors` and `onCatch`**, web and React Native: an error boundary. A render error inside the content shows the error state with a retry button, and the rest of the screen stays. `onCatch` receives the error for logging.
- **Heading line heights**: tokens `text-4xl-leading` to `text-lg-leading` (40, 36, 32, 28, 28, 24 for headings of 36, 30, 24, 20, 18, 16), used by `Heading`, `Text type="h*"` (web and React Native) and `.prose` headings.

### React Native

- **A touch scale**: tokens `touch-control-h-sm/md/lg`, 40, 48 and 56 at comfortable density; 36, 44, 52 at compact; 44, 52, 60 at spacious. The web keeps its own scale.
- **`Accordion`**: `items`, `variant` (`default`, `surface`), `multiple`, `defaultValue`, and controlled `value` with `onValueChange`. The chevron rotates on a spring and the answer fades in.
- **`ScrollShadow`**: a 1px line at the edge where content is hidden, and only there. The list sits on an Aurea surface; `variant="plain"` removes it for use inside a card. `orientation`, `visibility`, `isEnabled`; supports inverted lists.
- **`SkeletonGroup`** (and `SkeletonGroup.Item`): `isLoading`, `isSkeletonOnly` and `animation`, with one pulse for the whole group. **`Skeleton`** gets `isLoading`, `children` and `animation`; with `isLoading={false}` the content fades in.
- **`PressableFeedback`**: a touch target that shrinks slightly when pressed, with three combinable parts: `.Highlight`, `.Ripple` and `.Scale`.
- **`Slider`**, **`OTPField`** and **`TagGroup`**: the web components, for touch.
- **`Popover`** and **`DropdownMenu`**: a panel with title and arrow, and a menu with the same `MenuEntry` as the web (action, link, toggle, single choice, submenu, section). React Native only for now: `destructive` on action items.

### Dependency graph

- **`GraphEdgeItem.status`**: the state of an edge, like the node badge: `label`, `tone` (`neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`) and an optional `mark` in the middle of the edge. Colored edges are twice as thick so the color shows; all three weights double together.
- **A two-part legend**: the link type (`legend`, shown by the drawing, without color) and the status (`status.label`, in color), each with a visible title (`graphLegendKind`, `graphLegendStatus`). With only one part, the legend looks as before.
- **`@aurea-uds/react/graph-worker`**: the layout worker through an Aurea path. In Vite: `import GraphWorker from "@aurea-uds/react/graph-worker?worker"` and `layoutWorker={() => new GraphWorker()}`. It imports the `elkjs` worker (the optional peer), so `elkjs` is not bundled into the package.
- **Keyboard on the read-only graph**: the graph is one Tab stop (the last visited node, or the first). Arrows move between nodes. With a node focused, Tab goes through its close button and its edges, then leaves the graph. On a focused edge, the arrows go to its ends.

## Changed

### Look and behavior on the web

- **`Button variant="secondary"` now has brand-colored text** on the neutral background. **A `Button` without `variant` does not change**: the default is now `tertiary`, the same look as before (class `btn-tertiary`, no longer `btn-secondary`). The `ConfirmDialog` cancel button moves to `tertiary` and looks the same; the `DataGrid` export and `FileInput` buttons stay `secondary` and get the brand text. For the neutral look on a `secondary` button, use `tertiary`.
- **`Button`**: 16px side padding (was 15), `lg` 16px (was 20). Icons are 16px from 640px up and 20px below, and always 16px at `sm` and `xs`.
- **`ButtonGroup` and `ToggleGroup` are attached** in one capsule: no gap, rounded only at the ends, a thin divider between buttons. For separate capsules, pass `detached`.
- **`Toggle`** has a neutral background by default; the on state is unchanged. For no background, pass `variant="ghost"`.
- **`IconButton` inside a `ButtonGroup` with `variant`** follows the group; on its own, it stays ghost.
- **Control heights on the web**: `sm` 32 and `lg` 40 (were 30 and 42); `md` stays 36. Compact 28/36, spacious 36/44.
- **Fields**: 12px side padding in inputs and text areas, 8px top and bottom in text areas, labels in medium weight, hints and descriptions at 12/16, errors with a 4px indent.
- **`NumberField` in a group**: one group with the field background, and the plus and minus buttons inside it (40px wide), with a divider. Previously two ghost buttons beside the field. 44px on touch.
- **`OTPField`**: 38 × 40px cells, digits at 18px semibold (were 36 × 36, 14px).
- **`Checkbox` and `Radio`**: a 16px mark (was 18), checkbox radius 6px, 12px to the text, medium-weight text, description at 12/16. A selected radio is filled, with a dot.
- **`Switch`**: a 40 × 20 track (sm 32 × 16, lg 48 × 24; was 42 × 24), a 22 × 16 capsule thumb, 12px to the text.
- **`Kbd`**: 24px tall, 8px side padding, 14px medium-weight text in the body font, neutral background, no border, capsule-shaped and round for a single character (was 20px, 11px code font, with a border). Inside a button, 20px.
- **Headings**: line heights now follow the heading scale (no longer 1.2 for all).
- **`Tabs` and `SegmentedControl`**: a rail with 4px padding and no gap, 32px tabs with 16px sides, medium weight. The rail is 40px (was 36).
- **`Breadcrumb`**: 6px gap, medium weight, underline on hover, current page in the text color, 12px separator.
- **`Accordion`**: no box around it, a divider between items, 16px padding, a 16px chevron at the end that rotates when open (was the browser marker at the start), muted 14px answer, and **one item open at a time**. `multiple` restores the previous behavior.
- **`Pagination`**: the default is now page numbers, with the current page highlighted. The previous look is `variant="compact"`. `onPageChange` is no longer required (with `href`, pages can just navigate).
- **`CommandPalette`**: the list lives inside the palette box (was a popup under the field), and the first result is preselected.
- **`Dialog` and `ConfirmDialog`**: the X is a `CloseButton` in the corner, 16px from the edge. Title 16px medium; body 14/20 in the muted color, and only the body scrolls (header and footer stay). **On phones the dialog sits at the bottom** (`placement="auto"`, the default; `center` restores the middle). Screen margin is 16px on phones and 40px from 640px up. It grows in and shrinks out.
- **`Drawer`**: side drawers are 320px on phones and 384px from 640px up, never more than 85% of the screen (was up to 480). Radius 22 on the inner side, a scrolling 14px muted body, and a `CloseButton` in the corner. The default side is still the right.
- **`Tooltip`**: 8px padding, 12/16 text, up to 320px wide, the popup background. Opens after 1.5 s of hover and closes 0.5 s after leaving; from the keyboard, immediately. Non-focusable triggers (a `span`, a `Badge`) now receive focus.
- **`Popover`**: 14px text, title in medium weight.
- **`Table` and `DataGrid`**: a gray frame without border, a header of 12px medium muted text without uppercase, and the body as a card inside. Cells have 12px top and bottom and 16px sides, 14px text. The selected `DataGrid` row is highlighted. On phones the table scrolls sideways inside the frame. The `caption` sits on top, aligned with the columns.
- **`Badge`**: 4px between glyph and text (was 6), `sm` 6px padding (was 8), `lg` 14px (was 12), 16px line height.
- **`Avatar`**: 32, 40, 48 (were 32, 36, 40), initials at 12, 14, 16 in medium weight.
- **`Card`**: 16px padding (was 20; compact 12, spacious 20), title 14/24 and description 14/20 right below.
- **`Calendar`**: the month at the start and both arrows together at the end, round days in medium weight, today highlighted (was a ring), days outside the month at half strength, disabled days struck through.
- **`Alert`**: a card background without border, with the surface shadow (the state color used to tint background and border). The state color goes on the 16px icon and the medium-weight title; the body is muted. The X is a `CloseButton`. `Banner` does not change.
- **`Spinner`**: sizes 16, 24, 32, 40 (were 16, 20, 24), and the default is `md`, **24px** (was 16). The spinner inside buttons stays 16.
- **`Skeleton`**: radius 8px, and static for users who ask for reduced motion.
- **Toasts (`useToast`)**: toasts stack in one place (the front one whole, the others peeking; hover or focus expands the stack), at the bottom center (was the bottom end corner), 460px wide (was 360), dismissed after 4 s (was 5), three visible. The type colors the icon and title instead of the background. The X is a 20px `CloseButton` that appears on hover or focus (always on touch).
- **`Sidebar` scrollbar**: light and hidden at rest; it appears on hover, with keyboard focus inside, and always on touch screens. `scrollbar="visible"` keeps the previous one.
- **`Sidebar` group titles and the `TableOfContents` title**: 14px, no uppercase (were 12 and 11px, spaced uppercase). The table of contents title gets a lines icon drawn in CSS (`span.toc-label-icon`).
- **`Sidebar` items that are not current are muted** and light up on hover; group titles and the current item stay strong. Measured contrast: 7.6:1 dark, 5.4:1 light.
- **`TreeView` and `NavList` no longer widen the page**: in a `1fr` grid column or a `flex: 1` child they asked for the full label as minimum width. Rows keep their position and height.
- **`Field`**: the `label` now has an `id`, so other parts (like the `DatePicker` popup) can point to it. Nothing changes on screen.
- **Gradients**: the no-gradients rule has one exception, for painting pickable colors in the color area and color tracks. The CSS still has no gradients.
- **`@aurea-uds/react` `sideEffects`** is now a list containing `dist/graph-worker.js`; every other file stays side-effect free.

### React Native: the 48px touch scale

- **`Button`, `IconButton`, `LinkButton`**: sm 40, md 48, lg 56 (were 32, 36, 40), with 14, 16, 20 side padding and 14, 16, 18 medium-weight text. `xs` (32) and `xl` (64) remain.
- **Fields** (`Input`, `InputGroup`, `PasswordField`, `SearchField`, `Combobox`, `NumberField`, `DatePicker`, `FileInput`): 40, 48, 56 with 12px sides. `Select` options show a 20px check on the selected one (register the `check` icon). `Textarea` is 128 tall. `Field` labels in medium weight.
- **`Checkbox`** 24 (was 18) with radius 6; **`Radio`** 24 with a 10px dot; **`Switch`** 48 × 24 with a 28 × 20 capsule thumb.
- **`Avatar`**: 40, 48, 64 (were 32, 36, 40).
- **`NavList`** with 16px padding and 16px medium titles; **`Tabs`** with 16px medium labels.
- **`Dialog`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Drawer` and `BottomSheet`**: 20px padding, 18px medium titles; the `Dialog` and `Drawer` X is a `CloseButton` in the corner.
- **`Alert`** matches the web (card, no border, shadow, state color on icon and title). **`Toast`** no longer tints its background, has 16px padding and a `CloseButton`.
- **`Spinner`**: 16, 24, 32, default 24 (16 inside the `Combobox` list).
- **`NumberField` `display`** grows to 64 (was 50).
- **`BottomNav` does not change.**

### Dependency graph

- **"Fit to screen"** reserves space at the top for the editing toolbar and zoom buttons, so the top node is no longer hidden behind them. The space is measured, so it follows a toolbar that wraps on narrow screens.

## Fixed

- **Windows high contrast, color swatches lost their color** in `ColorSwatch`, swatch options, the `ColorPicker` trigger and the `ColorField` swatch: they turned into white circles and the check vanished. They now opt out of the system override; the focus ring stays in the system color.
- **Windows high contrast, mask-drawn glyphs vanished**: the `Header` menu, the external link arrow, the `KPI` arrow, the copied check on anchored toasts and the `Accordion` chevron. They now paint in the system text color.
- **`Accordion` chevron** no longer depends on the icon sprite: it is drawn in CSS, at the same size and position. Pages using only the `Accordion` showed a network error and an empty arrow.
- **`InputGroup` with an `Input variant="secondary"` inside** showed the `primary` border. The group now reads the skin of the inner input too.
- **`Toggle` without `size`** rendered the class `btn-undefined`.
- **`Slider` thumbs had no accessible name in server-rendered HTML.** The label now has its own id that names the group and each thumb in the markup; `disabled` also sets `aria-disabled` on the group.
- **Two `Pagination` on one page** were two landmarks with the same name. Use `label` to name each one.
- **The current `Pagination` page drew two lines on focus**; the ring now touches the border.
- **`Table` with `stickyFirstColumn`**: cells showed through a 4px strip left of the pinned column when scrolling sideways, including in right-to-left layouts.
- **`Button` `kbd`**: the key inside a button now gets its size from the `btn-kbd` class, not from context. A `Kbd` placed manually inside a button keeps the standalone size.
- **The published API surface** listed only 8 of the 21 `Slider` props, because props written as `Base & (A | B)` were not merged. All props are listed now.
- **Prop descriptions** for `appearance`, `tone` and `share` on `Button`, `IconButton` and `ToolbarButton` were partly not in English, and some component descriptions mentioned versions or dates.

## Breaking changes

- **New `AureaStrings` keys.** If you build the whole object yourself (your own translation), add them; `ptBR` already has them. Web and React Native: `dataCrashed`, `dataRetry`. Web: `graphLegendKind`, `graphLegendStatus`, `datePlaceholder`, `dateRangePlaceholder`, `colorPicker`, `colorArea2D`, `colorChannel`, `colorHue`, `colorTone`, `colorNameFormat`, `colorHex`, `colorSwatches`, `paginationPage`, `commandHintMove`, `commandHintSelect`, `commandHintClose`, `codeBlockPreview` and `codeBlockCode`.
- **`IconWeight`** is now `"regular" | "fill" | "bold"`, and **`ButtonVariant`** gains `"tertiary"`: an exhaustive `switch` over either stops compiling.
- **`Button variant="secondary"`** now has brand-colored text. Use `tertiary` for the old neutral look.
- **Defaults that changed**: `ButtonGroup` and `ToggleGroup` are attached (`detached` for the old look), `Toggle` has a background (`variant="ghost"`), `Accordion` opens one item at a time (`multiple`), `Pagination` shows numbers (`variant="compact"`), `Dialog` sits at the bottom on phones (`placement="center"`), `Spinner` defaults to 24px, and the `Sidebar` scrollbar hides at rest (`scrollbar="visible"`).
- **Redesigned looks**: `NumberField` groups, `Alert`, toasts, `Table`, `DataGrid`, `Dialog`, `Drawer` and the `Sidebar` items and titles look different.
- **React Native sizes**: controls, fields, `Avatar` and dialogs are larger on the new 48px touch scale. Check layouts that relied on the previous heights.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.32.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.32.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.32.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.32.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.32.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-31-0.html">
# v0.31.0

Editing for the DependencyGraph - drag, align and pin nodes, undo, containers that collapse, routed edges, tree and radial layouts, and options for large graphs.

The second round of the [DependencyGraph](./dependencygraph.html): you can now edit the graph. Nodes can be dragged, aligned, distributed and pinned, with undo and redo. Containers group nodes and collapse, edges avoid crossing nodes, and there are two new layouts. Nothing is removed. The read-only graph's keyboard behavior changes, and step edges in the layered layout are drawn differently.

## New

### Editing

- **`editable`**: drag on an empty area to lasso; Shift, Ctrl or Cmd add to the selection; dragging moves all selected nodes, snapping to a 16px grid (`grid`). A toolbar (the Aurea `Toolbar`) aligns by six edges, distributes with the ends fixed, pins and re-runs the layout.
- **Keyboard and panning in edit mode**: arrow keys move the selection one grid step (four with Shift). Pan with the middle or right mouse button, or Space + drag. With `editable` off, the graph is read-only as before.
- **Undo and redo**: buttons, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y, with the last 100 steps.
- **`onLayoutChange`**: called on every step (forward or back) with the position of every node and the pinned ones. Saving is up to the app. Also `onSelectionChange`.
- **`pinned`**: a pinned node cannot be dragged, and re-running the layout moves every node except it. Nodes that would land on a pinned one move aside.

### Edges and labels

- **Edges that avoid nodes.** In the layered layout, step edges follow the route computed by `elkjs`, at right angles with parallel edges spaced apart. After manual arranging (or with saved positions), an edge that would cross a node detours around it.
- **New optional dependency `@tisoap/react-flow-smart-edge`** (5.0, MIT, no dependencies) computes the detour; the drawing stays Aurea's. Without it, edges stay as they were and the console warns once.
- **Bridges at crossings**: the later edge jumps over the earlier one in a small arc.
- **Labels that hide**: no label covers another label or a node. The one with higher `priority` stays; on a tie, the one earlier in the list. Below 60% zoom, edge text hides.

### Containers and layouts

- **Containers (`parentId`)**: a box around child nodes (site, floor, rack) with a collapse button, icon and name. In the layered layout, children go inside it. One parent per node.
- **`collapsed` and `onCollapseChange`**: a collapsed container hides its children and shows how many ("+4"). Their edges leave from the container, and edges between the same pair merge into one with a count.
- **`collapsible`**: a button in the node's corner hides what can only be reached through it. With redundant links, a node reachable another way does not hide.
- **`shape: "cloud"`**: for the internet, public clouds and remote sites.
- **`layout="tree"`** (a compact tree) and **`layout="radial"`** (the root in the center, straight edges). In these layouts, open containers are not drawn as boxes; children appear on their own.

### Large graphs and export

- **`visibleOnly`**: draws only what is on screen.
- **`layoutWorker`**: runs the layout off the main thread, with a worker your app provides (the Vite recipe is in the README). Zoom out now goes down to 10%.
- **`.drawio` export** includes containers (with their children inside), cloud shapes and bends.
- **`apiRef`**: `undo()`, `redo()`, `align(edge)`, `distribute(axis)`, `relayout()` and `getLayout()`. New types: `GraphLayoutChange` and `GraphAlign`.

## Changed

- **Layered layout with `edgeShape="step"`**: edges follow the route from the layout engine instead of the renderer's default step. These edges look different, and no longer pass through nodes.
- **HTML edge labels** (the pill and the port name) render above edges and nodes (`--graph-label-z`). Inside a container, port names used to appear under the container box.
- **The `@xyflow/react` peer now requires `^12.11.3`** (was `^12.11.2`): 12.11.3 fixes touch dragging together with the lasso, which edit mode uses. Tested on 12.12.0.
- **Nodes with ports** send the position of each port to the layout engine (not just the order), so routes start at the drawn handle.

## Fixed

- **Keyboard on the read-only graph.** Each node had two Tab stops, and every edge received Tab, with an English name from the renderer and an instruction to delete it. Now each node is one stop. An edge is a stop only with `onEdgeSelect`, gets a name built from the two nodes it links, and Enter selects it. All text shown by the renderer comes from the Aurea strings.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` (web) has 22 new keys**: `graphArrange`, `graphUndo`, `graphRedo`, `graphAlignLeft`, `graphAlignCenter`, `graphAlignRight`, `graphAlignTop`, `graphAlignMiddle`, `graphAlignBottom`, `graphDistributeH`, `graphDistributeV`, `graphPin`, `graphPinned`, `graphRelayout`, `graphExpand`, `graphCollapse`, `graphHidden`, `graphEdge`, `graphEdgeHelp`, `graphHandle`, `graphNodeHelp` and `graphMoved`. If you build the whole object yourself, add them. Passing only some strings to `AureaProvider` is unaffected.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.31.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.31.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.31.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.31.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.31.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-30-0.html">
# v0.30.0

Reading large graphs with the DependencyGraph - vertical layered layout, icons, badges and ports, edges that explain themselves without color, minimap, path highlight and export.

The first round of the [DependencyGraph](./dependencygraph.html) for network and topology maps: reading the graph. It can flow top to bottom in layers, nodes and edges carry more information without relying on color, and large graphs get a minimap, navigation and export. The web [Icon](./icon.html) now accepts your own icon component. Nothing is removed and no default changes.

## New

### Layout

- **`orientation="vertical"`**: edges enter at the top and leave at the bottom, with each layer centered.
- **`layout="layered"`**: arranges the graph with `elkjs`, with fewer crossings, `rootId` at the top, a suggested `layer` per node and ports in the declared order.
- **`edgeShape="step"`**: right-angle edges with rounded corners.
- **New optional dependency `elkjs`**, loaded only when requested. Without it, the simple layout is used.

### Nodes and edges

- **Nodes say more, without relying on color**: an `icon` next to the type (never replacing it), a count badge (`count`, with `countLabel` for screen readers), a status badge (`status`, the word) and `ports`, with name and side.
- **Edges say what they are, without relying on color**: `pattern` (dashed, dotted, double), `weight` (thicker), a `mark` in the middle (×, dot, lock), `count`, the port name at each end (`sourceLabel`, `targetLabel`) and a `legend` that builds itself from the edges on screen.
- **`groupParallel`**: repeated edges between the same two nodes become one edge with "×10". It is a button that expands them and groups them again.

### Reading a large graph

- **`minimap`**: an overview of the whole graph.
- **`controls`**: zoom in, zoom out and fit to screen.
- **`focusId`** (go to a node), **`highlight`** (a path lights up and the rest dims), **`highlightNeighbors`** and **`hiddenIds`** (hide nodes without re-running the layout).
- **Events**: `onNodeHover`, `onNodeContextMenu` and `onEdgeSelect`.
- **Low vision and keyboard**: `textSize="lg"` (node text independent of zoom, and the box grows with it), `highContrast` (edges and text in the text color, and thicker), and arrow keys that move from node to node.

### Export

- **`apiRef.toDrawio()`**: a `.drawio` file, written by Aurea with no dependency.
- **`apiRef.toPng()` and `apiRef.toSvg()`**, through `modern-screenshot`, a new optional dependency.

### Icons and docs

- **The web `Icon` accepts your own icon component** (`AureaIconComponent`), as React Native already did, for glyphs the set does not have, such as a router.
- **The icon-name migration table to Phosphor** gains 7 names: `add--alt`, `edge-node`, `flow--connection`, `ibm-cloud-pak--network-automation`, `location`, `network-interface` and `router`.
- **The README** now says to restart your dev server after updating Aurea.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` (web) has eight new keys**: `graphConnections`, `graphFit`, `graphJoin`, `graphLegend`, `graphOverview`, `graphShow`, `graphZoomIn` and `graphZoomOut`. If you build the whole object yourself, add them. Passing only some strings to `AureaProvider` is unaffected.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.30.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.30.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.30.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.30.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.30.0
```
</page>

# v0.29.0

A Card that stands out in both themes, a colored accent strip on top of cards, and a fix for dark sections inside the lory brand.

This release adds two ways to make a card stand out, on the web and in React Native. `Card variant="contrast"` puts the dark theme inside a single card, and `Card accent` draws a thin colored strip along its top. Nothing was removed and no default changed.

## New

- **[`Card`](./card.html) `variant="contrast"`** (web and React Native): a card that stands out from the screen in both themes. In the light theme it is the dark theme's card, with no outline; in the dark theme it is the regular card with a yellow outline.
- **Dark theme inside the contrast card**: every child (text, badge, button, field) adjusts by itself. On the web the card carries `data-theme="dark"`; in React Native only its children get the dark tokens. The app theme (`useAureaTheme`) does not change, and anything that opens from inside (the `Select` list, a `Dialog`) opens in the app theme.
- **Contrast card interaction**: accepts `onPress` in React Native and `render` on the web. Do not use it in a list of choices: in the dark theme its outline looks like `selected`.
- **`Card accent`** (web and React Native): a 4-unit strip along the top in `brand`, `success`, `info`, `warning` or `danger`, using the full tone color, the same in both themes. It is decoration only; the card title still says what it is about. Works with `onPress`, with `accessible` and inside a `Grid`.
- **Token `--accent-width`** (4): the height of the accent strip. The regular border stays `--border-width`.

## Fixed

- **A dark section inside a `lory` brand page used the default Aurea dark colors.** `Section theme="dark"` (and now the contrast card) sets only the theme on the element, while the brand selector required brand and theme on the same element. The brand colors now apply when the theme is set inside the brand. The bug existed since v0.22.0.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.29.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.29.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.29.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.29.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.29.0
```

# v0.28.0

Share buttons that fall back to copying the link, a phone frame for screenshots, an extra-bold weight and tabular numbers.

Buttons can now share a link, with a "Link copied" message when the device cannot share. `Image` gains a generic phone frame, and the type scale gets an extra-bold weight and tabular numbers. Tables now align their digits.

## New

- **`share` on [`Button`](./button.html) and [`IconButton`](./iconbutton.html)** (web and React Native): if the browser can share the link (`navigator.canShare`), the device share sheet opens; cancelling is not an error. Otherwise the link is copied and a "Link copied" message appears attached to the button, with the button's own height, padding, type and capsule shape. Without `url`, the page address is shared.
- **Share failures and screen readers**: if copying fails, the button says so and shows the link selected, ready for Ctrl+C. The message is announced to screen readers.
- **Share on the web and in plain HTML**: in React, the message is the anchored `Toast`, managed by `AureaProvider`. In plain HTML, `aurea.js` does the same for `[data-aurea-share]`, through the new `window.Aurea.share`.
- **Share in React Native**: opens the system share sheet. On Android the link goes inside the message text, because Android drops the `url`. In the browser it follows the web behavior and shows the message through `ToastHost`.
- **[`Image`](./image.html) `frame="phone"`** (web and React Native): a screenshot inside a generic phone frame, with no notch, island or buttons. Outer corner 32, inner corner 24, 9/19.5 ratio by default. With a frame, class and style go to the frame.
- **Dark-theme screenshot**: `srcDark` on the web, `sourceDark` in React Native.
- **Heading and weight tokens**: `--font-heading` (for now the same font as body text) and `--weight-extrabold: 800`. The default heading stays semibold.
- **Atkinson Hyperlegible at weight 800**, shipped for both targets (12 KB on the web, downloaded only when used).
- **Typography props**: `weight="extrabold"` and `numeric` (equal-width digits) on `Text`, `Heading`, `Paragraph` and `Code`.
- **React Native typography**: `Text numeric`, `weight={800}` and the `heading` role. `fontFamilies` accepts `heading`; without it, headings use the `ui` map as before.

## Changed

- **Tables use equal-width digits** (web), so price and year columns line up. The number field does too. In React Native, the `KPI` number and the `Table` cells. Only digits change.
- **"Copied" is announced.** Copying from a code block (in `aurea.js` and in React) and from the `FileInput` receipt now tells screen readers "Copied"; before, only the icon changed.

## Fixed

- **React Native: status-toned text and the `Progress` bar used the background color.** `Text tone="success"` (and `danger`, `warning`, `info`) gave about 2.5:1 in the dark theme. They now use the `-400` text colors, like the web. Tones that are not status tones are unchanged.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` has new keys.** Web: `copied`, `linkCopied` and `linkCopyFailed`. React Native: `linkCopied` and `linkCopyFailed`. If you build a complete object of this type, add them. Passing a partial object to the provider needs no change.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.28.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.28.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.28.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.28.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.28.0
```
</page>
