# v0.27.0

New neutral and status colors for both themes, with separate tokens for fills and text. Also ships v0.26.0 (category badges, KPI direction) and v0.26.1.

Every app using Aurea gets new neutral and status colors in both themes; the brand yellow stays the same. Status fills are now identical in light and dark, and text on the screen uses a separate `-400` color. This release also ships v0.26.0 (category colors for `Badge`, a `KPI` that shows direction) and v0.26.1 (the React Native `DatePicker` in the browser). No props changed and nothing was removed.

## Changed

- **New neutrals.** Light: background `#f5f5f5`, white cards, text `#242424`, muted text `#616161`, borders `#e0e0e0`. Dark: background `#1f1f1f`, cards `#292929`, white text, muted text `#adadad`, borders `#525252` (lighter than before, with more visible borders).
- **New status colors.** Green `#107c10`, orange `#f7630c`, red `#c50f1f` and blue `#0078d4` as solid fills, the same in both themes. Text on them is white; on orange, dark.
- **Fill and text are separate tokens.** `--success`, `--info`, `--warning` and `--destructive` are the solid fill. Text, icons, borders and bars on the screen use the `-400` pair, tuned per theme: outline and ghost buttons, `Status`, the alert icon, `LogStream` and the `Progress` bar. Web and React Native.
- **The solid status badge matches the solid button** of the same tone (same color, same text color), on the web and in React Native. Category, brand and neutral badges are unchanged.
- **Sidebar group labels** go from 62% to 72% of the sidebar text color, for contrast in the light theme.
- **Contrast**: every text role passes 4.5:1 on all five surfaces of each theme.

## Breaking changes

- **If your app paints text with a status fill**, switch to the text tokens: `--success-400`, `--info-400`, `--warning-400` and `--danger-400` instead of `--success`, `--info`, `--warning` and `--destructive`. In the dark theme the fill used as text gives only 2.4 to 3.6:1.
- **React Native**: use `t.color.success400` (and its siblings) for text, and `t.color.success` for fills.

## Includes v0.26.1

### Fixed

- **React Native in the browser: [`DatePicker`](./datepicker.html) now opens the browser's date picker.** The date library has no web version, so nothing opened. Now the browser's own `<input type="date">` (or `type="time"`) sits invisibly on top of the Aurea trigger: the look stays Aurea's, touch and screen readers use the browser field, and the calendar follows the Aurea theme.
- **How it opens**: on desktop a click calls `showPicker()`; inside a page from another origin, where Chrome refuses that call, the field's own icon, stretched over it, opens it. The `Field` label and error reach screen readers. Android and iOS are unchanged.

## Includes v0.26.0

### New

- **Category colors on [`Badge`](./badge.html)** (web and React Native): eight named colors, `red`, `orange`, `green`, `teal`, `cyan`, `blue`, `violet` and `pink` (`variant` on the web, `tone` in React Native). They mark a group, not a state. Yellow is left out because it belongs to the brand.
- **Category badge details**: they work in all three emphases (`soft`, `solid`, `outline`) and pass 4.5:1 in both themes and both brands. Neighboring hues alternate two lightness levels, so they are not told apart by hue alone. New types: `BadgeCategory` (web) and `AureaBadgeCategory` (React Native).
- **Tokens `--category-<color>` and `--category-<color>-bg`** (32 in total, dark and light): the accent and soft background of each category. They do not change with the brand.
- **[`KPI`](./kpi.html) direction** (web and React Native): `direction` (`up`, `down`, `flat`) draws an arrow, colors the trend and adds a word for screen readers. `tone` (`success`, `danger`, `neutral`) flips the color when going up is bad; without `direction`, `tone` paints nothing.
- **KPI labels and layout**: `directionLabel` replaces the spoken word (default in English: "Up", "Down", "No change"). The arrow stays on the first line when the trend wraps.
- **KPI without a box**: `variant="plain"`, for a number inside a card that already exists.
- **New KPI types**: `KPIProps`, `KPIDirection`, `KPITone`, `KPIVariant` (web) and `AureaKPIDirection`, `AureaKPITone`, `AureaKPIVariant` (React Native).
- **New catalog patterns**: a summary box built from `Card`, `Stack`, `Cluster` and the `check` icon; badge categories; KPI direction and KPIs inside a card.

### Changed

- **React Native `KPI` matches the web**: the number goes from `2xl` (24) to `3xl` (30), and the trend from 14 to 16. With `direction`, the accessible name is built from label, number, direction word and trend, because the arrow is a drawing. Apps register the `trend-up`, `trend-down` and `minus` glyphs, like any icon.
- **The KPI inner gap comes from a token** (`--space-1`, 4) instead of a raw `5px`, on both targets.
- **On the web the KPI arrow is drawn in CSS** (the Phosphor icon as a mask), so the KPI stays plain markup with no JavaScript in the browser.
- **The contract** now allows the eight category colors as an exception to the "no alternative palettes" rule.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.27.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.27.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.27.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.27.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.27.0
```

# v0.25.0

Focus is drawn as a single line instead of border plus ring, and the selected tab is finally visible against its track.

Focus used to draw two lines on any part with a border: the part's own border, a gap, and the yellow ring. It is now a single line. The selected item in `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` also gets its own surface and a small shadow, so it can be seen in both themes. No props changed.

## New

- **Token `--segment`**: the surface of the selected item on a track. Light: white; dark: `oklch(0.3964 0.01 285.93)`; `lory` brand in dark: `oklch(0.312 0.02 250)`.
- **Token `--shadow-sm`**: the small shadow under that surface, with three layers.
- **React Native: `t.shadowLayers`**: every shadow with all its layers, in the list format of React Native's `boxShadow` (for example `boxShadow: t.shadowLayers.shadowSm`). The token generator used to keep only the first layer of a shadow; `t.shadow` still has the first layer, so code reading `.offsetX` keeps working.

## Changed

- **Focus is one line (web).** Before, the focus ring sat 2px away from every part and also turned every border yellow with `!important`, giving border, gap and ring on 84 parts: fields, `Select`, `Textarea`, `InputGroup`, `Combobox`, drop zones, checkbox, switch, and outline, secondary and ghost buttons.
- **Parts with their own border**: the border takes the focus color and the ring touches it, a single 3px band (1 of border plus 2 of ring).
- **Parts without a border** (solid button, ghost button, tab, menu item): the ring stays offset, as before. A transparent border no longer turns yellow.
- **Checked checkbox and switch on**: the ring stays offset, because the fill has the ring's color and would disappear if touching.
- **Invalid field**: the ring takes the danger color, so yellow does not hide the red.
- **The selected tab is visible (web and React Native).** In [`Tabs`](./tabs.html) and [`SegmentedControl`](./segmentedcontrol.html) the selected capsule was `--secondary` on a `--muted` track: the same color in light (1:1) and 1.02:1 in dark. It is now `--segment` with `--shadow-sm`: white with a small shadow in light, a lighter gray in dark. The segmented control keeps the brand-colored text and its thin line. This also applies where the segmented control appears inside other parts (`ButtonGroup`, `ToolPermission`).

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.25.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.25.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.25.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.25.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.25.0
```
</page>

# v0.24.1

Fixes the anchored Badge in React Native and the KPI number size on the web, and adds a CSS variable for chart text size.

A patch release with two fixes and one opt-in CSS variable. No new props.

## New

- **`--chart-text`** (web): the size of chart axis and legend text. It was locked to `--text-xs`, and the CSS rule won over the chart's own `tick` setting. Set it on the container, for example `--chart-text: var(--text-sm)` or `var(--text-base)`. Without it, text stays `--text-xs`.

## Fixed

- **React Native: an anchored [`Badge`](./badge.html) was stretched and out of place.** A `Badge anchor="top-end"` around an `IconButton` attached to the 44 touch area instead of the 36 drawn circle, used a fixed `-8` offset and kept vertical padding: a "1" measured 14.9 × 22, with its center outside the circle.
- **How the anchored badge sits now**: it touches the target's corner and moves out by 25% of its own size; minimum size is a 16 square (`xs`/`sm`), 28 (`md`) or 32 (`lg`), which becomes a circle with one digit; no vertical padding; a 1-unit ring in the background color. Around an `IconButton` it ignores the touch area and attaches to the circle. Apps need no change.
- **Web: the [`KPI`](./kpi.html) number had no size.** It rendered at 14, the same as the label, with the trend at the browser's `small`. The number is now `--text-3xl` with tabular digits, and the trend is `--text-sm`. The React Native KPI is unchanged.

## Update

On the web:

# v0.24.0

Comparison tables: sticky header and first column, a two-item mobile fit, a "differences only" switch, and styling for groups and best values.

`Table` gains four switches for comparison pages, plus styling for grouped rows and highlighted best values. A grouped spec sheet joins the catalog as a pattern. Nothing was removed or renamed, and no dependency was added.

## New

- **[`Table`](./table.html) `stickyHeader`**: the header stays at the top of the table box, which gets a maximum height (`--table-max-h`, 60vh) and scrolls inside. Same name and mechanism as `DataGrid`. It sticks to the box, not to the page, because the box also scrolls sideways.
- **`stickyFirstColumn`**: the first column (each row's name) stays in place when scrolling sideways, with an opaque background and a thin line at its end. With both switches, the corner sits on top.
- **`fit`**: removes the 720 minimum width, so two items fit on a 360-wide phone without scrolling sideways. Which two items to show is up to the site (for example with a `Select`).
- **`differencesOnly`**: hides the rows marked as identical (`<tr data-same>`). The site provides the toggle.
- **Comparison markup styling**, with no props: a group band is `<th scope="rowgroup" colSpan>` at the start of each `<tbody>` (styled like the header); the row name is `<th scope="row">`; the best value is `<td data-best>`, in bold. Mark it with a text label too (a `Badge` in the cell), because color alone is not enough. The `Table` entry declares the `best` and `same` states.
- **Catalog patterns**: a spec sheet in groups (a `Card` per group with a title and a `DataList`, in a `Grid` that stacks on phones), and three `Table` patterns: comparison with groups and best value, two items on a phone, and "differences only".

## Changed

- **`<th scope="row">` in the table body** no longer uses the header styling (small uppercase text on the header background). It is now body text in medium weight.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.24.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.24.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.24.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.24.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.24.0
```
</page>

# v0.23.0

Topbar is renamed Header (the old name still works), with a site header that collapses into a mobile menu, and a site footer section.

`Topbar` is now called `Header` on both targets, and the old name keeps working. On the web, `Header` becomes a site header with navigation links and a mobile menu, and `Section variant="footer"` builds a site footer. Nothing was removed.

## New

- **Site header: [`Header`](./header.html) with `items`** (web): the same item list as `Sidebar` and `BottomNav`. `current` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`, the accent color and medium weight; `actions` sits on the right; `maxWidth` aligns the bar with the page `Container`. The bar is 64 tall (`--topbar-height`).
- **Mobile menu**: below 768 the links leave the bar and drop into a panel right under it, as wide as the bar, opened by a button. The panel is a native popover (`<nav popover="auto">`), with no JavaScript, so `Header` stays a server component. Escape and tapping outside close it, and Escape returns focus to the button when the panel was opened by keyboard.
- **Menu id**: the panel id is fixed (`aurea-header-menu`); a page with two site headers passes a `menuId` to each.
- **Known limits**: in apps with client-side routing the panel does not close on navigation, so give `Header` a `key` that changes with the route. In WebKit, after clicking the button, Escape closes the panel but focus goes to the page.
- **Site footer: [`Section`](./section.html) `variant="footer"`** (web): a `<footer>` with the brand (`brand`), link columns with titles (`links`) and a legal line (`legal`), inside a `Container`. It inherits the section background, spacing and theme (a dark footer on a light page is `theme="dark"`). On phones everything stacks; on desktop the columns share the width.

## Changed

- **`Topbar` is renamed `Header`, on the web and in React Native.** `Topbar` remains as the same component, marked as the old name, with identical markup. Types follow: `HeaderVariant` and `HeaderProps` on the web, `AureaHeaderVariant`, `AureaHeaderInset` and `HeaderProps` in React Native; the old type names still work. The `.topbar*` classes and the `AppShell` props (`topbarVariant`, `topbarDivider`) are unchanged.

## Fixed

- **Site header links wrapped to a second line** between 768 and 1023 wide without `maxWidth`, growing the bar from 64 to 80. The `AppShell` bar rule also matched the site header's `nav`. The links now stay on the brand's line.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.23.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.23.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.23.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.23.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.23.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-22-0.html">
# v0.22.0

Layout parts for site pages (Container, Grid.Item span, Section with surface and theme). Also ships v0.21.0 and v0.20.0.

This release adds the layout parts of a website page on the web: `Container`, column spans for `Grid`, and full-width `Section` bands that can switch theme. It also ships v0.21.0 (a choice card for `RadioGroup` in React Native) and v0.20.0 (continuous iOS corners, `fullWidth` segmented controls, a plain `Tabs` panel and photo dates in `PhotoInput`). Nothing was removed or renamed, and no dependency was added.

## New

- **[`Container`](./container.html)** (web): the reading width of a site page. Centered, with a maximum width (`size`: `sm` 640, `md` 768, `lg` 1024, `xl` 1280 by default, `2xl` 1536, `full`) and side padding of 16 that becomes 32 from `md` up.
- **`Grid.Item` with `span`** (web): the item says how many of the 12 columns it takes, for example `<Grid columns={12}><Grid.Item span={{base: "12", viewport: {md: "7"}}}>`. It uses the existing responsive layer (`vp-*` by viewport, `ct-*` by container), with the new `grid-span` family.
- **[`Section`](./section.html)** (web): a full-width band of a site page, a `<section>` with `surface` (`background`, `card`, `inset`) and `spacing` (`md`: 64, and 96 from `md` up; `sm`: half of that).
- **`Section theme`** (web): `theme="dark"` makes a dark band inside a light page, and the other way around.

## Fixed

- **Light-theme rules leaked into a dark section** (web). The 22 `[data-theme="light"] X` selectors in the core still applied inside `<section data-theme="dark">`, so outline buttons, section labels and selected items got light-theme ink on a dark background. Each now carries a zero-specificity guard; rule precedence does not change, and pages without a dark band compute the same styles. Known limit: four alternating nested levels are not covered.

## Includes v0.21.0

### New

- **[`RadioGroup`](./radiogroup.html) `variant="card"`** (React Native): the whole card is the option, announced as a radio button by screen readers (before, cards built from `Card` plus a press handler were announced as buttons). It uses the `Card` look: the regular card, and the selected look of `variant="selected"`. The mark moves to the title line, and the item accepts `children` for extra content inside the card (price, list).

### Fixed

- **A horizontal interactive [`Card`](./card.html) lost its image column** (web). `.card-interactive { display:block }` came after `.card-horizontal { display:grid }` with the same specificity and won. The interactive block is now a zero-specificity default, so the orientation wins regardless of rule order.
- **Cards and menu items rendered as links were underlined** (web). The `<a>` of a `Card` with `render` and the `<a class="menu-item">` of a `DropdownMenu` item with `href` inherited the browser underline. Other parts that become links already removed it.

## Includes v0.20.0

### New

- **`fullWidth` on [`SegmentedControl`](./segmentedcontrol.html)** (web and React Native): the control fills the row, and each segment grows from its label without shrinking below it. When the options do not fit, it scrolls, as without the prop.
- **`panel` on [`Tabs`](./tabs.html)** (web and React Native): `"card"` (default) or `"plain"`. With `panel="plain"` the panel is only top spacing (`space3`), with no box, so content is no longer inset by padding plus border. On the web the new class is `.tabs-panel`.
- **`exif` on `PhotoInput`** (React Native): the date the photo was taken, in `takenAt`. Off by default. Reads `DateTimeOriginal` (with the `OffsetTimeOriginal` time zone when present; otherwise the device time), and stays empty when the photo has no date. The EXIF data itself never leaves the component, because gallery photos carry location.
- **Multiple photos at once**: from the gallery, when `max` still allows more than one photo, several can be picked together (`allowsMultipleSelection` plus `selectionLimit`, Android and iOS 14+).
- **Token `radius-sheet`** (`radiusSheet` in React Native, `--radius-sheet` on the web): the 32 corner of bottom sheets.

### Changed

- **Continuous iOS corners across React Native.** Every radius in the package now goes through one helper that sets the radius together with `borderCurve: "continuous"`. Only iOS 13+ draws it; Android and the browser do not change. The `Spinner` ring stays circular because it spins.
- **[`Alert`](./alert.html) and `Toast` corners are 22** (were 16), on the web and in React Native: the Aurea panel radius, the same as `Popover`, `Dialog` and `Banner`.
- **Bottom sheets have a 32 corner** (was 22) in React Native: `BottomSheet`, the `Select` list and the `Combobox` sheet.

### Fixed

- **The React Native `SegmentedControl` wrapped labels onto two lines** in the browser, because `flex: 1` split the width into equal parts. On devices the label did not wrap, but the capsule did not fill the row. Each segment is now as wide as its label, like a `Tabs` tab and the web segmented control.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.22.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.22.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.22.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.22.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.22.0
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-19-1.html">
# v0.19.1

Fixes square BottomNav indicators on Android. Also ships v0.19.0: lazy TreeView, batch Gallery, attachments and replies in chat, long conversations.

This patch fixes `BottomNav` indicators that rendered square on Android. It also ships v0.19.0, which extends four web components for large data: `TreeView` loads children on open, `Gallery` selects in batches and loads more, `MessageComposer` attaches, replies and edits, and `MessageList` handles long conversations without jumping. No dependency was added.

## Fixed

- **Android: the selected [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html) indicator rendered square** with `capsule` and `circle-bold`. The box that gets painted only had a border radius, so it was flattened into its parent, and when it was created later on selection the radius did not reach Android.
- **The fix**: the icon frame and the `circle-bold` disc now use `collapsable={false}` and exist from mount. This covers the five indicators that paint that box: `capsule`, `circle-bold`, `circle`, `circle-raised` and `circle-outline`. The web never had the bug.

## Includes v0.19.0

### New

- **[`TreeView`](./treeview.html) lazy loading**: `hasChildren` on a node lets it open before it has children. `onExpand(node)` is called on each open; if it returns a promise and the node has no children yet, the node is `aria-busy` with a spinner in place of the arrow until it settles. Children arrive through `items`. A rejected promise closes the node, and opening again retries.
- **`TreeView` controlled selection**: `selectedId` (`string | null`), as in `DependencyGraph`.
- **[`Gallery`](./gallery.html) batch selection**: `selectionMode="multiple"` with `selectedIds` and `onSelectionChange`. Each tile becomes a toggle button (`aria-pressed`) with the usual selected mark; while selecting, a click marks and does not enlarge.
- **`Gallery` videos**: `kind: "video"` and `duration` (seconds) on an item show a `Badge` in the corner with the time as `m:ss`, and "Video" for screen readers.
- **`Gallery` loading more**: `hasMore`, `onReachEnd` and `loading`. A row after the grid notifies when it enters the screen; while loading it shows a spinner and does not notify again; if the new batch does not fill the screen, it notifies again.
- **[`MessageComposer`](./messagecomposer.html) attachments**: `attach` (`true` or `{accept, maxSize, multiple}`) adds a paperclip inside the field. Files sit in a strip above the field, using the `FileInput` row (name, size, image thumbnail, remove). With an attachment, empty text can be sent.
- **`MessageComposer` reply and edit**: `replyTo` with `onCancelReply` shows a quote with a close button; `editing` with `onCancelEdit` puts the old text in the field and turns send into save. Escape cancels both.
- **`onSend` second argument**: `{files, replyToId, editingId}`, only when one of the new props is in use. Code expecting `onSend("text")` still receives exactly that.
- **[`MessageList`](./messagelist.html) message props**: `direction` (`incoming` / `outgoing`; outgoing sits at the end of the row, with no avatar, tinted with the brand), `forwardedFrom`, `replyTo`, `attachments` (photos and videos become a `Gallery` album; files become a `FileInput` row with a download link), `edited` ("edited" next to the time) and `day` (a separator when the day changes).
- **`onOpenAttachment`**: the app opens a photo or video from the album instead of the built-in enlarge.
- **`data-message-id` on every message**, with or without the new props. The list uses it to keep its place, and apps can use it to jump to a message.
- **Sliding window for long conversations**: `hasMoreBefore`, `onReachStart` and `loadingBefore` at the top; `hasMoreAfter`, `onReachEnd` and `loadingAfter` at the bottom. The app keeps a window of messages and swaps at the edges; the list does not jump (the message at the top stays in place, even when a photo grows later), opens at the end and follows new messages when the reader is at the end.
- **Announcements with the window**: the list is no longer a live region; an announcer reads only messages arriving at the end, so older messages loaded at the top are not read aloud.

### Changed

- **`TreeView` items are capsules.** The selected and hover highlights use `--radius-control` instead of `--radius-sm`, like fields, tabs and text buttons.

### Fixed

- **The `TreeView` arrow in right-to-left writing** relied on `:dir(rtl)`, which app bundlers can rewrite. It now flips by the provider's direction (`.tree-twist-rtl`) and turns with the `rotate` property.

### Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` (web) has ten new keys**: `chatAttach`, `chatAttachments`, `chatEditCancel`, `chatEdited`, `chatEditing`, `chatForwardedFrom`, `chatReplyCancel`, `chatReplyTo`, `chatSave` and `galleryVideo`. If you build a complete object of this type, add them. Passing a partial object to `AureaProvider` needs no change.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.19.1 @aurea-uds/core@0.19.1 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.19.1 @aurea-uds/icons@0.19.1
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.19.1
```
</page>

# v0.18.0

Indeterminate Progress with detail and tone, named Grid minimums, NavList avatars and indicators, and a collapsible AppShell sidebar.

`Progress` can run without a total, `Grid` accepts named column minimums, `NavList` shows avatars and small indicators, and `AppShell` gets a button to collapse the sidebar. Component metadata now lists the Phosphor icon names each component actually draws. Nothing was removed or renamed.

## New

- **[`Progress`](./progress.html) without a total** (web and React Native): `value` is optional. Without it the bar is indeterminate: a 2/5 segment runs across in 1.5 s and `aria-valuenow` (`now` in React Native) is omitted. Before, it showed 0% and looked stuck. With reduced motion, the whole bar shows dimmed (`--opacity-disabled`) instead of a moving segment.
- **`Progress` `detail`**: supporting text at the top right, small, medium weight, muted, with equal-width digits. As text it goes into `aria-valuetext` (for example "64%, 2.3 MB/s"), so it is heard once.
- **`Progress` `tone`**: `brand` (default), `neutral`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`. Paused is `neutral`; failed is `danger`.
- **[`Grid`](./grid.html) `min` by name** (web; `minColumnWidth` in React Native): `xs` 8rem, `sm` 12rem, `md` 15rem (default) and `lg` 20rem. Written sizes still work. Before, `min="sm"` passed the type check but produced a single column.
- **[`NavList`](./navlist.html) `avatar` and `indicators`** (web and React Native): `avatar` takes the place of the icon; `indicators` (`[{icon, label}]`) adds small muted signs before the value, such as pinned or muted, and each `label` is what screen readers hear.
- **[`AppShell`](./appshell.html) `sidebarCollapsible`**: draws a button at the top of the seam between the menu and the content, and collapses the sidebar on its own between 1024 and 1279 wide. `defaultSidebarCollapsed` and `onSidebarCollapsedChange` complete the controlled and uncontrolled pair. Without the prop, the shell is unchanged.
- **New strings**: `sidebarCollapse` and `sidebarExpand`, the labels of the collapse button.

## Fixed

- **A collapsed sidebar drawer was a rail of unnamed icons.** Below 1024, with `sidebarCollapsed`, the drawer opened as a rail with names hidden. The drawer is now never a rail, controlled or not.
- **In right-to-left writing the content touched the page edge** and left a 32 gap at the seam, because the `.content` margin was physical. It is now logical; left-to-right is unchanged.
- **The `BottomNav` entry** did not list `capsule` and `expand` in the `indicator` type, and still said every indicator shows the label.
- **Component icon metadata**: 19 old icon names in 12 component entries were replaced with the Phosphor names the code draws, and 22 entries that were missing icons now list exactly what the component draws.
- **The contract** (`aurea.contract.json`) now names Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono and Phosphor as the brand fonts and icons, and describes the icon button as round.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` has two new keys**: `sidebarCollapse` and `sidebarExpand`. If you build a complete object of this type, add them. Passing a partial object to `AureaProvider` needs no change.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.18.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.18.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.18.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.18.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.18.0
```

# v0.17.0

BottomNav no longer shifts when switching tabs, is shorter with labels closer to icons, and gains the capsule and expand indicators.

`BottomNav` was reworked on the web and in React Native. The bar no longer moves when the selected tab changes, it is shorter, and labels sit right under the icons. Two indicators are new: `capsule` and `expand`. Apps get the steadier, slimmer bar just by upgrading.

## New

- **`indicator="capsule"`**: a 56 × 32 yellow capsule behind the icon, present on every item and painted only on the selected one; the label sits below, outside it. The counter stays on the icon's corner and inverts on yellow (web), as in `circle-bold`.
- **`indicator="expand"`**: other items show only the icon; the selected one becomes a yellow capsule with the label beside it, at 14. The selected slot has a fixed width (136), so buttons move but the bar does not. Labels longer than 80 end with an ellipsis.
- **Hidden labels in `expand`**: labels of unselected items leave the screen but stay available to screen readers (`.sr-only` on the web, `accessibilityLabel` in React Native).

## Changed

- **A shorter [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html)** on both targets: 54 for `none`, `subtle`, `pill` and `expand`; 58 for `circle-bold`; 62 for `circle`, `circle-raised`, `circle-outline` and `capsule`, which have a 32 frame around the icon. Before, `circle-bold` measured 73.
- **Label size**: 12 on a 16 line (was 14 on 21 in React Native).
- **Spacing**: the button's top and bottom padding goes from `space1` to `space05`, and the label touches the icon (gap zero, was `space05`).
- **`circle-bold`**: the 32 frame is removed; the circle is the disc, 56 × 48.
- **Unselected labels** now use medium weight, the same as the selected one.

## Fixed

- **The bar moved when switching tabs** (web and React Native). The selected label got heavier, and heavier text is wider; in `circle-bold` the circle was the selected item itself, measuring 56 while the others measured their content. Now no size depends on selection, only the paint changes: every label has medium weight, and the `circle-bold` circle is a disc inside every item (`.bottom-nav-disc` on the web), yellow only when selected.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.17.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.17.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.17.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.17.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.17.0
```
</page>

# v0.16.0

In the light theme, emphasis text and icons move from brown to a darkened brand yellow that still meets 4.5:1 contrast.

A visual change to the light theme, on the web and in React Native. Emphasis text and icons now use a darker shade of the brand yellow instead of brown. No API changes.

## Changed

- **Light theme emphasis colour**: the `primary-emphasis` and `primary-outline` tokens now point to the new `brand-yellow-text` token, `oklch(0.516 0.105 86.047)` (`#826202`). It is the same hue as the primary yellow, darkened to reach 4.5:1 on the hardest light-theme background. It replaces the brown `brand-yellow-foreground` (`#733e0a`).
- **Where you see it**: the selected [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html) item without an indicator, the `primary` [`Badge`](./badge.html), `primary` text, and the outline of a selected card.
- **What stays the same**: the primary yellow itself, the dark theme (where emphasis text is already the pure yellow), the light-theme focus ring and checked controls (still brown), text placed on top of yellow, and the `data-brand` brands.
- The pure yellow is not used as text in the light theme: it only reaches about 1.9:1 on white.

# v0.15.0

React Native gets custom icon components in every icon prop, a richer Timeline, a new FileInput, and a PhotoInput that opens the photo.

A React Native release. Every icon prop now accepts your own drawing, `Timeline` gains icons and tones, and a new `FileInput` picks files from the device. `EmptyState` and `PhotoInput` also look different.

## New

### React Native

- **`AureaIcon` type**: every icon prop (`Icon`, `IconButton`, `BottomNav` and `NavList` items, `Alert`, `EmptyState`, `RadioGroup.Item` and more) accepts either a glyph name (`"truck"`) or a component, such as one made with `criarGlifo` or imported from `icons/*`. A logo can be passed as `icon={Logo}`, with no name registration and no `declare module`. The component receives the `size` and `color` the host asks for. Unknown names still fail in TypeScript.
- A component passed directly has no filled variant for the selected state; the filled shape comes from the registry, as `<name>-fill`.
- **[`Timeline`](./timeline.html)**: new `icon`, `tone`, `trailing` and `between` props. `icon` replaces the dot with a glyph in a 40-point round frame; `tone` colours the frame with the `Badge` colours; `trailing` shows a value to the right of the title; `between` describes what happened between one item and the next, next to the line (for example "6 days later"). One item with `icon` is enough to widen the whole column. Without `icon`, nothing changes.
- **[`FileInput`](./fileinput.html)**, from `@aurea-uds/native/system/file`: picks a file from the device with the system picker (`expo-document-picker`, an optional peer, `>=12`). It returns `{uri, name, size, mimeType}`, never the content. Props: `accept`, `max` (1), `maxSize`, `disabled`, `addIcon`, `fileIcon`, `removeIcon`. Cancelling changes nothing; a file that is too large or of the wrong type is rejected with a red message below.
- `FileInput` has its own entry point so that apps using `DatePicker` from `/system` do not need to install the file picker.
- **New strings**: `fileChoose`, `fileRemove`, `fileTooLarge`, `fileWrongType`, `photo`, `positionOf`, `photoOpen` and `photoAdd`.

## Changed

### React Native

- **[`EmptyState`](./emptystate.html)**: the glyph now sits in a 64-point round frame on the `muted` background. The glyph stays at 32 and uses `mutedForeground`.
- **`PhotoInput` lets you look at the photo**: thumbnails are now 64-point squares, the same size as the add button. Tapping a thumbnail opens the photo full size, with the same zoom as [`Gallery`](./gallery.html). The remove button has a background and sits fully outside the photo.
- Screen readers hear "Photo 2 of 3" and "Opens the photo" on a thumbnail, and "Remove photo 2" on its remove button.

## Fixed

### React Native

- **`PhotoInput`**: the add button only had an accessible name inside a `Field`. Outside one, screen readers now hear "Add photo".
- **`PhotoInput`**: when disabled, the remove button still removed the photo. It no longer does; viewing the photo still works.
- **In the browser, React Native no longer requests the native animation driver.** `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Switch`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Combobox` and `Toast` always set `useNativeDriver: true`, which logged a warning on the web. They now use it only on devices. Nothing changes on devices.

## Breaking changes

- **`AureaStrings` (React Native)** has eight new keys: `fileChoose`, `fileRemove`, `fileTooLarge`, `fileWrongType`, `photo`, `photoAdd`, `photoOpen` and `positionOf`. If you build the full object with this type, add them. Passing only some strings to the provider is unaffected.
- **Appearance**: the `EmptyState` glyph now has a frame, and `PhotoInput` thumbnails are square with the remove button outside the photo.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.15.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.15.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.15.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.15.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.15.0
```
</page>

# v0.14.1

A busy IconButton now shows only a centred spinner. Also ships v0.14.0, with new React Native props for Tabs, Combobox, NumberField and RadioGroup.

On the web, a loading [`IconButton`](./iconbutton.html) now shows only the spinner, centred, and a loading [`Button`](./button.html) replaces its leading icon with the spinner. This release also publishes v0.14.0, which adds new props to several React Native components and deprecates the `text-md` token.

## Fixed

- **`IconButton` with `loading`** showed the spinner next to the glyph, and in a 36-pixel button the spinner spilled outside. It now replaces the glyph and sits in the centre.
- **`Button` with `loading` and `leadingIcon`** showed the spinner, the icon and the text together. The spinner now takes the place of the leading icon, and the text stays.
- `ToolbarButton` uses `Button` internally and gets the same fix. Outside the loading state the button markup is unchanged. The React Native `IconButton` has no loading state and is unchanged.

## Includes v0.14.0

### New

- **[`Tabs`](./tabs.html) `variant="secondary"` (React Native)**: no capsule; a thin line under the whole row and a yellow line under the open tab. The row has the same height as the capsule. Without `variant`, or with `"primary"`, you get the capsule as before. New type: `AureaTabsVariant`.
- **`description` on [`Combobox`](./combobox.html) items (React Native)**: a second, muted 14-point line under the label. Screen readers read it as the item hint. Search still looks only at `label`.
- **[`NumberField`](./numberfield.html) `size="display"` (React Native)**: a large highlighted number, using the 30-point semibold heading size, the `controlHXl` height (which follows density), a 96-point width and the `lg` buttons. New type: `AureaNumberFieldSize`.
- **`icon` on `RadioGroup.Item` (React Native)**: an icon name shown before the text, at 24 with a 12-point gap, in the label colour. The selected option uses the filled shape when the registry has `<name>-fill`.

### Changed

- **`text-md` is now an alias of `text-sm`** (both are 14). It is marked `$deprecated` in the token file. Nothing changes on screen.
- **Deprecated**: `text-md` (and `textMd` in React Native) will be removed in 1.0. Use `text-sm` instead. Aurea's own CSS no longer uses the old name.

### Fixed

- **[`RadioGroup`](./radiogroup.html) description (React Native)** was 16, the same size as the label. It is now 14, matching `Checkbox` and `Switch`.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.14.1 @aurea-uds/core@0.14.1 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.14.1 @aurea-uds/icons@0.14.1
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.14.1
```
</page>

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-13-0.html">
# v0.13.0

New typeface and icon set. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next replaces IBM Plex, and Phosphor icons replace Carbon. Icon names change.

Aurea switches its typeface and its icons across all seven packages. Text now uses **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (and **Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono** for code), and icons are **Phosphor**, Regular weight, with the filled shape on selected items. This release breaks every app that uses icons: read the breaking changes before upgrading.

## New

- **`weight` on [`Icon`](./icon.html)**, on the web and in React Native: `"regular"` (default) or `"fill"`. New type: `IconWeight`. On the web, an app's own icon requested as `fill` falls back to regular instead of rendering an empty `<use>`.
- **Name mapping table**: `@aurea-uds/icons/carbon-para-phosphor.json` lists 260 Carbon icon names with their Phosphor replacement.

## Changed

- **Icons: Phosphor instead of Carbon** (`@phosphor-icons/core` 2.1.1, MIT), from the same source on both targets. 1,433 icons, each in two shapes (regular and `-fill`): 2,866 symbols in the sprite and 2,866 components in `@aurea-uds/native/icons/*`.
- The 79 Phosphor brand logos are not included.
- The Regular stroke matches the previous icons: 1/16 of the size.
- **Selected items show the filled icon**: [`Sidebar`](./sidebar.html) and [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html) on the web, `BottomNav` in React Native.
- **Still filled**: the `Alert` and `Toast` variant glyphs, the moon and sun of [`ThemeToggle`](./themetoggle.html), the completed-upload check in `FileInput`, and the `MediaEmbed` play button. Icons you choose render as you request them.
- **Typeface: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono instead of IBM Plex** (SIL OFL 1.1). Eight files in two formats: Latin-only `.woff2` for the web and full `.ttf` for devices. The font has the same vertical metrics as IBM Plex, so existing line heights still fit.
- **IBM Plex Serif is removed.** `--font-editorial` and the React Native `editorial` role remain as aliases of the body font until 1.0.

## Breaking changes

- **Icon names are Phosphor names.** Carbon names no longer compile. Use `@aurea-uds/icons/carbon-para-phosphor.json` to migrate. Common ones: `close` to `x`, `add` to `plus`, `chevron--down` to `caret-down`, `search` to `magnifying-glass`, `settings` to `gear`, `home` to `house`, `trash-can` to `trash`, `checkmark` to `check`, `menu` to `list`, `notification` to `bell`. The `*--filled` names become the same name with `weight="fill"`.
- **Six names exist in both sets with different drawings**, so they compile but look wrong: `list`, `notification`, `radio`, `subtract`, `tree` and `video`. Replace them using the table even without a compiler error (Carbon `list` is `list-bullets`; Phosphor `list` is the three-line menu).
- **Web**: copy the new sprite, `@aurea-uds/icons/dist/aurea-icons.svg`, to where your app serves it. Symbol ids are `i-<name>`, and `i-<name>-fill` for the filled shape.
- **React Native**: update deep imports (`@aurea-uds/native/icons/plus`, no longer `.../icons/add`) and the registry keys. For selected items, alerts and `ThemeToggle` to render filled, also register the filled shape, for example `{house: House, "house-fill": HouseFill}`. Without it, the regular shape is used.
- **Types**: `CarbonIconName` is removed; use `PhosphorIconName`.
- **Fonts**: just update `@aurea-uds/fonts`. In React Native, `AUREA_FONTS` and `FONT_FAMILIES` already carry the new names (`AtkinsonHyperlegibleNext-SemiBold` and so on).

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.13.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.13.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.13.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.13.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.13.0
```
</page>

# v0.12.4

React Native components running in the browser now expose their state to screen readers through aria attributes.

An accessibility fix for apps that run the React Native package in a web browser. Component state (checked, selected, disabled, expanded, busy) now reaches screen readers there too. No API changes, and nothing changes on devices.

## Fixed

- **React Native state on the web**: components reported their state only through `accessibilityState`, which is not translated in the browser. A `RadioGroup` there, for example, had no `aria-checked`, so screen readers could not tell which option was selected.
- State is now reported in both forms, `accessibilityState` and the matching `aria-*` attribute, with the same value. This covers 20 components (`Button`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Radio`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `SearchField`, `NumberField`, `Card`, `Tabs`, `BottomNav`, `NavList`, `Stepper`, `Chart`, `Gallery`, `DataState`) plus `DatePicker` and `PhotoInput` from `@aurea-uds/native/system`.
- **Toggle buttons** (`pressed` on `Button` and `IconButton`) stay `checked` on devices, as before, and become `aria-pressed` on the web, which screen readers announce on buttons.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.12.4 @aurea-uds/core@0.12.4 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.12.4 @aurea-uds/icons@0.12.4
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.12.4
```

# v0.12.1

React Native fixes for bottom sheets and Grid, plus LinkButton. Also ships v0.12.0 with typed icon names, round icon buttons, ThemeToggle and text components.

This release fixes bottom sheets that slid behind the Android navigation buttons, makes the React Native `Grid` share leftover space, and adds `LinkButton`. It also publishes v0.12.0, which can break builds and changes some appearance: icon names are type-checked, icon-only buttons are round, and the React Native `Button` now follows its parent's alignment.

## New

- **`LinkButton` (React Native)**: a text button that sits flush with the margin. It is a `Button` with no background, no side padding, no border and no fixed height. The touch area keeps a 44-point height. Like every button it follows its parent: to keep it at the margin, use `Stack align="start"`.

## Fixed

- **Bottom sheets behind the Android buttons (React Native)**: `Select`, `Combobox` and `BottomSheet` did not get a bottom inset inside a `Modal`. The inset now comes from the app's safe area context and becomes space at the end of the sheet. Without a `SafeAreaProvider`, the initial window metrics are used.
- `Select` now covers the whole screen like the other two sheets, and `Combobox` drops the inset while the keyboard is open.
- **[`Grid`](./grid.html) (React Native) did not share leftover space between columns.** With `minColumnWidth={150}` in a 372-point row, you got two 150 columns and 56 empty points. The grid now measures its width and works like the web: the minimum decides how many columns fit, the leftover is shared, and a single cell on the last row is one column wide. Children still stretch in height.

## Includes v0.12.0

### New

- **[`ThemeToggle`](./themetoggle.html)**, on the web and in React Native: a round icon-only button to switch between light and dark. In the light theme it shows a filled moon in the text colour; in the dark theme, a filled sun in the brand yellow. Its accessible name says where it goes ("Switch to dark theme"). In React Native, register `asleep--filled` (moon) and `light--filled` (sun) in your app's icon registry.
- **`render` on `Button`, `IconButton` and navigation items** (`Sidebar`, `BottomNav`, `NavList`, `Breadcrumb`): `render={<Link href="/reports" />}` renders your router's link with the component's skin and content. When the button is disabled or loading, clicks are blocked on the element too.
- **[`Text`](./text.html), [`Heading`](./heading.html), [`Paragraph`](./paragraph.html) and [`Code`](./code.html)**, on the web and in React Native: a closed list of roles instead of loose sizes (heading 1 to 6, body, small, extra small and code). Colour is normal or `color="muted"`, with four weights, alignment and `truncate`.
- `Heading level={2}` renders an `h2` styled as heading 2. `Paragraph size="sm"` is a 14-pixel `p`. `Code` is a `code` with the `Prose` code skin. `Text` is a `span` with the role you choose.
- In React Native, the existing `Text` keeps its loose options and gains `type`, the same role as on the web. `Heading`, `Paragraph` and `Code` are new there too.
- **`Stack` (React Native) gets `align`**: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`. New type: `AureaStackAlign`.

### Changed

- **One focus outline, from two new tokens**: `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` (2px and 2px). Every focus rule in the core uses them, so changing focus system-wide is a one-line change.
- **Scrollable tables (`.table-region`) and [`DataGrid`](./datagrid.html)**: focus was a faint halo; it is now the focus outline, drawn inside.
- **[`MediaPlayer`](./mediaplayer.html), light theme**: control focus was dark brown on the near-black player and disappeared. It is now yellow in both themes.
- **Menus, keyboard focus**: the focused item now gets the focus outline inside, not just the grey hover background. With the mouse it is still only the background. In `Combobox` and `CommandPalette`, where focus stays in the field, the highlight remains the background.
- Minor: the player's position control is 2px from its outline instead of 3, and the `DataGrid` column resize handle draws its line inside.

### Breaking changes

- **Icon names are type-checked**, on the web and in React Native. `IconName` is no longer `string` but the list of 2,571 icon names, generated from the same source as the sprite and the native icons. A misspelled name used to compile and draw nothing; now it does not compile, in every prop that takes an icon. In React Native, the `criarRegistroDeIcones` keys are checked too.
- If you pass an icon name in a `string` variable, type it as `IconName`. For your own sprite or a `criarGlifo` glyph, declare the names once in `interface AureaIconNames` (see each package's `README.md`).
- **The React Native `Button` follows its parent**, like the web `.btn` in a `.stack`. In a column without alignment the button now takes the full width (for example in the `Screen` footer). To size it to its text, set `align` on the parent `Stack`. `IconButton` keeps a fixed width and never stretches.
- **Icon-only buttons are round**, at every size, on the web and in React Native. They were squares with 10px corners (6px on the two smallest). This covers every [`IconButton`](./iconbutton.html), close buttons and player controls, which also lost their side padding to become square.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.12.1 @aurea-uds/core@0.12.1 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.12.1 @aurea-uds/icons@0.12.1
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.12.1
```
</page>

# v0.11.0

React Native fixes for Android (clipped button text, lists that did not scroll, sheets behind system buttons), new Badge sizes and centred Radio and Checkbox marks.

A React Native release focused on Android. Button text no longer loses its descenders, `Select` and `Combobox` lists scroll, and bottom sheets stay clear of the system buttons. It also changes some appearance: `Radio` and `Checkbox` marks are vertically centred, and `Badge` follows new sizes.

## New

- **`justify` on [`SegmentedControl`](./segmentedcontrol.html) and [`Tabs`](./tabs.html)**: `start` (default), `center` or `end`, to place the row when it fits on the line. Wrapping them in a centred `Cluster` had no effect. New type: `AureaFilaJustify`.
- **`align` on [`Radio`](./radio.html) and [`Checkbox`](./checkbox.html)**: `center` (default) or `start`. With `start`, a multi-line label keeps the mark centred on its first line.
- **`searchKeyboardType` on [`Combobox`](./combobox.html)**: the keyboard for the sheet's search field, for example `"number-pad"` to search for a year. Without it, the regular text keyboard.

## Changed

- **`Radio` and `Checkbox` marks are centred on the text height.** They used to sit at the top of the label with a fixed 1-point offset.
- **[`Badge`](./badge.html) sizes**: `sm` 8 by 2 padding, 12-point text, 16 line; `md` 12 by 4, 14-point text, 20 line; `lg` 16 by 6, 16-point text, 24 line; 4-point gap. Heights grow from 20 to 22, 24 to 30 and 28 to 38. The `xs` counter stays 16 tall, now with 12-point text. The capsule radius is unchanged.
- **Inside `Card variant="brand"`**, a solid button with a tone (success, danger, warning, info) keeps its colour and gets an outline in the card's ink colour, so it stands out from the yellow. Outline and ghost buttons stay in the ink colour.
- **Bottom sheets** (`Select`, `Combobox`, `BottomSheet`) inset their bottom edge with `SafeAreaView`, like `Screen`: only as much as the sheet actually sits behind the Android button bar, and zero otherwise.

## Fixed

- **[`Button`](./button.html) clipped descenders** (g, p, ç) on Android. The label used a line height of 1.0; it now uses the normal 1.5, which fits at every size and density. `Badge` had the same problem and is fixed by its new sizes.
- **`Select` and `Combobox` lists did not scroll on Android.** A wrapper claimed the touch and kept it from the inner scroll view. That redundant handler is removed from `Select`, `Combobox`, `Dialog` and `Drawer`.
- **`Combobox` with a selected value**: the clear button and the arrow sat at different heights on Android. The arrow now has the same touch box as the clear button (44-point minimum height, centred), so both line up with the field, and its touch target grows from 16 to 44.

## Breaking changes

- **Appearance**: `Radio` and `Checkbox` marks move to the middle of the text, and `Badge` heights grow. Check screens that depend on these sizes.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.11.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.11.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.11.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.11.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.11.0
```

# v0.10.1

criarGlifo can now draw stroked shapes, so line-drawn logos work in React Native without importing an SVG library.

A small, additive React Native release: `criarGlifo` now draws with strokes as well as fills.

## New

- **Stroked shapes in `criarGlifo`**: each shape accepts `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeLinecap` and `strokeLinejoin`, with their SVG names.
- **`"currentColor"`** in `stroke` or `fill` uses the `Icon` colour, so the stroke follows the theme.
- **Paint on the whole drawing**: set the paint once for the glyph, like attributes on a root `<svg>`; a value on a single shape wins.
- Without `stroke`, nothing changes. Stroke width is in `viewBox` units, so it scales with the glyph.

```tsx
const Logo = criarGlifo({fill: "none", stroke: "currentColor", strokeWidth: 2,
                         strokeLinecap: "round", paths: ["M…"]});
```

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.10.1 @aurea-uds/core@0.10.1 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.10.1 @aurea-uds/icons@0.10.1
```

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.10.1
```

# v0.10.0

Web layout additions for Topbar, AppShell, Field and Card, a clearer current item in the Sidebar, and a fix for a stretched top bar.

A web release. `Topbar`, `AppShell`, `Field` and `Card` get new layout options, and the current item in the side navigation is easier to spot. The current-item change is visual, so check your navigation after upgrading.

## New

- **[`Topbar`](./topbar.html) `divider`**: a thin line under the flush bar (`variant="flush"`). Ignored on the other variants, which already float with their own border.
- **[`AppShell`](./appshell.html) `topbarDivider` and `contentVariant="plain"`**: `plain` removes the box (background, border, radius and padding) around the content, for screens that bring their own cards.
- **[`Field`](./field.html) `description`**: supporting text below the control, linked through `aria-describedby` in the order hint, description, error. `hint` stays next to the label.
- **[`Card`](./card.html) `orientation="horizontal"` and `Card.Media`**: a list layout with a 96-pixel cover on the left (`--space-24`) and text on the right. In vertical cards, `Card.Media` as the first child sits flush with the top edge, clipped to the 22 radius.

## Changed

- **The current item in [`Sidebar`](./sidebar.html) and `AppShell`** now uses the sidebar's accent colour for text and glyph, with a 2-pixel underline. It used to be only a grey background. Contrast passes AA in both themes. In the collapsed sidebar the underline fits the narrow rail.

## Fixed

- **`AppShell` stretched the top bar on short pages.** With no explicit rows, the grid shared the leftover height between the bar and the content; on narrow screens the bar grew from 134 to 414 pixels at 375 wide. The leftover now goes to the content row.

## Update

# v0.9.0

Layout props for the web primitives, Button, Card, Separator and Dialog. The default Dialog width changes from 560 to 448.

A web release with layout props across the primitives and several components. One change is not additive: a `Dialog` without a `size` is now narrower.

## New

- **[`Stack`](./stack.html), [`Cluster`](./cluster.html) and [`Grid`](./grid.html)**: `gap` with three steps (`tight` 8, `normal`, `loose` 24); `align` and `justify` with the same names as the React Native `Cluster`; `wrap` on `Cluster`; `min` and `columns` on `Grid`. Without these props, no class changes.
- **`width` on [`SearchField`](./searchfield.html) and [`InputGroup`](./inputgroup.html)**, so a search field no longer takes the full width of a toolbar.
- **`aria-label` on [`Combobox`](./combobox.html) and [`MultiCombobox`](./multicombobox.html)**, for filters without a visible label.
- **[`Button`](./button.html) `grow`**, plus `target`, `rel` and `download` on a `Button` with `href`.
- **[`Separator`](./separator.html) `spacing`**, with the same three steps as `gap`.
- **[`Card`](./card.html) `padding="none"`**: the cover sits flush with the edge, clipped to the 22 radius.
- **[`Dialog`](./dialog.html) `size`**: `xs` 320, `sm` 384, `md` 448, `lg` 512, plus `xl` 1024 and `full`.
- **`Dialog` `dismissible={false}`**: neither Escape nor an outside click closes it, and the close button is disabled.

## Breaking changes

- **A `Dialog` without `size` is now 448 wide instead of 560**, 112 pixels narrower. For something close to the old width, pass `size="lg"` (512). [`ConfirmDialog`](./confirmdialog.html) stays at 420.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.9.0 @aurea-uds/core@0.9.0 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.9.0 @aurea-uds/icons@0.9.0
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.9.0
```
</page>

# v0.8.14

Additive props for Badge, Cluster, Topbar and Screen, a shared disabled-opacity token, and criarGlifo for custom glyphs in React Native.

An additive release, mostly for React Native. It adds layout props, a footer for `Screen`, an opacity token, and `criarGlifo` to draw custom glyphs such as logos.

## New

- **[`Badge`](./badge.html) `fit="content"`**, on the web and in React Native: the badge sizes to its text inside a column. The default is unchanged. On the web it becomes `inline-size: fit-content`; in React Native it becomes `alignSelf: "flex-start"`, which only works in a column. Ignored when the badge is anchored.
- **[`Cluster`](./cluster.html) (React Native) with `align`, `justify` and `wrap`**. Without these props, nothing changes.
- **[`Topbar`](./topbar.html) `inset`** (`bar`, `page`, `none`), on the flush variant only. `page` uses the same 16 inset as `Screen`, so the title lines up with the content; the default is still 20.
- **`opacity-disabled` token (0.5)**: fields, menus and `Combobox` now read it, on the web and in React Native. No value changes; the disabled button keeps its 0.45. `comOpacidade` is now exported from `@aurea-uds/native`.
- **`Screen` `footer` (React Native)**: stays outside the scroll area, above the system area, and above the tab bar inside a `BottomNavProvider`. It does not require a `SafeAreaProvider`.
- **`criarGlifo` (React Native)**: draws your own glyph, such as a logo, from rectangles, circles and paths, without your app importing an SVG library. It adds no new weight.

## Changed

- **`text-md` is documented as a synonym of `text-sm`** (14). No value changes.

## Fixed

- The `Card` `onPress` example in the React Native type definitions now uses neutral sample text.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.14 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.14 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.14 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.14
```

# v0.8.13

The React Native Card responds to taps with onPress, and the BottomNav can size itself to its tabs with width="content".

Two additions: a tappable [`Card`](./card.html) in React Native, and a compact [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html) on the web and in React Native. Without the new props, nothing changes.

## New

- **`Card` with `onPress` (React Native)**: `<Card onPress={open} accessibilityLabel="…">`. You no longer need to wrap the card in a `Pressable`.
- With `onPress`, the type requires `accessibilityLabel`, and screen readers treat the card as a button.
- With `onPress`, the type does not accept `variant="brand"`, because that variant requires an `action` button, and a button inside a button disappears for VoiceOver on iPhone.
- A tappable card without `variant` uses the `interactive` skin. Its press feedback matches `Button` (scale 0.97, opacity 0.9).
- A card with `onPress` must not contain other tappable elements; the type cannot check your content.
- **`BottomNav` `width="content"`**, on the web and in React Native: the bar sizes to its tabs and centres itself instead of spanning edge to edge. Only on `floating`; ignored on `edge`. With four tabs the gain is small (about 275 instead of 328 on a 360 screen).

## Fixed

- The `BottomNav` documentation still described the iPhone safe area as padding inside the bar. Since v0.8.8 it is an outer margin.
- If your floating bar still sits in a box or behind the Android buttons, update and remove any painted `View` wrapped around `BottomNav`: that wrapper draws the box. The underlying fixes shipped in v0.8.8.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.13 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.13 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.13 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.13
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.8.13
```
</page>

# v0.8.12

A new type scale (12 to 48). Web components return to 14 pixels, while React Native components use 16.

The type scale changes to **12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48**. On the web, component text becomes smaller than in v0.8.8 to v0.8.11; in React Native it stays one step larger.

## Changed

- **Web**: components return to 14 (button, field, `Select`, tabs, sidebar, label), and supporting text to 12 (badge, tag, field error). Small buttons and fields stay at 14. Card titles are 14 with medium weight.
- **Web, on phones**: text typed into fields grows to 16, which keeps Safari from zooming the page.
- **React Native**: components stay at 16 and supporting text at 14, one step above the web. Component `size` values are unchanged; the mapping is done in one place.
- **Headings** barely change: `lg` 20 to 18, `2xl` 25 to 24, `3xl` 31 to 30.

## Breaking changes

- **Smaller web text**: component text goes from 16 to 14 compared with v0.8.8 to v0.8.11, and `md`, the `body` size, also becomes 14.

## Update

On the web:


# v0.8.11

Adds MediaEmbed, which shows a video from another site (YouTube, Vimeo) in Aurea's frame, with an optional poster that loads nothing until clicked.

A new web component, `MediaEmbed`, to show videos from other sites inside the same frame as [`MediaPlayer`](./mediaplayer.html): card radius, border and dark background.

## New

- **`MediaEmbed`**: a video from another site (YouTube, Vimeo) in Aurea's frame.
- **`title` is required by the type**: it is the video's accessible name.
- **`ratio`** (`16/9` by default) is reserved before loading, so the page does not jump.
- **Privacy defaults**: `referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"` and `loading="lazy"`.
- **With `poster`, nothing from the other site loads until the click.** Until then you see the image and a play button. On click the video loads and starts playing (`autoplay={false}` turns that off), and focus moves to it.
- **`href`** shows a link to the video on its original site, a way out when the owner blocks embedding. The page cannot detect that block, so the link is always visible.
- Enter and Space open the video.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.11 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.11 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.11 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.11
```

On React Native:

```bash

```

# v0.8.10

Select gets Aurea's own skin and floating list instead of the browser's native control. Also ships v0.8.9, with navItems on AppShell and labelWidth on Field.

The web [`Select`](./select.html) no longer opens the operating system's list: it is now built on Base UI with Aurea's skin. The way you write it stays the same, but the element on the page changes. This release also publishes v0.8.9, which fixes a double sidebar box in `AppShell` and squeezed horizontal fields.

## New

- **`Select` props**: `items`, `onValueChange`, `placeholder` and `required`.

## Changed

- **`Select` has Aurea's skin**: a capsule trigger and a floating list like [`Combobox`](./combobox.html), without a search field. It is still the same `Select` component.
- **Usage is unchanged**: `<option>` and `<optgroup>` as children, `value` and `defaultValue`, `onChange` with `e.target.value`, `name` (submitted through a hidden field), `disabled` and `size`.
- Keyboard: arrows, Home, End, Enter and Space.

## Fixed

- **Documentation site**: nine samples scrolled inside their box and two pages overflowed sideways at 320 pixels. The samples were rearranged to fit.

## Breaking changes

- **`Select` renders a `<button>` with the `combobox` role**, not a `<select>`, and `ref` points to that button. If you read `ref.current.value` or styled `select` by tag name, update that code.

## Includes v0.8.9

### New

- **[`AppShell`](./appshell.html) `navItems`, `currentNavId` and `navLabel`**: the list goes into the `Sidebar` that the shell already creates. Passing another `Sidebar` as `navigation` produced two nested boxes that cut text; with `navItems` there is one box and long names end in "…". `navigation` still works and is now optional; when both are set, the list comes first.
- **[`Field`](./field.html) `labelWidth`**: in `orientation="horizontal"` the label column was a fixed 192 pixels (`--field-label-width`). On a 375-pixel phone the selected value could disappear. `labelWidth="auto"` sizes the column to the label; a CSS length (`"8rem"`) sets another width. Without the prop, 192 as before.
- To use the fixes, replace `navigation={<Sidebar items current />}` with `navItems` and `currentNavId`, and add `labelWidth="auto"` to narrow fields.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.10 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.10 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.10 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.10
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.8.10
```

<page url="https://aureauds.dev/release-v0-8-8.html">
# v0.8.8

Web fixes for Combobox, the mobile drawer, DependencyGraph and DataGrid, React Native fixes found on Android, BottomNavProvider, and a new type scale.

A large fix release. On the web it corrects item layout in `Combobox`, the mobile drawer, graph edges and table search. In React Native it fixes `NumberField`, controls without labels, `Grid` cells and the floating `BottomNav`. It also introduces a new type scale with clearly distinct steps.

## New

- **`BottomNavProvider` and `useBottomNavSpace()` (React Native)**: the floating bar measures its own height and reports it to the provider, and `Screen` with `scroll` reserves that space so the end of the content is not hidden. For screens without `Screen`, the number is available from the hook. Outside a provider both are zero.

## Changed

- **New type scale with five visible steps.** The small end had four steps four points apart (12, 13, 14, 16), which read as mistakes rather than hierarchy. Caption and supporting text become 13, body and control text 16, card titles 20, screen titles 25, and highlighted numbers 31. Nothing gets smaller.
- The ten size names stay, and some now point to the same value, so no component had to change `size`. The web tokens change too, since the scale lives in `aurea.tokens.json`.
- **Menu item radius goes from 8 to 18**, and the `.menu` panel gets the card radius and `--space-1` padding. This applies to every list using `.menu`: [`Combobox`](./combobox.html), [`MultiCombobox`](./multicombobox.html), [`DropdownMenu`](./dropdownmenu.html), [`ContextMenu`](./contextmenu.html), [`Menubar`](./menubar.html) and the [`CommandPalette`](./commandpalette.html) list.

## Fixed

### Web

- **`Combobox` and `MultiCombobox`**: item text fell into the check column when the item was not selected, so long labels wrapped onto four lines. The column now always exists, and each item is 36 tall. The core also places the last child in the second column for hand-written HTML.
- **The mobile drawer did not close when an item was picked.** It now closes, both with the declarative list and with navigation passed as `children`, in `@aurea-uds/react` and in `aurea.js`.
- **Widening the window left the drawer stuck over the page**, without its overlay or close button. Crossing `lg` (1024 pixels) now closes it.
- **[`DependencyGraph`](./dependencygraph.html)**: edge labels were black on black. Labels now read the colour variables directly, and the gap between columns grows with the longest label so labels do not slide under nodes. Graphs without labels are unchanged.
- **`DependencyGraph`**: two edges between the same pair of nodes became one. `GraphEdgeItem` gets `id?: string`, and parallel edges leave the node at different heights. Without `id`, the first edge of each pair keeps its usual id.
- **[`DataGrid`](./datagrid.html)**: global search ignored a column that was empty in the first row. It now uses the first present value. `enableGlobalFilter: false` on a column still wins.
- **Floating `BottomNav`**: the iPhone safe area was added as `padding-bottom` inside the pill. It is now `margin-bottom`, and `.bottom-nav-edge` keeps its padding.

### React Native

- **[`NumberField`](./numberfield.html) only reported the number on blur.** Tapping "Save" with the keyboard open could save the previous value without any error. It now reports on every keystroke, following the `locale` rules: in pt-BR `"12,"` is `12`, `"1.234,5"` is `1234.5`, clearing the field is `null`, and `","` or `"-"` alone report nothing.
- `min` and `max` are not applied while typing, so the field never overwrites what you are typing. They are applied on blur, and if that changes the number it is reported again. Formatting still happens only on blur.
- **[`Switch`](./switch.html) without a label stretched and hid the row name in [`NavList`](./navlist.html).** Without label and description, the root is now just the track. `Checkbox` and `Radio` had the same issue and are fixed too.
- **[`Grid`](./grid.html) children did not fill their cell**, so two `KPI` side by side had different heights when one wrapped its text. Children now fill the cell height.
- **The floating [`BottomNav`](./bottomnav.html) slid behind the Android buttons and did not float.** `floating` is now `position: absolute`: the screen uses the full height and scrolls under the pill, and the system inset becomes `marginBottom`. Do not wrap the bar in a painted `View`. The `edge` variant is unchanged.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.8 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.8 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.8 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.8
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.8.8
```
</page>

# v0.8.7

In React Native, the brand Card now keeps its fields, buttons and focus readable on the yellow, and menus or sheets opened from inside it no longer inherit its colors.

A patch for React Native that completes the yellow brand card introduced in v0.8.6. In v0.8.6 only the text inside the card got a readable color; borders, icons, fields and buttons still used colors that do not show on the yellow. They now use the same dark ink as the text.

## Fixed

- **[`Card`](./card.html) `variant="brand"`: the ink now reaches borders and icons, not only text.** Field outlines, the invalid border, the focus ring and icon-only buttons were below 3:1 against the yellow in at least one theme. They now use `primary-foreground`, the only system color that reads on the yellow in both themes.
- **Fields inside the brand card**: they drop their background and are drawn as an outline in the ink color, since no background color separates from the yellow.
- **Invalid fields inside the brand card**: the red border would read worse than the normal one on the yellow, so the field keeps the ink outline. The error is shown by the `Field` message and announced to screen readers.
- **Focus inside the brand card**: it is shown by a thicker outline, not by color, because in the dark theme the focus color is the same yellow.
- **Buttons inside the brand card**: the filled [`Button`](./button.html) inverts (ink background, yellow label); outline and ghost buttons use the ink.
- **Overlays opened from inside the brand card no longer inherit its ink.** A `Select` sheet opened from inside the card would have painted dark brown text on a normal background. The six overlay components of the package now reset the brand ink.
- **Known limit**: the components that read the brand ink are `Text`, the field family, `Button` and `IconButton`. Other components, and content your app places inside the card, may still be hard to read on the yellow.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.7 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.7 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.7 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.7
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.8.7
```
</page>

# v0.8.6

React Native gets a yellow brand Card that requires an action, and SegmentedControl and Tabs now scroll sideways with a visible hint when the options do not fit.

Two additions for React Native. `SegmentedControl` and `Tabs` scroll sideways when their options do not fit the screen, and show a scroll bar only when there is more to see. `Card` gains a `brand` variant, the first large surface filled with the brand yellow.

## New

### React Native

- **[`SegmentedControl`](./segmentedcontrol.html) and [`Tabs`](./tabs.html) scroll sideways when they do not fit**, as the web already did on small screens. The cut-off option at the edge plus a scroll bar tell you there is more; the scroll bar appears only when the content actually overflows.
- **[`Card`](./card.html) `variant="brand"`**: a card filled with the brand yellow. The text color inside is forced to `primary-foreground`, because normal and muted text do not read on the yellow in the dark theme. Inside it there is a single text color; hierarchy comes from weight and size.
- **`variant="brand"` requires `action`**: the brand card is meant for asking the user to do something, so it does not compile without an action.

## Fixed

### React Native

- **`Tabs`: the tab row scrolled without showing that more tabs existed.** The scroll indicator was turned off in v0.8.5, so anyone who did not think to swipe never found the hidden tabs. `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` now share the same scrolling piece.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.6 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.6 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.6 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.6
```

# v0.8.5

React Native gets Tabs, new props on Badge, Switch and NavList, and fixes for controls that VoiceOver on iPhone could not reach.

This release adds `Tabs` to React Native and fills several gaps in existing components. It also fixes a family of iPhone accessibility bugs: when an accessible container holds something tappable, VoiceOver hides what is inside, so close buttons, chart data and switches could not be reached.

## New

### React Native

- **[`Tabs`](./tabs.html)**: tabs inside a screen that switch a panel instead of changing page, with the `tablist` and `tab` roles. No new dependency.
- **`Tabs` scrolls sideways**, unlike the web version: on a narrow phone four labels do not fit, and squeezing them would hide the text.
- **`Tabs` unmounts the inactive panel**, unlike the web. Its internal state (scroll position, typed text) is lost when you switch tabs.
- **`Tabs` does not use the brand color for the selected tab**, matching the web, where the selected tab uses the text color.
- **[`Badge`](./badge.html)**: `leading` and `trailing`. They take a node, not an icon name, and do not tint what they receive.
- **[`Switch`](./switch.html)**: `description`. The web `Switch` does not have it yet.
- **[`NavList`](./navlist.html)**: a row with no action no longer announces itself as a link, and the chevron only appears when the row does something.

## Fixed

### React Native

- **[`Alert`](./alert.html): the close button was unreachable for VoiceOver on iPhone.** It sat inside the alert's reading group. It is now outside it.
- **[`Chart`](./chart.html): on iPhone, screen reader users heard the chart name and no data.** The accessible name moved from the frame to the drawing, so the tappable bands with their labels and values are reachable again.
- **[`NavList`](./navlist.html): a tappable `value` (for example a `Switch`) became a button inside a button.** The value now sits outside the row's pressable area. Text values stay inside, as part of the row's sentence.
- **[`SegmentedControl`](./segmentedcontrol.html): the selected option now uses the same selected style as the web and `BottomNav`**: the brand emphasis color and the yellow underline. It uses `primaryEmphasis`, because plain yellow text does not read on the light theme.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.5 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.5 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.5 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.5
```

On React Native:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/native@0.8.5
```
</page>

# v0.8.4

In React Native, the Combobox clear button is reachable by VoiceOver on iPhone, and the arrow now opens the list.

A single fix for the React Native `Combobox`. Its clear button was a button inside another button, which VoiceOver on iPhone hides.

## Fixed

- **[`Combobox`](./combobox.html): the clear button moved out of the trigger.** On iPhone it was visible but did not exist for VoiceOver. The capsule is now a frame, and the trigger, the clear button and the arrow are siblings inside it. Android was not affected.
- **The arrow now opens the list when tapped.** It stays silent for screen readers, since the trigger already announces the label, the value and whether the list is open.
- **Small behavior change**: the empty space at the right end of the capsule no longer opens the list. The text and the arrow do.

# v0.8.3

React Native fixes for brand and destructive text contrast and for Input dropping props, plus Separator, a link tone on Text and new PasswordField props.

A React Native release focused on sign-in screens. `Input` now forwards every `TextInput` prop, so password managers, autocorrect and the keyboard's next key work again. Brand and destructive text reach readable contrast in the light theme, and `Separator` arrives.

## New

### React Native

- **[`Text`](./text.html)**: a `link` tone, so you no longer need to set the link color by hand.
- **[`PasswordField`](./passwordfield.html)**: `leading`, a slot in front of the field (for a padlock, for example).
- **[`PasswordField`](./passwordfield.html)**: `icons`. The show/hide eye needs the `view` and `view--off` icons in the registry; without them the button is invisible and the warning only appears in development.
- **[`Separator`](./separator.html)**: same color and thickness as the web one, horizontal or vertical, plus a `label` for a line with text in the middle ("or continue with"). `label` does not exist on the web. It has no accessibility role, because React Native has no `separator` role.

## Fixed

### React Native

- **Brand text was written in the fill yellow.** [`Button`](./button.html) and [`IconButton`](./iconbutton.html) with `appearance="ghost"` or `"outline"` and `tone="brand"` measured 1.73:1 on the light theme. The label now uses `link`: the same hue, darker, 5.02:1 on light, and unchanged on dark.
- **Destructive text was also below contrast on light** (4.30:1). Ghost and outline buttons with `tone="destructive"` now use `danger400` (6.86:1 light, 7.47:1 dark), matching the web.
- **[`Input`](./input.html) silently dropped props.** `autoComplete`, `textContentType`, `autoCorrect`, `returnKeyType`, `onSubmitEditing`, `maxLength` and any other `TextInput` prop were discarded, and so were the ones `PasswordField` forwarded. `InputProps` now extends `TextInputProps` (minus what Aurea controls), and `ref` is accepted as a prop.

## Update

On the web:

```bash
pnpm add @aurea-uds/react@0.8.3 @aurea-uds/core@0.8.3 @aurea-uds/fonts@0.8.3 @aurea-uds/icons@0.8.3
```
